en.name: Ponte Sant’Angelo
description: At the time of Bernini's interventions, the statue of St. Peter (by Lorenzo Lotti, called Lorenzetto) and that of St. Paul (by Paolo Romano) were already there, guarding the bridge towards the southern side. Coming from Campo Marzio, the beholder first encounters the *Angel with the Column,* by Antonio Raggi, to symbolize the Flagellation as the beginning of the Passion of Christ, while at the end of the path the *Angel with the Lance of Longinus* appears, sculpted by Domenico Guidi, the final event of the Crucifixion, when Longinus pierced the side of Christ. Between these two extremities there are, in order, the *Angel with the Scourges* by Lazzaro Morelli, the *Angel with the Crown of Thorns* by Paolo Naldini (copy of the Bernian original in Sant'Andrea delle Fratte), the *Angel with the Holy Face* by Cosimo Fancelli, the *Angel with the Robe and the Dices* by Paolo Naldini, the *Angel with the Nails* by Gerolamo Lucenti, the *Angel with the Cross* by Ercole Ferrata, the *Angel with the Subscription* by Giulio Cartari (or by Bernini himself) and the *Angel with the Sponge* by Antonio Giorgetti. The angels, located in accordance with the chronological sequence of the events of the Passion as indicated by the objects they carry, underline with great dramatic force the processional role the bridge had. The bridge in fact played as an obligatory point of passage between the secular city and the holy city of the Vatican, in line with contemporary Counter-Reformation dictates on devotional practices connected to meditation on the Passion of Christ. Such practices were strongly encouraged and supported by the Catholic Church in the 17th century. Bernini replaced the previous travertine parapets with elegant, grated balustrades so as to allow the view of the river. Placed between the transient elements of the water and the sky, the angels are also characterized by an accentuated dynamism. The frescoes by Anastasio Fontebuoni in the church of Santa Prisca (early 17th century) and those in the church of Santa Prassede (1594–96) have been identified as possible referents for Bernini's iconography: the church of Santa Prassede, moreover, supposedly hosted a relic of the column of the Flagellation, which Antonio Raggi faithfully reproduced for his *Angel with the Column*.
The statues of the Angels on the bridge commissioned by pope Clement IX were designed by Bernini in 1669. A scenografical fix route created for pilgrims and travellers heading for Saint Peter’s.
artist: Gian Lorenzo Bernini; Lazzaro Morelli; Antonio Raggi; Cosimo Fancelli; Girolamo Lucenti; Giulio Cartari; Ercole Ferrata; Antonio Giorgetti; Domenico Guidi; Paolo Naldini
history:
The ancient Aelian Bridge was built by Hadrian in the 2nd century AD to connect the ancient *Campus Martius* with his mausoleum. It underwent structural changes under Alexander VI (late 15th century) and was decorated to celebrate the triumphal procession of Charles V (1536). On that occasion Lorenzetto and Raffaello da Montelupo had created stucco statues of patriarchs and evangelists. It is very likely that, for the realization of his own project for the bridge, Bernini had gathered information, through prints, about the older decorative apparatus.  
The project to redecorate the bridge was resumed in 1669 by Pope Clement IX Rospigliosi, who commissioned Bernini to repair the structure, to enlarge it with an arch and to decorate it with a double row of angels bearing the symbols of the Passion of Christ, to be placed on the parapets. To ensure a degree of uniformity, Bernini provided a series of terracotta drawings and models to his collaborators, reserving for himself the execution of the *Angel with the Crown of Thorns* and the *Angel with the Subscription.* Clement IX, who saw the two sculptures in the artist’s studio, was deeply impressed and had copies made for the bridge, while donating the originals to Cardinal Rospigliosi for his palace. They remained there until 1729, when they were transferred to S. Andrea delle Fratte, Bernini’s parish church. Paolo Naldini made the copy of the *Angel with the Crown of Thorns* while Giulio Cartari (but according to other sources it was actually Bernini himself) that of the *Angel with the Subscription*.
keywords: Saint Peter’s

it.name: Ponte Sant’Angelo
description:
All'epoca degli interventi berniniani, la statua di San Pietro (di Lorenzo Lotti, detto Lorenzetto) e quella di San Paolo (di Paolo Romano) si trovavano già a guardia del ponte, verso il lato meridionale. Provenendo da Campo Marzio, si incontra per primo l'*Angelo con la Colonna*, di Antonio Raggi, a simboleggiare l'inizio della Passione di Cristo, ossia la Flagellazione, mentre a conclusione del percorso compare l'*Angelo che reca la lancia di Longino*, di Domenico Guidi, l'evento finale della crocifissione, quando Longino trafisse il costato di Cristo.  
Tra questi due estremi si presentano, nell'ordine, l'*Angelo con i flagelli* di Lazzaro Morelli, l'*Angelo con la corona di spine* di Paolo Naldini (copia di quello di Sant'Andrea delle Fratte), l'*Angelo con il Volto Santo* di Cosimo Fancelli, l'*Angelo con la Veste e i dadi* di Paolo Naldini, l'*Angelo con i chiodi* di Gerolamo Lucenti, l'*Angelo con la croce* di Ercole Ferrata, l'*Angelo con Titolo della croce* di Giulio Cartari (o di Bernini stesso) e l'*Angelo con la spugna* di Antonio Giorgetti.  
Questa schiera angelica, nella sequenza cronologica degli eventi della Passione illustrati dagli attributi retti dagli angeli, sottolinea con grande forza drammatica il ruolo processionale assunto dal ponte, punto di passaggio obbligato tra la città laica a quella sacra del Vaticano. Si viene pertanto a creare una sorta di Via Crucis all'aperto, e al contempo una simbolica ostensione delle reliquie della Passione che il credente, dopo un breve percorso a piedi, avrebbe di lì a poco potuto venerare in San Pietro, ossia i frammenti della croce, quelli della lancia di Longino e il velo della Veronica. Si tratta di un intervento in linea con i contemporanei dettami controriformistici relativi alle pratiche devozionali connesse alla meditazione sulla Passione di Cristo cui la Chiesa diede nel XVII secolo un impulso decisivo.   
Bernini sostituì i precedenti parapetti in travertino con eleganti balaustre a grate in modo da permettere la vista del fiume: posti tra gli elementi transeunti dell'acqua e del cielo, gli angeli sono connotati anch'essi da un accentuato dinamismo.  
Sono stati individuati, come possibili referenti per l'iconografia berniniana, gli affreschi di Anastasio Fontebuoni in Santa Prisca (inizi XVII secolo) e quelli in Santa Prassede (1594-1596): quest'ultima era, peraltro, una chiesa dove si venerava la supposta reliquia della colonna della Flagellazione, non a caso riprodotta fedelmente da Antonio Raggi nel suo *Angelo con la Colonna*.

Le statue degli angeli recanti i simboli della Passione furono concepiti in modo unitario da Bernini ed eseguiti dai suoi collaboratori. Punto di passaggio obbligato per la basilica di San Pietro, il ponte diviene una solenne Via Crucis in cui gli angeli sottolineano con grande forza drammatica il ruolo salvifico assunto dalle reliquie che il pellegrino avrebbe di lì a poco potuto venerare in San Pietro.
artist: Gianlorenzo Bernini (ideazione); Lazzaro Morelli; Antonio Raggi; Cosimo Fancelli; Girolamo Lucenti; Giulio Cartari; Ercole Ferrata; Antonio Giorgetti; Domenico Guidi; Paolo Naldini
history:
L'antico ponte Elio era stato costruito da Adriano nel II secolo d.C.  per collegare l'area del Campo Marzio con il suo mausoleo. Subì modifiche strutturali sotto Alessandro VI (fine XV secolo) e venne decorato in occasione del corteo trionfale di Carlo V (1536), quando Lorenzetto e Raffaello da Montelupo realizzarono statue di patriarchi ed  evangelisti in stucco. È molto probabile che, per il suo progetto per il ponte, Bernini fosse venuto a conoscenza di questo apparato decorativo attraverso delle stampe.  
Il progetto di ridecorare il ponte venne ripreso nel 1669 da Clemente IX Rospigliosi. Bernini ricevette dal papa l'ordine di riparare la struttura, di ingrandirla di un'arcata e di decorarla con una doppia schiera di angeli recanti i simboli della Passione di Cristo, da collocarsi sui parapetti. Per garantire un grado di uniformità, Bernini fornì una serie di disegni e di modelli in terracotta ai suoi collaboratori, riservando per sé l'esecuzione dell'*Angelo con la corona di spine* e dell'*Angelo con il Titolo della croce*. Clemente IX, che vide le due sculture nello studio dell'artista, rimanendone vivamente impressionato fece eseguire delle copie per il ponte donando gli originali al cardinale Rospigliosi per il suo palazzo. Lì rimasero fino al 1729 quando vennero trasferiti a S. Andrea delle Fratte, chiesa parrocchiale di Bernini. Paolo Naldini eseguì la copia dell'*Angelo con la corona di spine* mentre Giulio Cartari (ma secondo altre testimonianze lo stesso Bernini) quella dell'*Angelo con il Titolo della croce.*
keywords: Scultura; Controriforma; Pellegrinaggio

en.name: Bridal apron jewellery (*Mangura*)
short_description: The influences of Eastern art in Macedonia were largely expressed in the jewellery of the 19th century through the so-called Levantine Baroque style. This piece preserves evidence of the exceptional diversity of the jewellery. Worn on the apron, it also shows that articles of adornment used to be applied on many different items of clothing. A *mangura* consists of a string of tiny beads adorned with ornaments. The larger central pendant has been made in the filigree technique and embellished with decorative stones. It is flanked by minor ornaments decorated by perforation.
keywords: Mangura; filigree; perforation; silver; costume; accessories; wedding; marriage
materials: Silver, silver alloy, tiny beads, hammering, casting, filigree, perforation

ar.name: ساكف باب.
description:
وُجِد في بادية الشام مجموعة من القصور الأموية، لعل من أهمها قصر الحير الغربي الذي يقع على بعد 80كم إلى الجنوب الغربي من مدينة تدمر. وهو عبارة عن مجموعة معمارية متكاملة تشتمل على مبنى القصر بالإضافة إلى خان وحمام وبستان وسد ومستودعات مياه.  
  
وُجِد هذا الساكف عند مدخل الخان، وهو خالٍ من الزخارف باستثناء نقوش تشكّل نصاً توثيقياً يمكن من خلاله تحديد اسم الخليفة الذي أمر بإقامة مباني قصر الحير، وهو هشام بن عبد الملك، واسم المتعهد الذي أشرف على أعمال البناء، وهو ثابت بن أبي ثابت، وتاريخ إقامة هذه المباني، وهو شهر رجب من عام 109 / 727. استخدم العلماء هذه المعلومات الخاصة بالخان لترجيح فترة بناء قصر الحير الغربي الذي ألحق به الخان.  
  
تعبّر هذه النقوش عن استمرارية وتحوير للعادة القديمة في المنطقة الخاصة بنقش الكتابات المفخمّة. كتب النص بالعربية بالخط الكوفي، وهو خط مبكر كثر استعماله في بداية العصر الإسلامي. أما أسلوب الكتابة على هذا الساكف فهو غريب وفريد، حيث نُقش النص على الرخام بأسلوب التثقيب.  
  
ويمكن قراءة النص على النحو التالي: "بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم، لا إله إلا الله وحده لاشريك له أمر بصنعة هذا العمل عبد الله هشام أمير المؤمنين أوجب الله أجره عمل على يد ثابت بن أبي ثابت في رجب سنة تسع ومايه."
عتبة باب، اكتسبت أهميتها من النقوش والكتابات الموجودة عليها، والتي تحتوي على تاريخ يدل على فترة انتهاء أعمال البناء، بأمر الخليفة الأموي هشام بن عبد الملك، في سنة 109 هـ/ 727 م.
keywords: خان؛ رخام؛ ساكف؛ قصر الحير الغربي؛ القصور الصحراوية؛ نقش.

en.name: Door Lintel.
description:
A lintel that belonged to the entrance of the *khan* found in the region of the Qasr al-Hayr al-Gharbi complex, which included a market (*suq*), a bathhouse (*hammam*), a garden, a dam, a storage area and, most importantly a palace (*qasr*). The lintel is not extensively ornamented, but it is important inasmuch as scholars have used it to approximate the date the palace was constructed. The inscriptions specify that Caliph Hisham bin Abd al-Malik was patron of the *khan*; Thabit bin Abi Thabit was supervisor during its construction; and the month of Rajab in the year AH 109 / AD 727 was when the *khan* was completed.  
This inscription represents a continuation and adaptation of a long-used tradition in the region – that of monumental inscriptions – into an Arabic-language context. The text is written in *kufic* script, an early calligraphic style often used in inscriptions from this period. The technique used to inscribe the marble lintel is, however, unusual as it is done by piercing and drilling holes.  
The Arabic text may be translated as follows: “In the name of God, the Merciful the Compassionate. There is no God except the One and Only God he by himself who has no partner. The making of this work was ordered by the servant of Allah Hisham, Commander of the Faithful, may God ensure his reward. \[This work was\] carried out by the hand of Thabit bin Abi Thabit in Rajab of the year 109 \[21st October 727\].

This door lintel displays important inscriptions that helped to establish the dating of the completion of the urban architectural structure constructed by the Umayyad Caliph Hisham bin 'Abd al-Malik in the year AH 109 / AD 727.
place: Syrian Desert; 80 km southwest of Palmyra.
keywords: Umayyad; qasr; desert palace; lintel; khan; Daniel Schlumberger; marble; inscription

es.name: Dintel de puerta.
description:
Este dintel perteneció a la entrada del *jan* del complejo de Qasr al-Hayr al-Garbi, que consta de un zoco *(suq)*, unos baños *(hammam)*, un jardín, una represa, una zona de almacenes y el palacio en sí *(qasr)*, que es el elemento más importante. El dintel no está excesivamente decorado, pero su importancia radica en que ha servido a los especialistas para calcular la fecha aproximada de construcción del palacio. En la inscripción se dice que el califa Hisham ibn Abd al-Malik patrocinó el *jan*, que Zabit ibn Abi Zabit supervisó la construcción y que el edificio se terminó en el mes de *rayab* del año 109 / 727.  
Esta inscripción es una demostración de que la antigua tradición local de grabar inscripciones en los monumentos continuó y se adaptó a la lengua árabe. El texto está escrito en letra cúfica, uno de los primeros estilos caligráficos, frecuente en las inscripciones de este periodo. No obstante, la técnica aplicada para tallar el mármol es inusual, ya que se hizo agujereándolo.  
El texto puede traducirse de la siguiente manera: “En el nombre de Dios, el Misericordioso, el Compasivo. No hay más Dios que el Dios único que no tiene compañero. Esta obra se llevó a cabo por orden del servidor de Allah Hisham, comandante de los fieles, que Dios le conceda su recompensa. \[Esta obra fue\] realizada por mano de Zabit ibn Abi Zabit en *rayab* del año 109 \[21 de octubre de 727\]».

En este dintel hay inscritos textos que revisten importancia documental y que ayudaron a establecer la fecha de finalización del edificio construido por orden del califa omeya Hisham ibn Abd al-Malik en 109 / 727.
place: Desierto sirio, 80 km al suroeste de Palmira.
keywords: Omeyas; qasr; palacio del desierto; dintel; jan; califa Hisham bin Abd al-Malik; Daniel Schlumberger; mármol; inscripción.

fr.name: Linteau de porte.
description:
Linteau ayant appartenu à la porte d'entrée du *khan* découvert dans les environs du complexe de Qasr al-Khayr al-Gharbi qui comprenait un marché (souk), des bains (hammam), un jardin, un barrage, des greniers et un palais (*qasr*). Ce linteau peu ornementé est important car il a servi à déterminer la date de construction du palais. Son inscription spécifie que le calife Hicham bin ‘Abd al-Malik était le commanditaire du *khan*, qu'un certain Thabit bin Abi Thabit en avait supervisé la construction et que les travaux furent achevés au cours du mois de *rajab* de l'an 109 (octobre 727 J.-C.).  
Elle illustre la continuation et l'adaptation d'une longue tradition d'inscriptions monumentales en langue arabe dans la région. Le texte est rédigé en écriture de style coufique ancien, souvent utilisé dans les inscriptions de cette période. La technique employée est en revanche inhabituelle puisqu'elle fait appel à des trous percés et forés.  
Le texte arabe peut se traduire par : “Au nom de Dieu, le Clément, le Miséricordieux. Il n'y a pas d'autre Dieu que le seul et unique Dieu qui n'a pas d’associé. La réalisation de cette œuvre a été ordonnée par le serviteur d'Allah, Hicham, Commandeur de la Foi, que Dieu lui accorde sa récompense, \[cette œuvre\] a été menée à bien par la main de Thabit bin Abi Thabit en *rajab* de l'an 109.”
Ce linteau présente d'importantes inscriptions qui ont aidé à établir la datation de l'achèvement d'un ensemble architectural urbain édifié par le calife omeyyade Hicham bin 'Abd al-Malik.
place: Qasr al-Khayr al-Gharbi, désert de Syrie, à 80 km au sud-ouest de Palmyre.
keywords: Omeyyades ; qasr ; palais du désert ; linteaux ; khan ; Daniel Schlumberger ; marbre ; inscriptions

en.name: Wine glass
description:
This lead glass wine glass is wheel-engraved with a scene showing the biblical figures David and Jonathan but also shows a coded message of love between two men. Jonathan was the son of Saul, the first king of the Israelites, and David was the handsome shepherd boy who was anointed to become the future king of the Israelites. David becomes important to Saul's court, playing music for the king and slaying the philistine giant Goliath, winning the admiration of the Israelites. He also forms a strong bond with Jonathan, which eventually drives Saul to banish David in a fit of jealous rage. The scene on this goblet shows David and Jonathan sealing their friendship through an embrace.  
  
Somewhat uncommonly, the depiction of David and Jonathan also shows that the figure on the right has his foot placed on top of the figure on the left. It has been suggested this alludes to sexual desire between men, as in the late 17th century, when homosexuality was illegal and men accused of it could face the death penalty, court records describe that treading on each others feet was one way men discreetly expressed their wish for sexual contact with each other whilst in public.

de.name: Amalienburg
description: Die Amalienburg, ein sich in die Breite erstreckender eingeschossiger Bau, ist außen schlicht in Rosa und Weiß gehalten. Sein architektonischer Mittelpunkt, der innen kreisrunde Spiegelsaal, wölbt sich aus der ansonsten gerade geführten Gartenfront hervor und wird von einer Flachkuppel überwölbt. Eine runde Plattform auf dem Dach mit kunstvoll geschmiedeter Balustrade diente der Kurfürstin als Schießstand bei der Fasanenjagd. An beiden Seiten des Spiegelsaales grenzen zwei gleichgroße Flügel an, die Jagdzimmer, Ruhezimmer, Küche und weitere Räume zur Zerstreuung der Hofgesellschaft enthalten. Die stilistisch einheitliche Innendekoration der Amalienburg ist auf ein Gesamtkonzept von Bau und Ausstattung zurückzuführen.

Das im Schlosspark Nymphenburg gelegene elegante Jagd- und Lustschlösschen Amalienburg ist im Typus einer französischen Maison de plaisance erbaut und zählt wegen seiner künstlerisch hochrangigen Innenausstattung zu den bedeutendsten Vertretern dieser Art. Der bayerische Kurfürst Karl Albrecht ließ die Amalienburg ab 1734 für seine Gemahlin Maria Amalie vom berühmten Architekten François de Cuvilliés d.Ä. planen und errichten. Als Hauptwerk des bekannten Münchner Hofstuckateurs Johann Baptist Zimmermann gilt die kapriziöse Stuckdekoration der Innenräume im späten Régence-Stil.
artist: Kurfürst Karl I. Albrecht von Bayern (reg. 1726-1745; 1742-1745 als Karl VII. Kaiser des Heiligen Römischen Reiches Deutscher Nation)
history: Schon unter Kurfürst Max Emanuel, dem Vater Karl Albrechts, war am Standort der Amalienburg ein kleiner Gartenpavillion vorhanden. 1734 erteilte Kurfürst Karl Albrecht seinem Hofkünstler François de Cuvilliés d.Ä. den Auftrag zum Bau eines Lustschlösschens für seine Gemahlin Maria Amalie, der Tochter von Kaiser Joseph I. Bereits fünf Jahre später war die Amalienburg fertiggestellt und mit Stuck von Johann Baptist Zimmermann und Ornamentschnitzereien von Johann Joachim Dietrich ausgestattet. Französischen Vorbildern entsprechend sollte die Amalienburg im Stil einer Maison de plaisance erbaut und ausgestattet werden, da in Frankreich im 18. Jahrhundert derartige kleinere Jagd- und Lustschlösschen besonders in Mode gekommen waren. In diesen konnte man, im Sinne des damaligen Wohnideals der commodité, der strengen Etikette der Hofgesellschaft und dem Zeremoniell entfliehen und in intimer Atmosphäre jagen, Feste feiern und sich andersweitiger Zerstreuung hingeben.
keywords: Ornamentschnitzerei; Stuck; Régence; Halbplastik; Lustschloss; Maison de Plaisance; Jagdschloss; Relief; Spiegelsaal

en.name: Amalienburg
description: The exterior of the broad, single-storey construction has a pale pink and white stucco facade. Its architectural centre is the round Hall of Mirrors, which curves towards the otherwise straight garden front and is vaulted by a flattened dome. On its roof, a circular platform with a skilfully forged balustrade served as a shooting stand for the Electress’s   pheasant hunt. Two equally sized wings adjoin to the Hall of Mirrors. They house hunting rooms, resting chambers, a kitchen and other rooms for the court society to enjoy their distractions . The stylistically homogeneous interior decoration of the Amalienburg is attributed to a cohesive concept of construction and décor.

Located in the Nymphenburg Palace Park, the elegant hunting pavilion was built in the style of a French maison de plaisance and is one of the greatest exponents of its kind, due to its prominent artful interior decoration. Starting in 1734, Charles Albert, Prince-Elector of Bavaria, assigned famous architect, François de Cuvilliés the Elder, to plan and build the Amalienburg for his wife Maria Amalia. The capriccio-like stucco décor of the interior in the late Régence  style is regarded as the magnum opus of Munich court stuccoer Johann Baptist Zimmermann.
artist: Prince-Elector Charles Albert of Bavaria (gov. 1726–45; 1742–45 as Charles VII, Holy Roman Emperor)
Architecture and ornament designs: François de Cuvilliés the Elder (1695–1768); Stucco: Johann Baptist Zimmermann (1680–1758); Ornamental carvings: Johann Joachim Dietrich (1690–1753)
history: During the reign of Charles Albert’s father, Prince-Elector Maximilian Emanuel, a garden pavilion existed at the location that would later become the Amalienburg. In 1734, Charles Albert tasked his court artist, François de Cuvilliés the Elder, with the construction of a hunting pavilion for his wife, Maria Amalia of Austria, daughter of Emperor Joseph I. Just five years later, the Amalienburg was completed and decorated with Johann Baptist Zimmermann's stuccowork and ornamental carvings from Johann Joachim Dietrich. The style and decorations of the Amalienburg were supposed to resemble a maison de plaisance, thereby following a trend from France where these hunting and summer estates had come into fashion in the 18th century. In accordance with the new living trend at the time, called "commodité" (intimate rooms and retreats for informal relaxation), they were designed to escape the strict court etiquette and indulge in hunting, celebrating and other kinds of leisure distractions in an intimate setting.
partner: University of Munich, Institute of Art History

en.name: Stand for Sweets
description:
The sweets stand was made in the factory of Nacko Janković & Son in Jagodina in the last decade of the 19th century. It is made of pressed, partially transparent, partially opal blue glass. The stand consists of a plate with a raised, wave-pattern rim set atop a high stem attached to a smaller base, decorated with radial rings and stars.  
Serbia’s movement toward the European way of life during the 19th century included the acceptance of new cultural models. Everyday life, especially in urban areas, changed with the introduction of novelties such as the use of porcelain and crystal sets to the culture of dining. High quality glass could be seen at first only in formal cultural settings. Later, imported glass products were augmented by the more accessible domestic glass products, whose design relied on the imported products. Thus, the Nacko Janković & Son factory had a wide range of items for sweets consumption. In addition to various types of fruit, cakes and sweets stands, candy bowls and saucepans, the Nacko Janković & Son factory produced various dishes for the traditional *slatko*, a special delight prepared from fruit, bowls for sugar or "*ratluk*", sweet Turkish delight, etc.
artist: Manufactury of Nacko Janković & Son, Serbia
keywords: Coloured glass; Mould-pressed; Brushed decoration

en.name: *Egypt. Plan of the remains of an existing circus, near Alexandria.*
names: Taken from *Description de l'Egypte: Dessins Préparatoires*
short_description: During the Egyptian expedition (1798–1801), Napoléon Bonaparte brought with him a group of scholars, engineers and artists, charged with collecting as much scientific information as possible. This was then used in a publication (of exceptional quality and execution) entitled Description de l'Égypte, in which the observations and enquiries made by the military expedition in Egypt were collected. The collection comprises of 10 volumes of illustrations and 9 volumes of texts published between 1809 and 1826.
keywords: Egyptian antiquities; Egyptomania

fr.name: *Egypte. Plan des restes d'un cirque existant, près d'Alexandrie*
names: Extrait de *Description de l'Egypte. Dessins préparatoires*
short_description: Napoléon Bonaparte a emmené avec lui, lors de l’expédition d'Égypte (1798-1801), un groupe de savants, d’ingénieurs et de dessinateurs, chargés de relever le plus grand nombre possible d’informations scientifiques. Les notes et dessins servent ensuite à une publication exceptionnelle de par sa qualité et son exécution, intitulée *Description de l'Égypte, ou Recueil des observations et des recherches qui ont été faites en Égypte pendant l'expédition de l'Armée française*. L’ensemble comprend 10 volumes de planches et 9 volumes de textes publiés entre 1809 et 1826.
keywords: Antiquités égyptiennes; égyptomanie

ar.name: حزامان من العاج مزينان بالمجوهرات.
description:
حزامان من العاج، أحدهما يتألف من خمس صفائح مزوَّدة برصائع بيضوية، والآخر من أربع صفائح مع رصائع دائرية متصلة ببعضها بعضاً بواسطة مجموعات من القطع الصغيرة المترابطة، وجميعها مزخرفة بعدة طبقات. السطوح منقوشة بزخارف من أزهار ونباتات معترشة أنيقة ذات خطوط مشبعة بصمغ المصطكاء الأسود. الطبقة الثانية من الزخرفة تشتمل على ورود ذهبية تضم في مركزها الياقوت والتركواز، وترتبط بنباتات ذات أوراق ذهبية. الخلفية محجوبة تحت زخرفة شاملة، أما المواد الأساسية فتشع بأحجار كريمة مرصوفة بشكل رائع. إن الأزهار المنضدة بالذهب وتقنية الزخرفة ذات الطبقات المتعددة تعكس أناقة صنع المجوهرات في عهد السلطان سليمان القانوني (حكم في الفترة 926- 974 / 1520- 1566).  
  
تأسست تنظيمات الفنانين والحرفيين (ما يدعى أهل الحرف) في عهد السلطان بايزيد الثاني (حكم في الفترة 886- 918/ 1481- 1512)، وكانت هذه التنظيمات بمثابة مدارس لجميع حقول الفن العثماني. يمكن معرفة عدد الفنانين المشتغلين في القصر من خلال سجلات الرواتب التي تم الاحتفاظ بها بصورة نظامية بدءاً من عهد سليمان القانوني.  
  
تعدّ الأحزمة من ملحقات الزينة الشائعة للرجال والنساء، فقد كانت تستخدم حول الخصر لتجميل اللباس وتزيينه. علاوة على ذلك، فهي تحمل مغزى طقسياً أيضاً. كما أن تعزيز منزلة شخص ما كان يتم عبر الاحتفال بتطويقه بالحزام. وهذه العادة، المعروفة لدى النقابات الحرفية، كانت هامة للسلاطين أيضاً، وتم التأكيد عليها من خلال وضع الحزام على النصب التذكارية للسلاطين ورجال الحاشية المتوفين. ففي العهد العثماني كانت الأحزمة تنتج من الأقمشة الغالية وتطرَّز بخيوط الذهب والفضة. أما الأحزمة المنقوشة والمزينة، المصنوعة من الصفائح المعدنية المرصوفة لصق بعضها بعضاً، فتعكس مستويات راقية في مهارة الصنعة. وفي حين كانت أحزمة النساء غنية بالزخارف، فقد كانت تلك التي يرتديها الرجال خالية من الزخارف إلى حد ما.

في الفترة العثمانية، كانت الأحزمة تُستخدم ليس فقط ملاحق للملابس النسوية والرجالية، بل وبوصفها مكافآت ملكية ممنوحة، لدى الترقية إلى مراتب أعلى، أو عند القيام بإنجازات مهنية مميزة، في حفلات خاصة لـ "لف الأحزمة".
keywords: حزام؛ عاج.

en.name: Bejewelled ivory belts.
description:
Two ivory belts, one comprising five large plaques with oval medallions, and the other four large plaques with round medallions, attached to each other with groups of small conjoined rectangular pieces. All are decorated in multiple layers. The surfaces are decorated with finely engraved spiralling tendrils and flower motifs, their lines filled with black mastic. The second layer of decoration includes gold flowers with rubies and turquoises at their centres, connected to tendrils with golden leaves. The background is concealed under the all-pervasive decoration, and the base materials are outshone by the ostentatiously encrusted stones. The deeply inlaid flowers in gilded settings, and the technique of decoration in multiple layers, reflect the courtly art of jewellery during the reign of Süleyman the Magnificent (r. AH 926–74 / AD 1520–66).  
  
The organisations of court artists and artisans (called the Ehl-i Hiref) were founded in the reign of Bayezid II (r. AH 886–918 / AD 1481–1512) and these organisations served as a school for all fields of Ottoman art. The number of artists at work in the palace can be followed from the books of salaries, which were kept regularly beginning in the reign of Süleyman the Magnificent.  
  
A popular accessory for both men and women, belts were used to enrich and decorate a costume, secured around the waist. They bore a ritual meaning as well. Promotion to a certain rank was completed with the ceremony of girding on a belt. This custom, known from professional guilds was important for the sultans as well, and it was emphasised by placing a belt on the cenotaphs of deceased sultans and courtiers. In the Ottoman period, belts were produced from precious textiles and embroidered with silver and gold threads. Carved and ornamented belts made from metal plaques fitted side by side exhibit high standards of craftsmanship. While women's belts were elaborately decorated, those worn by men were fairly plain.

In the Ottoman period, belts were used not only as accessories for women's and men's costumes, but were also palatial awards given for promotion to a higher rank or for remarkable professional accomplishments in a 'belt girding' ceremony.
holder: Museum of Turkish and Islamic Arts.
dates: Hegira, first half of the 10th century / AD 16th century.
keywords: Belt; ivory; costume; floral motifs; precious gems

es.name: Cinturones de marfil con piedras preciosas.
description:
Dos cinturones de marfil, uno de ellos formado por cinco placas con medallones ovalados y el otro, por cuatro placas con medallones redondos, unidas entre sí por cadenas de pequeñas piezas rectangulares. Ambos presentan varias capas de decoración. Las superficies están adornadas con zarcillos espirales y motivos florales finamente grabados con las líneas rellenas de almáciga negra. La segunda capa de decoración contiene flores doradas con rubíes y turquesas en el centro, unidas entre sí por zarcillos con hojas de oro. El fondo está oculto bajo la abundante ornamentación y los materiales básicos quedan eclipsados por las suntuosas piedras engastadas. Las flores incrustadas profundamente en engastaduras de oro y la técnica de la decoración en varias capas reflejan el arte de la joyería palaciega durante el sultanato de Süleyman el Magnífico (926-974 / 1520-1566).  
Bajo de Bayezid II (r. 886-918 / 1481-1512) se fundaron organizaciones de artistas y artesanos de la corte –llamadas *Ehl-i Hiref*– en las que se enseñaban todas las ramas del arte otomano. El número de artistas que trabajaban en el palacio se conoce gracias a los libros de salarios, que comenzaron a mantenerse regularmente a partir del sultanato de Süleyman el Magnífico.  
Los cinturones eran un accesorio popular entre hombres y mujeres, que se los ponían para adornar su vestimenta. También tenían un significado ritual; el ascenso a determinados rangos se completaba con la ceremonia de ceñirse un cinturón. Esta costumbre, común en los gremios profesionales, también era importante para los sultanes, como demuestra la tradición de colocar cinturones en los cenotafios de los sultanes y cortesanos fallecidos.  
En el periodo otomano, los cinturones se fabricaban con ricos tejidos y se bordaban con hilos de oro y plata. Los cinturones tallados y adornados con placas de metal acopladas demuestran un elevado nivel de destreza artesanal. Los cinturones de mujer estaban laboriosamente decorados, pero los masculinos tenían escasa decoración.

En el periodo otomano, los cinturones se usaban como accesorios, pero también se obsequiaban en palacio, en ceremonias de "imposición del cinturón", a aquellos que ascendían a un rango superior o alcanzaban un logro profesional notable.
holder: Museo de Arte Turco e Islámico.

fr.name: Ceinture d’ivoire ornée de pierres précieuses.
description:
Ceinture d'ivoire composée de cinq importantes plaques à médaillons lobés attachés par des chaînes de petites pièces rectangulaires. Chaque élément comporte plusieurs niveaux de décor. Les surfaces sont ornées de vrilles spiralées finement gravées et de motifs de fleurs aux lignes de gravure comblées de mastic noir. Le second niveau comprend des fleurs d'or ornées de rubis et de turquoises, réunies par des vrilles à feuilles dorées. Le fond disparaît sous cette surabondance de décor et les matériaux de base sont éclipsés par la présence ostentatoire des pierres. Les fleurs incrustées d'ornements en or et la technique de décor à multiples niveaux reflètent l'art de la joaillerie de cour sous le règne de Soliman le Magnifique (r. 926-974 H / 1520-1566). Les organisations d'artistes et d'artisans de la cour (appelées *Ehl-i Hiref*) fondées sous le règne de Bayézid II (r. 886-918 H / 1481-1512 J.-C.) enseignaient également dans les domaines de l'art ottoman. Le nombre d'artistes travaillant au palais figure dans les livres de salaires régulièrement tenus à partir du règne de Soliman le Magnifique.  
Accessoire important aussi bien pour les hommes que pour les femmes, les ceintures servaient à orner et enrichir un costume. Elles possédaient également un sens rituel. Une promotion à un certain rang s'accompagnait de la cérémonie de la remise d'une ceinture. Cette coutume, connue dans les guildes professionnelles, était également très pratiquée par les sultans, comme le manifeste le dépôt d'une ceinture sur leur cénotaphe ou sur celui de courtisans décédés. Pendant la période ottomane, des modèles furent fabriqués en textiles précieux brodés de fils d'or et d'argent. Les ceintures ornementales sculptées et ornementées, faites de plaques de métal accolées, témoignent de hauts critères de fabrication. Si les ceintures des femmes étaient d'une décoration élaborée, celles des hommes restaient assez sobres.

Durant la période ottomane, les ceintures étaient non seulement utilisées comme accessoires pour les costumes des femmes et des hommes, mais aussi comme récompenses palatiales attribuées, pour une promotion à un rang supérieur ou en reconnaissance d’accomplissements professionnels remarquables, au cours d’une cérémonie de “remise de ceinture”.

tr.name: Murassa Fildişi Kemerler.
description:
Fildişi kemerler, dilimli beş büyük madalyonlu pafta ve onları bağlayıcı mafsallı, birbirine geçmeli küçük ara paftalardan oluşur. üzerleri kademeli bezelidir. Tüm yüzey siyah tutkallı boyayla (mastika) ince bir uçla kazanarak kıvrım dal ve çiçeklerle süslenmiştir. İkinci kademe süsleme, altın yapraklı dallarla bağlı, yakut ve firuze göbekli çiçeklerdir. Tüm yüzeyi saran bu süsleme altında, zemin kaybolmakta, yapım malzemesi ve form gösterişli kakma taşlar yanında geri plana itilmektedir. çiçeklerin altın yuvalarının formu ve derin gömme biçimi, kademeli yüzey değerlendirmesi Kanuni Sultan Süleyman (926-974 / 1520-1566) dönemi saray kuyumculuğunu yansıtır. Osmanlı sanatının her dalı için bir okul işlevi görecek olan sanatçı ve zanaatçı örgütlerinin (Ehl-i Hiref) örgütlerinin kurulmasına II. Bayezid (886-918 / 1481-1512) döneminde başlanır. Topkapı Sarayı'nda görev yapan bu örgütlü sanatçıların sayısı, Kanuni Sultan Süleyman döneminden itibaren tutulan düzgün maaş defterlerinden izlenebilmektedir.  
  
Hem erkek, hem de kadın giyiminin başta gelen aksesuarlarından olan kemer, giysiyi biçimlendirme, süsleme, bele oturmasını sağlama amacının dışında ritüel bir anlamda taşımıştır. Belli bir rütbeye ve makam ulaşmış olmak kemer kuşanma töreni ile tamamlanmıştır. örneklerini esnaf loncalarında tanıdığımız bu adet tahta çıkan sultanlar içinde önem taşımış, bu gelenek ölen Sultan ve Saray mensuplarının türbelerinde sandukaların üzerine kemer koyma adeti ile de vurgulanmıştır. Osmanlı döneminde değerli kumaşlardan yapılan kemerler, sırma, sim ile işleniyordu. üzeri işlemeli, çeşitli biçimlerde bezenmiş maden plakaların yan yana dizilmesiyle meydana gelen kemerler ince bir işçilik sergilemektedir. Kadınların kullandıkları kemerlerin çok gösterişli olması yanında erkek kemerleri oldukça sadedir.

Erkek ve kadın giysilerinde kullanılan kemer, Osmanlı döneminde giysiyi biçimlendirme ve süsleme amacı dışında, belli bir rütbe ve görevde gösterilen başarı derecesine göre 'kemer kuşanma' geleneğinin devamı olarak saray tarafından verilen bir ödül niteliği de taşımaktaydı.
keywords: Kemer; Fildişi

ar.name: قبة السماء.
description: القطعة عبارة عن رسم لقبة السماء بأبراجها المختلفة نفذ على القبة التي تعلو الحجرة الساخنة في حمام قصير عمرة. من الواضح أن هذا الرسم قد نسخ من مخطوطة، ونقل على السطح الكروي للقبة. تظهر في الرسم بعض الأخطاء مما يدل على أنها نسخت بواسطة شخص ليس على دراية بعلم الفلك. تجدر الإشارة إلى أن قبة السماء في قصير عمرة هي أقدم صورة رسمت على سطح كروي معروفة حتى الآن.
اللوحة الفسيفسائية للمجرَّات، على قبة المرجل، في قُصيِّر عمرة، هي الصورة الأقدم الباقية للنجوم على سطح كروي. عددٌ من الأخطاء في المواضع، تشي بأن الرسَّام لم يكن مطلعاً على علم الفلك.
dates: النصف الأول من القرن 2 ﻫ/ 8 م.
keywords: أبراج؛ الحجرة الساخنة؛ فلك؛ قبة السماء.

en.name: Fresco on the Cupola.
description: The caldarium or hot room in the *hammam* (bath) at Qusayr ‘Amra has a fresco of the constellations on the cupola; the earliest surviving representation of the stars on a spherical surface. The painting was apparently copied from a manuscript and transferred to the cupola. A number of errors in the placement of the constellations indicate the painting was executed by someone who was not familiar with Astrology.

The fresco of the constellations on the cupola of the caldarium at Qusayr ‘Amra is the earliest surviving representation of the stars on a spherical surface. A number of errors in the placements indicate that the painter was not familiar with astrology.
dates: Hegira first third of the 2nd century / AD first half of the 8th century.
keywords: Astrology; caldarium; constellations; cupola; Fresco

es.name: Fresco de la cúpula
description: El *caldarium* o sala caliente de los baños de Qusayr Amra posee una cúpula que está decorada con un fresco de las constelaciones; es la representación más antigua que se conserva de las estrellas en una superficie esférica. Parece ser que la pintura se copió de un manuscrito y se trasladó a la cúpula. Hay diversos errores en la colocación de las constelaciones, lo cual indica que la realizó un artista que no sabía astrología.

El fresco de las constelaciones de la cúpula del *caldarium* de Qusayr Amra es la primera representación que se conserva de las estrellas en una superficie esférica. Varios errores en su ubicación indican que su autor no sabía astrología.
holder: En su emplazamiento original, Qusayr Amra.
dates: Primer tercio del siglo II de la Hégira / segunda mitad del siglo VIII d. C.
keywords: Astrología; caldarium; constelaciones; cúpula; fresco.

fr.name: Fresque de coupole.
description: Le *caldarium*, ou pièce chaude, du hammam de Qousayr Amra est surmonté d'une coupole décorée d'une fresque représentant les constellations. Il s'agit de la plus ancienne représentation subsistante d'astres sur une surface sphérique. La fresque a sans doute été copiée dans un manuscrit. Un certain nombre d'erreurs dans l'emplacement des constellations montre que le peintre n'avait pas de connaissances astrologiques.

La fresque des constellations de la coupole du caldarium de Qousayr Amra est la plus ancienne représentation d’étoiles sur une surface sphérique à nous être parvenue. Un certain nombre d’erreurs dans le positionnement des astres montre que le peintre n’avait pas de connaissances astrologiques.
dates: Premier tiers du IIe siècle de l’Hégire (première moitié du VIIIe siècle J.-C.).
keywords: fresques ; astrologie ; caldarium ; constellations, coupoles

en.name: Church of Santa María la Antigua
description: The Church of Santa María la Antigua is 12th-century Mudéjar with three naves in brick of the second style of Sahagún. It has three apses with two levels of blind arcades in brick, those on the higher level larger in proportion. It is finished off with a frieze of raked courses and a *scotia* under the eaves. The interior decoration has two similar levels, which converge in an apse vault. The aisles and part of the apses were renovated some time later, but now neither the roof nor the vaulting is preserved. The plasterwork realised by the Corral de Villalpando family has also disappeared. The tower and part of the original walls can still be seen at the base, since this church, along with others in the town had a dual religious and defensive function. This wall is from the end of the 12th century and possibly dates from the resettlement of the town in 1170.

es.name: Iglesia de Santa María la Antigua
description: La iglesia de Santa María la Antigua es mudéjar del siglo XII, con tres naves en ladrillo y del estilo segundo de Sahagún. Tiene tres ábsides con dos pisos de arquerías ciegas de ladrillo, mayores en proporción los del piso superior. La remata un friso de esquinillas y una nacela en el alero. El interior también está decorado con dos pisos iguales, que convergen en bóveda de horno. Las naves y parte de los ábsides fueron reformados en época posterior, pero actualmente no conservan techo ni bóveda. También desaparecieron del todo las yeserías realizadas por la familia de los Corral de Villalpando. A los pies se mantienen la torre y parte de la muralla original, que, como en otros templos de la villa, cumplía una doble función, religiosa y defensiva. Es muralla de fines del siglo XII, y posiblemente data de la repoblación de la villa en 1170.

en.name: Head
description:
Martin Janecký is one of the best-known Czech artists for his use of a technique based on modelling from inside a bubble of melted glass, known as “inside sculpting”. This technique requires great precision in order to control the thickness of the glass, its temperature and ductility, in addition to great skill in managing the tools. Martin works with the help of incredibly skilled assistants who work with him in perfect synchronisation. Janecký can be identified primarily for his head and hand sculptures,  
created with diverse attitudes, textures and tones.  
Martin began to work with glass at age 13 in his father’s factory. He graduated from the Glass School in Nový Bor in 1998, and it wasn’t until 2003 that he began to gain international acknowledgement following his trip to a glass symposium at the Corning Museum of Glass.  
He has been a guest artist at numerous glass schools, workshops and museums across the globe, demonstrating how he creates his sculptures. Some of these include the Corning Studio, Museum of Glass (USA), Pilchuck Glass School, Tacoma Museum of Glass, Stand Wood, Chrysler, Norfolk, Bronholm, Rietvel and at the Real Fábrica de Cristales de La Granja, where he created this piece during his stay in 2017.

es.name: Head
description:
Martin Janecký representa uno de los artistas checos más conocidos por utilizar una técnica basada en el modelado desde el interior de una burbuja de vidrio fundido “inside sculpting” (escultura interior). Técnica que exige una gran precisión para controlar el espesor del vidrio, su temperatura y ductibilidad, además de una gran destreza en el manejo de las herramientas. Martin trabaja con la ayuda de hábiles asistentes perfectamente sincronizados con él. Janecký se identifica sobre todo por sus esculturas de cabezas y manos  
en actitudes, texturas y tonalidades muy diferentes.  
Martin comenzó a trabajar con vidrio, a la edad de 13 años, en la fábrica de su padre. En 1998 se graduó en la escuela de vidrio de Nový Bor y no será hasta el año 2003, a raíz de su viaje a un simposium de vidrio celebrado en el Corning Museum of Glass, cuando comenzó a darse a conocer a nivel internacional.  
Ha sido artista invitado en numerosas escuelas, talleres y museos de vidrio de todo el mundo para mostrar el modo de trabajar sus esculturas, como en el Studio del Corning, Museum of Glass (USA), la Pilchuck Glass School, Tacoma Museum of Glass, Stand Wood, Chrysler, Norfolk, Bronholm, Rietvel y en la Real Fábrica de Cristales de La Granja, donde realizó esta obra durante su estancia en el año 2017.

en.name: Painting of Vittorio Emanuele II, King of Italy
short_description: This oil on canvas portrait from 1862 depicts the King Vittorio Emanuele II (1861–1878). Fair-skinned with blue eyes and brown hair, the king is dressed in official uniform, with a black jacket and silver buttons and a silver belt. The Ordre du Sang, the Nichan al-Dam and the Annunziata medals are on the left of his chest. A royal red cape is draped over his shoulders, bordered by gold decorations, a white fur collar and lapels embellished with black feathers. A gold crown decorated with red and green strasses sits is on his left, and red curtains with tassels and tiebacks in the same colour form the backdrop. This painting is evidence of an active diplomatic relationship between the Palais du Bardo and the European chancelleries.
holder: Musée d’Histoire Moderne et Contemporaine de Kassar Saïd
keywords: Oil on canvas; Vittorio Emanuele II
materials: Canvas, wood, coloured pigments, gold leaf

fr.name: Tableau de peinture *Le roi d’Italie Victor-Emmanuel II*
short_description: Tableau de peinture à l’huile sur toile réalisé en 1862, il représente le portrait du roi Victor-Emmanuel II (1861-1878). De teint clair aux yeux bleus avec des cheveux marron, le roi porte son costume officiel, composé d’une veste noire avec des boutons en argent et une ceinture argentée. Sur la partie gauche de la poitrine, l’ordre du sang, le Nichan ad-Dam sous la plaque de l’ordre de l’Annonciade. Le roi porte une cape royale rouge avec des motifs décoratifs dorés dans la lisière et un col revers en fourrure blanche ornée de plumes noires. Une couronne dorée et ornée de strasses vertes et rouges se trouve sur son côté gauche tandis qu’un rideau rouge avec franges et embrasses de même couleur se trouve en arrière-plan. Œuvre témoin d’une intense activité diplomatique entre le palais du Bardo et les chancelleries occidentales.
holder: Musée d’Histoire moderne et contemporaine de Kassar Saïd

en.name: *Meshouf* (canoe collection)
description:
The Open Museum for Water Cultures (Basra) holds in its collection 11 *meshoufs* of various types and sizes. *Meshouf* is a generic term for a flat-based canoe made in the region of Iraq's southern marshlands. *meshoufs* range from 3-11m in length and have a narrow form, often with a distinctive crescent-shaped prow.  
  
Variants range from small flat-prowed canoes like the *matour* (a one-man canoe used for hunting waterfowl), to larger types with a prominent curved prow such as the *chilaika*, the prestigious *tarada* (hunting and war canoe of the Marsh Sheikhs), and working vessels like the *barkash*, used for harvesting and transport.  
  
*Meshoufs* became almost extinct from the Iran-Iraq war (1980s) onwards. In Huwair, once a well-known centre for their making, modernised boatbuilding methods and carpentry remained common forms of livelihood. *Meshouf* production was revived with the support of the Safina Projects initiative from AH 1440 / AD 2018 onwards. In addition to the Open Museum’s collection, by AH 1447/ AD 2025 over 70 *meshoufs* were in use across the Iraqi Heritage Boat Clubs Network established by Safina.  
  
Boats of a comparable form have been recorded since the Sumerian period (from around 2500 BC), although in the modern-day *meshouf* the prow is typically much taller than the stern, whereas in the Sumerian version prow and stern are of equal height.  
  
Rashad Salim’s research with Safina Projects has concluded that the AH 14th/ AD 20th century *meshouf* was strongly influenced by the availability of industrially manufactured nails and tools and imported wood. In the pre-industrial period, wood was scarcer, and many marsh dwellers made *meshoufs* from reeds.  
  
The extended family who built the *meshoufs* in this collection are among the most renowned boatbuilders of Huwair. They are part of the Beni Asad tribe, who came to the marshes 300-400 years ago from Arabia, learned boatbuilding methods from the Mandaean-Sabean population, and gradually took over as the main practitioners of the craft.
holder: Open Museum Initiative for Water Cultures
artist: Zuhair Rissan Obaid (Abu Sajjad), Jewad Kadhim Allawi (Abu Kadhim), Hassan Shakir Abdallah, Adil Shakir Abdallah, Nassir Saddam Saalim, Hafedh Ghaji Jabbar, Yusuf Majid Jassim, Duway Rissan Obaid, Munshid Abu Nassir

en.name: Citadel
description:
The history of the Ayasuluğ Citadel stretches back as far as the 4th century AD. During the time of Byzantine Emperor Justinian (AD 527-565), a large church was constructed in the name of St. John next to the fortress and later surrounded by walls. St. John’s Church was enclosed within the walls when the fortifications were extended because of the threat of Arab raids. The fortress was reinforced through periodic repairs after the city’s fall to the hands of Mehmed Bey, son of Aydın, in 1304. During the Turkish period Ayasuluğ ranked high as one of the East Mediterranean’s most lively trading centres and important harbours. Merchants from, for instance, Venice, Genoa and Pisa dealt in international trade here. Evidence of the importance of this town is several-fold: the Venetian Consulate became intensely active in the city beginning in 1337; the Genoese Consulate was founded here in 1351; the number of westerners living in the city increased and trade agreements were made between the Aydın Emirate and westerners.  
As its importance continued throughout the Ottoman period, up to 60 military guards charged with protecting the citadel were present in the time of Sultan Mehmed II. At the end of the 16th century, various tax exemptions were granted to those working on the renovation of the citadel. Evliya Çelebi, who visited Ayasuluğ in 1671, states that the citadel, founded on a steep stone outcrop, had a circumference of 300 footsteps (approximately 200 meters) and that about 40 people were on duty.  
The walls constructed of re-used materials are still in good condition today; the main entrance preserves its original shape; an old Byzantine chapel, several cisterns, and a small mosque are located within the walls.

es.name: Ciudadela
description:
La historia de la ciudadela de Ayasuluğ se remonta nada menos que al siglo IV. En la época del emperador bizantino Justiniano (527-565), cerca de la fortaleza se construyó una gran iglesia consagrada a San Juan que más tarde se rodeó de una muralla, coincidiendo con la extensión de las fortificaciones debido a la amenaza de las incursiones árabes. La ciudadela fue reforzada con reformas periódicas después de caer en manos de Mehmet Bey, hijo de Aydın, en 1304. Durante el periodo turco, Ayasuluğ fue uno de los centros comerciales y de los puertos más activos. Mercaderes de Venecia, Génova, Pisa, etcétera, hacían tratos comerciales en él. De la importancia de la ciudad dan fe, entre otras cosas, que en 1337 el consulado veneciano estuviese en plena actividad, que en 1351 se abriera el consulado genovés, que el número de europeos establecidos en la ciudad fuese en aumento y que el emirato aydiní cerrara acuerdos comerciales con los occidentales.  
La ciudad conservó su importancia en el periodo otomano, y en tiempos del sultán Mehmet II había hasta 60 soldados protegiendo la ciudadela. A finales del siglo XVI, se concedieron exenciones de impuestos a quienes trabajaban en la reforma de la ciudadela. Evliya Çelebi, que visitó Ayasuluğ en 1671, escribe que esta, levantada sobre un promontorio rocoso, tenía un perímetro de 300 pies (unos 200 m) y un cuerpo de guardia de unas 40 personas.  
La muralla, construida con materiales de expolio, está aún en buen estado; la puerta principal conserva su forma original; intramuros hay una antigua capilla bizantina, varias cisternas y una pequeña mezquita.

en.name: Information book for the Syrian Hejaz railway
description: This rare document provides crucial insight into the Hijaz Railway during the Arab Revolt led by T.E. Lawrence. It outlines essential regulations regarding train operations and communication, highlighting the railway's strategic role in disrupting Ottoman reinforcements. This manual also explores the logistical challenges of wartime, contributing to our understanding of military strategy and railway operations.
keywords: Railways; Saudi Arabia; Hejaz

description: المعراج هو مشهد صعود النبي العظيم محمد للسماء وصولا لعرش الله .وأصبحت أيقونية المشهد راسخة في تقاليد فن الرسم الإيراني منذ القرن الخامس عشر. وقد فتح التأليف المترافق للمعراج مع الثناء الشعري على الله ورسوله بشكل تقليدي الباب لكتابة مخطوطات عن أعمال تاريخية ، بيوغرافية وشعرية للأدب الفارسي الكلاسيكي.ونرى في وسط المشهد  النبي محمد يمتطي الحيوان الرائع البراق وهو عبارة عن فرس برأس امرأة.ويصور النبي محمد عادة محاطا بهالة متوهجة كبيرة حول رأسه ويغطى وجهه بحجاب والذي ربما أضيف لاحقا للصورة .ونرى أمام النبي  الملاك جبريل وهو يريه الطريق. وفوق الملاك هناك أسد وهو التشخيص السماوي لعلي أول إمام معتبر من قبل الشيعة. والملائكة الحاملين للهدايا يطيرون حول النبي. ويوجد بين الشخوص مقابل السماء الزرقاء غيوم صينية كثيفة. وموضوع المنمنمة يجمع معجزتين مهمتين في الإسلام هما الإسراء (سورة رقم17) والتي تقص سفر النبي ليلا طائرا من مكة إلى القدس والمعراج والتي رويت في الحديث وهي قصة معجزة صعود النبي للسماء وصولا لعرش الله.

en.name: Miniature 'Mi'raj (the Miraculous Ascension) of Prophet Muhammad'
description: Mi'raj is the scene of the Ascension of the Great Prophet Muhammad to Heaven to the throne of Allah. The iconography of the scene has become established in the Iranian painting tradition since the late AD 15th century. The composition of Mi'raj, together with the poetic dedication of God and His Prophet, traditionally opened manuscripts of historical, biographical and poetic works of classical Persian literature. In the centre of the scene we see Prophet Muhammad riding the fantastic animal Boraq, a mare with a woman’s head. Muhammad is traditionally depicted with a large flaming halo around his head. His face is covered by a veil, probably added to the picture later. In front of the Prophet, we see the Archangel Jabriel showing the way. Above the Archangel there is a lion, the heavenly personification of Ali, the first righteous Imam of the Shiites. Angels with gifts fly around the Prophet. Between the figures against the blue sky, golden "Chinese" clouds abound. The miniature subject combines two important Islamic legends. The Qur'anic Al-Isra (Night Journey, Surah 17) recounts the Prophet's magical night flight from Mecca to Jerusalem. The Al-Mi'raj (Staircase), narrated in hadiths, is the story of Muhammad's miraculous ascent to Heaven to the throne of God.
keywords: Mi'raj; Miniature; Iran; Safavid
materials: Opaque watercolour and gold on paper

en.name: Tuqan Family Soap Factory
description:
Established by the Tuqan Family at the end of the 13th/19th century, this soap factory is a large two-storey rectangular building, whose main façade overlooks al-Tuta Square. The façade is quite simple but has a large entrance portal at the centre to facilitate the entry of oil carriers and the exit of boxes of soap. The door is wooden and has a pointed arch above it, flanked by several windows topped by pointed arches, which are usually closed from the inside. Unlike the lower part of the entrance, the upper part is covered by large windows to allow ventilation which helps the soap dry.  
The large entrance leads into the ground floor, which is the administrative and production sector, including the finance office and the manager’s office. Soap manufacture takes place on this floor, which consists of a large hall with a high cross-vault ceiling, supported by stone pillars in the centre. A large area, called *al-balat* (the pavement), has a huge pot in which the process of cooking the soap takes place. In front of it is a semicircular basin called a *mibzal*, and next to this are several square containers for fermented and pure water. Under the pot is a small room that contains the furnace. The cooking process takes place here, enabling the soap to develop. It can be reached through a staircase opposite the *mibzal*. On top of the furnace is a chimney that extends high above the factory. Also on this floor is a cistern for storing oil when it is in season.  
On the south-eastern side of the factory is a staircase that leads to the upper floor, which consists of a large flat space called *mafrash*. Here the sticky soap is spread until it dries. Then it is cut into shapes by sharp metal tools. The pieces are arranged into a cylindrical lighthouse shape to allow the air through until they are completely dry and ready to use. The ceiling of this floor consists of successive shallow domes supported by arches that stand on pillars.

es.name: Factoría de jabón de la familia Tuqan
description:
Esta jabonería, fundada por la familia Tuqan a finales del siglo XIII/XIX, es un gran edificio de piedra de planta rectangular y dos niveles. Su fachada principal, escasamente decorada, da a la plaza al-Tuta y se distingue sobre todo por su gran entrada central, concebida para facilitar la descarga de aceite y la salida de las cajas de jabón. Sobre la puerta de madera aparece un arco apuntado, rodeado de pequeñas ventanas, generalmente cerradas desde el interior y rematadas, a su vez, por un arco apuntado. La parte superior de la fachada presenta, a diferencia de la parte inferior, ventanas de gran tamaño destinadas a facilitar la ventilación, que contribuye al secado del jabón.  
La gran entrada conduce al interior de la planta baja, el centro de la actividad administrativa y productiva, con las oficinas de dirección y contabilidad. Esta planta consta de una larga sala con un techo alto, cubierta de bóvedas por arista apoyadas sobre pilares de piedra, donde se lleva a cabo la fabricación del jabón. En esta planta un espacio amplio, llamado *al-balat* (pavimento), alberga una gigantesca caldera para la cocción del jabón. Delante de esta caldera hay una pila semicircular que se llama *mibzal*; junto a esta, otras pilas cuadradas recogen el agua de fermentación y el agua limpia. Debajo de la caldera se sitúa una pequeña habitación en la que se encuentra el horno donde se realiza el proceso de combustión que permite la cocción del jabón, y a la cual se accede por una escalera situada frente al *mibzal*. En la parte superior del horno hay una gran chimenea cuyo conducto se eleva muy por encima de la factoría. En esta planta también hay un pozo donde se almacena el aceite.  
En el lado sureste de la jabonería, una escalera conduce a la planta superior, una gran superficie plana llamada *mafrach*, donde se extiende el jabón líquido para que se seque. Luego se corta con unas herramientas metálicas extremadamente afiladas. Los trozos se colocan en forma de cilindro —como en forma de faros—, para permitir la circulación del aire hasta que los jabones se sequen totalmente y sean aptos utilizarse. La techumbre de esta planta está formada por una serie de cúpulas rebajadas que descansan sobre unos arcos sostenidos en pilares.

fr.name: Manufacture de savon de la famille Touqan
description:
C’est à la fin du XIIIe/XIXe siècle que la famille Touqan a fondé cette savonnerie, une imposante construction en pierre à deux niveaux et de plan rectangulaire. Assez peu décorée, la façade principale, qui donne sur le square al-Tuta, se distingue néanmoins par une grande entrée centrale conçue pour faciliter la décharge des huiles et la sortie des boîtes de savons. La porte, en bois, est surmontée d’un arc brisé entouré de petites fenêtres, généralement fermées de l’intérieur, dont chacune est coiffée d’un arc brisé. Contrairement à la partie inférieure de la façade, la partie supérieure est percée de grandes fenêtres destinées à faciliter la ventilation qui contribue au séchage du savon.  
La grande entrée conduit à l’intérieur du rez-de-chaussée, autrement dit au département administration et production, avec les bureaux de la direction et de la comptabilité. C’est là que s’effectue la fabrication du savon, dans une très vaste et haute salle couverte de voûtes d’arêtes reposant sur des piliers en pierre. Un grand espace appelé *al-balat* (pavement) y abrite une gigantesque cuve réservée à la cuisson du savon. Devant la cuve se trouve un bassin semi-circulaire appelé *mibzal*; à côté de ce dernier, d’autres bassins carrés recueillent l’eau de fermentation ainsi que l’eau pure. Sous la cuve est placée une petite pièce contenant le fourneau. Là se déroule le processus de combustion qui permet au savon de se former. On y accède par un escalier qui fait face au *mibzal*. Au-dessus du fourneau se trouve une cheminée dont le conduit s’élève très largement au-dessus de la manufacture. Toujours au même niveau, une citerne sert à stocker l’huile. Sur le côté sud-est de la savonnerie, un escalier conduit au premier étage, un immense espace plat appelé *mafrach* où l’on étale le savon liquide pour le laisser sécher. Le savon est ensuite coupé à l’aide d’instruments métalliques puissamment aiguisés. Les morceaux sont disposés en forme de cylindres – un peu en forme de phares –, de façon à permettre à l’air de circuler jusqu’à ce que les savons soient complètement secs et prêts à l’emploi. Le plafond de cet étage est composé d’une série de coupoles surbaissées qui prennent appui sur des arcs reposant à leur tour sur des piliers.
