en.name: Women's pants (*Don*)
short_description: The enclave of the Turkish Yoruk community in Macedonia living in the mountain villages of Dojran – Valandovo and Radovish – and the Shtip region is a genuine treasure of tangible and intangible heritage that adds to the diversity of traditional culture in Macedonia. In general terms, the traditional outfit of Yoruk women in Macedonia is distinguished with exceptional colouring and application of varied elements in all articles of clothing. This bridal attire preserves some of the traditions in clothing and embellishment of Yoruk women in Macedonia in the 19th century and the early 20th century. This piece of trousers shows decoration of embroidery with geometric patterns applied on the lower front part of the trousers.
keywords: costume; embroidery; geometric patterns; geometric motifs; Yörük community; nomads; Turkish; marriage; wedding
materials: White canvas decorated with embroidery og varied wool, as well as silver and gold wrapped thread

en.name: Portuguese carpet
description: The so-called Portuguese carpet of the MAK Collection can be regarded as the best preserved of the group of nine extant carpets and three fragments. “Scenes” depict people in the four corners of the main fields: boats with passengers in European attire sail on a heavy sea; a swimmer, fish, and a sea monster are in the water. Unusual for carpets, this depiction has led to various interpretations and notions about its genesis. Thus, one thought is of the legend from the Book of Jonah as a purely formal model, another is of the death of Bahadur Shah the Sultan of Gujarat, who drowned in 1537. European prints, converted to meet the more exotic tastes of an Iranian clientele, supposedly served as the template for the corner solution. The term “Portuguese carpets” developed out of the assumption that they had been produced in Iran for Portugal or Portuguese settlements in India, known as the Estado da India. Today, based on technical arguments, the Khorasan province in northeast Iran is generally accepted as the place of origin.
holder: MAK – Austrian Museum of Applied Arts / Contemporary Art
keywords: Safawid; textile; carpet; wool; cotton; floral design; figural design; animals
materials: Cotton warp and weft; wool; knotted; asymmetrical knot; scattered Jufti knot
partner: MAK – Austrian Museum of Applied Arts / Contemporary Art

en.name: Thirty belts
short_description: Belts like these were traditionally given to a bride by her parents, and were worn for the marriage ceremony. The belts are made of silver, and each one is carved with its tribe's traditional design. The bride would wear the belt of her own tribe during the ceremony as a sign of belonging. These belts date to the 19th century.
keywords: Accessories; Silver; Metalwork

en.name: *Khante*
description: A rectangular-shape carpet with two narrow string borders around a central *ebli* field. The central field has a red background on which are five small blue medallions decorated with flowers. Stylised vases of white flowers surround the medallions in the corners, developed in a four-one rhythmical pattern.
dates: Date unknown, purchased by the Museum in the 19th century
keywords: Carpet; Azerbaijan; Garabagh; *khante*; Xanliq
materials: Wool warp and weft; symmetrical knot

ar.name: ورقة من قرآن.
description: تضم هذه الورقة المأخوذة من قرآن مكتوب بالخط الكوفي الأسود، الآية الكريمة 8 من سورة التكاثر (سورة رقم 106)، والآية الكريمة الأولى من سورة العصر (سورة رقم 103). وقد أبرزت نقاط الإعجام للأحرف الصوتية باللون الأحمر، فيما تمت الإشارة إلى علامتي الهمزة والشدة بنقاط خضراء وصفراء وفقاً لنظام النحوي العربي، العلامة أبي الأسود، الذي توفي عام 61 للهجرة/ 681 ميلادية. وللإشارة إلى التقسيمات بين الآيات تم رسم عنصر زخرفي على شكل وردة ذهبية وسطها أخضر اللون، والتي شكلت حوافها بنقاط دقيقة كستنائية اللون. ويقوم العنوان الرائع للسورة في سطر من التزيينات من الخط الكوفي، والتي تنتهي بسعيفة نخل بارزة نحو الهامش، مؤلفة من وريقات ذهبية ومبسطة للغاية، ومن زخارف الرقش الإسلامي المزدانة بالزهور، التي جرى تزيينها باللون الأزرق والأخضر، مع لمسات رقيقة من اللون الكستنائي، وهي عناصر زخرفية تشكل جزءًا من الرصيد الزخرفي للمزخرفين وللخطاطين المسلمين منذ القرن 5 الهجري (القرن 11 الميلادي).

تضم هذه الورقة المكتوبة بالخط الكوفي الأسود نصين قرآنيين (السورة رقم 106- الآية 8 والسورة 103 – الآية 1). وقد تمت الإشارة إلى التقسيمات المتواجدة بين الآيات بوريدة مذهبة خضراء في الوسط؛ وتنتمي مجموعة الأشكال المرسومة إلى السجل الزخرفي الخاص بالمزوقين والخطاطين المسلمين منذ القرن 5 للهجرة (القرن 11 للميلاد).
dates: بداية الربع الثاني من القرن 5 الهجري/القرن 11 الميلادي.
keywords: فن الخط؛ الزخرفة النباتية؛ الحبوس؛ الوقف؛ قطعة دينية.

en.name: Page from a Qur’an.
description: Al-Takathur *sura* ('The Rivalry', 102: 8) and al-Asr *sura* ('The Time', 103: 1). This page is taken from a Qur'an written in black *kufic* script. The vowels are marked with red diacritic dots and the *hamza* and *shadda* are indicated by green and yellow marks in the style of Abi al-Aswad, the Arab grammarian (d. AH 61 / AD 681). The verses are divided by a gilded green-centred rosette outlined in brown dots. The magnificent title of the *sura* is contained within an ornamental line of *kufic,* terminating in a palm-leaf motif which projects into the margin of the page. This palm-leaf is composed of stylised, gilded leaves and floral arabesques and is illuminated in blue and green with delicate touches of brown. These motifs are part of the decorative repertoire of Muslim illuminators and calligraphers from the AH 5th / AD 11th century.

Written in black *kufic* script, this page contains two Qur'anic quotations (102: 8 and 103: 1). The division of verses is marked by a gold rosette with a green centre. All of the motifs belong to the decorative repertoire of Muslim illuminators and calligraphers after the AH 5th / AD 11th century.
dates: Hegira, beginning of the second quarter of the 5th century / AD 9th century.
keywords: Calligraphy; floral decoration; habus; religious objects; religious manuscript

es.name: Página de Corán.
description: Página con la última aleya de la sura CII (*Al-Takazur*, “La rivalidad”) y la primera de la CIII (*Al-Asr*, “La tarde”). Está extraída de un Corán escrito en letra cúfica negra. Las vocales se indican con puntos diacríticos rojos; la *hamza* y la *shadda*, con puntos verdes y amarillos, conforme al sistema de Abi al-Aswad, gramático árabe muerto en 61 / 681. Las divisiones entre los versículos se señalan con una roseta de oro, verde en el centro, cuyo contorno está dibujado con finos puntos de color marrón. El magnífico título de la sura se compone de una línea de ornamentación cúfica terminada en una palmeta que se proyecta hacia el margen. Hojas de oro muy estilizadas y arabescos florales integran esta palmeta, iluminada en azul y verde con delicadas pinceladas marrones. Estos motivos formaban parte desde el siglo V / XI del repertorio decorativo de iluminadores y calígrafos musulmanes.

Esta página, escrita en letra cúfica negra, contiene parte de las suras coránicas CII y CIII (aleyas 8 y 1 respectivamente). Una roseta dorada, con centro en verde, marca las divisiones entre versículos. El conjunto de motivos pintados formaba parte del repertorio decorativo de iluminadores y calígrafos musulmanes desde el siglo V / XI.
dates: Segundo cuarto del siglo V de la Hégira / XI d. C.
keywords: Caligrafía; decoración floral; habús; objeto religioso

fr.name: Feuillet d’un coran.
description: Sourates al-Thakathour (CII, “La rivalité”, verset 8) et al-Asr (CIII, “Le temps”, verset 1). Ce feuillet est tiré d'un coran écrit en coufique noir. Les voyelles sont marquées par des points diacritiques rouges, la hamza et la chaddah par des points verts et jaunes conformément au système d'Abi al-Aswad, le grammairien arabe mort en 61 H / 681 J.-C. Les divisions entre versets sont signalées par une rosette en or, verte au centre, dont les contours sont dessinés par de fins points marron. Le titre splendide de la sourate consiste en une ligne d'ornementation coufique terminée par une palmette qui se projette vers la marge. Cette palmette est composée de feuillets en or très stylisés et d'arabesques fleuries, elle est illuminée par le bleu et le vert, avec de délicates touches de marron. Ces motifs font partie du répertoire décoratif des enlumineurs et calligraphes musulmans depuis le Ve siècle H (XIe siècle J.-C.).

écrit en coufique noir, ce feuillet comporte deux citations coraniques (CII,8 et CIII,1). Les divisions entre les versets sont signalées par une rosette dorée, verte au centre. L'ensemble des motifs dessinés appartient au répertoire décoratif des enlumineurs et calligraphes musulmans depuis le Ve siècle H (XIe siècle J-C.).

en.name: The young ladies of the telephones: a view of a Parisian telephone exchange
short_description: The French telephone network was not automated at the beginning of the 20th century. Young unmarried women were often employed to take paying members' calls, and connect them to their requested number.
keywords: Communications; telephones; Paris; cartoon; caricature

fr.name: *Les Demoiselles du téléphone, aspect d'un bureau téléphonique parisien, du standard…*
short_description: Au début du XXe siècle, le réseau téléphonique français n’est pas automatisé. Des jeunes filles célibataires sont engagées pour prendre les demandes d'appel des abonnés, puis les mettre en relation.
keywords: Communications; Téléphone; Paris

de.name: Hauptfassade
description: Über zwei gedrungenen spätgotischen Laubenbögen erheben sich vier Stockwerke mit je drei Fensterachsen, deren mittlere von den beiden polygonalen Eckerkern symmetrisch gerahmt wird. Abschließend ein zusammenfassender barocker Grabendachgiebel mit Voluten und hochovalem Fenster in der Mitte. Der kraftvolle Stuck aus Blumen- und Fruchtgirlanden, Festons, Muscheln und Putten, verbunden durch Laub- und Bandelwerk, setzt außergewöhnlich plastische Akzente und bringt so den Reichtum und die Bedeutung des Bauherrn zum Ausdruck.

en.name: Main façade
description: Four storeys, each with three window axes, extend above two compact Late Gothic access arches, with the central axis symmetrically framed by two polygonal bay windows. The building is crowned by a Baroque valley roof gable with volutes and a vertical oval window in the centre. The bold stucco composed of garlands of flowers and fruit, festoons, shells and putti, linked by foliage and strapwork, establish an unusually sculptural accent, thus giving expression to the wealth and prestige of the building’s owner.

en.name: Scenes from the Life of John the Baptist
description:
John the Baptist was the cousin of Jesus Christ and preached in the Judean desert. He lived a life of self-denial by wearing camel hair clothing and eating only locusts and wild honey. The people of the region came to him to be baptized in the Jordan River. When Jesus asked to be baptized, John proclaimed that he was not worthy of such a task and that Christ should baptize him. Christ insisted, however, and during the baptism the Holy Spirit descended and a voice from heaven proclaimed, “This is my beloved Son in whom I am well pleased” (Matthew 3:17). John got into trouble when he criticized King Herod’s marriage to Herodias, who had a child from her previous marriage to Herod’s brother. Herod’s stepdaughter, Salome, convinced him to arrest John and demanded his head on a silver platter. Granting her wish, Herod ordered John beheaded.  
This icon shows several scenes from John the Baptist’s life in a single frame. At the top left, John is depicted in the wilderness, surrounded by animals. He receives inspiration from God in the form of flames. At the bottom, John is seen baptizing followers in the Jordan River while more followers prepare for baptism or don the white clothes of the newly baptized. In the top right corner of the icon, people stream out from the city while members of the aristocracy look on from above. The three figures in the central arch could be King Herod, his wife and stepdaughter, all of whom were responsible for John’s martyrdom.
keywords: Saints; Religious iconography

en.name: The peace treaty of Bucharest
short_description: The peace treaty that ended the Russo-Ottoman war of 1806-1812 was signed by the representatives of Russia and the Ottoman Empire in Bucharest, the capital of Wallachia, on the 28 May 1812. Both Wallachia and Moldavia had been occupied by Russia during the war. According to the third article of the peace treaty the Russian army had to liberate Wallachia and the Moldavian territory on the right side of the Prut River. The fourth article stipulated that Russia annexed the territory situated on the left side of the Prut, which became the new border between the Ottoman and the Russian Empires. The new area incorporated into the Russian Empire was given the name Bessarabia, which had in the past designated southern Moldavia.

ar.name: طست من خليط النحاس
description: طست دائري له قاعدة مسطحة وحافة عريضة متجهة للخارج وتحتوي على ستة عشر بروزا مدببا يعطي الحوض شكله النجمي. بداخله في المركز نقش على شكل زهرة محاطة بشرائط زخرفية ملتفة حول نفسها على القاعدة المطعمة بنقوش من الخط الكوفي وزخارف تشبه أشعة الشمس.  على الحواف توجد كتابات على شكل شريط بكلمات مبهمة لا معنى لها في الأغلب.  الطست ليست عليه نقوش على السطح الخارجي.  تستخدم مثل هذه الطسوت لتخزين المياه المستخدمة للوضوء قبل أداء فريضة الصلاة.
dates: القرنين السادس-السابع الهجريين/ الثاني عشر-الثالث عشر الميلاديين
keywords: طست، وضوء

en.name: Copper alloy basin
description:
A round basin with a flat base and sides rising to an everted scalloped rim with 16 lobes.  
The interior is engraved with a central rosette surrounded by concentric decorative bands of alternating spirals against a dotted ground; *kufic* script inscriptions; sunray motifs; and, just below the rim, a band of pseudo-calligraphy. There is no decoration on the outside of this basin.  
This type of basin held water for use in daily ablutions prior to prayers.
keywords: Basin; Ablutions

ar.name: مصحف وحيد المجلد
description: الصفحة اليسرى الباقية من واجهة أمامية ذات صفحتين (الصفحة 1a) مصممة كدائرتين متداخلتين في إطار مضفر وكل منها تحتوي جزءا من الآية وعدد الأحرف وعلامات التنقيط / التشكيل. وهذا مستمد من التذهيب لأولى المصاحف بشكل طولاني ويشير بأن الانتقال من الشكل الشاقولي لم يفرض مباشرة قانونا قاطعا جديدا على التوضع. وتنتهي المخطوطة بجزء نهائي مضاعف مذهب التي يسود بها اللون الذهبي. والنموذج ، أيضا هنا ، يستند للدوائر المتداخلة. والنص منسوخ بالخط النسخي وذو عشرين سطرا في الصفحة. وترويسات السور مكتوبة بالكوفي الذهبي ذات سعيفات ذهبية في الهامش والتي تحوي في بعض الأحيان اسم المكان الذي أنزلت به السورة. والآيات الإفرادية غير معلّمة ولكن المجموعات المكونة من خمس آيات مبينة بشكل بيضوي والمجموعات من عشر آيات بشكل دائري.

en.name: Single-volume Qur’an
description:
The surviving left-hand folio of the double-page frontispiece (folio 1a) is designed as two overlapping circles in a braided frame, each containing part of the verse, letter and diacritical count. This derives from the illumination of early Qur’ans in oblong format and indicates that the transition to vertical format did not immediately bring a radical new layout. The manuscript ends with an illuminated double finispiece in which gold predominates. The pattern, here too, is based on overlapping circles.  
The text is copied in *naskhi*, with 20 lines to the page. *Sura* headings are in gold *kufic*, with a marginal gold palmette, which occasionally contains the name of the place where the *sura* was revealed. Individual verses are not marked, but groups of five verses are indicated by an oval and groups of ten by a circle.
type: Manuscript; Qur’an; ink on paper; *naskhi* script; *kufic* script
holder: Khalili Family Trust – Nasser D. Khalili Collection of Islamic Art

en.name: "How Rustam Found a Spring"
names: Folio from a Shahnama (Book of Kings) of Firdausi
description: The two miniatures 69.74.8 and 69.74.9 illustrate the first and second of Rustam's seven ordeals. The first depicts the frequently illustrated scene of Rustam's gallant horse Rakhsh killing a lion while the hero sleeps. The subject of the second miniature is, on the other hand, rarely depicted. Rustam and Rakhsh nearly die of heat and thirst in the desert before, with the help of divine providence, they find a spring. Rustam bathes and grooms his faithful steed by the water's edge, as seen here. The painter is very sympathetic to the closeness between the hero and his trustworthy Rakhsh.
place: Attributed to Northwestern Iran or Baghdad
materials: Ink, opaque watercolour, silver, and gold on paper
tags: Ink, opaque watercolour, silver, and gold on paper

en.name: *A market in Bucharest*
short_description: Wallachia and Moldavia's contacts with the Ottoman Empire also influenced the aspect of Romanian cities. For example, marketplaces, as known from 19th century paintings and lithographs, were similar to Turkish bazaars and represented, just like in the Ottoman Empire, the commercial centre of a city. The watercolor is part of an album with reproductions after 15 of Amedeo Preziosi’s paintings that depict scenes from Bucharest. Maltese painter Amedeo Preziosi met Carol of Hohenzollern, ruler of Romania, in Istanbul in 1866. Invited by the prince to come visit his country, Preziosi was in Romania between June-July 1868 and May-July 1869. He is the author of more than 250 works inspired by Romanian landscapes, cities and people.

en.name: House of Sultan Qaytbay in al-Razzaz
names: Door to the House of Qaytbay in al-Razzaz (option)
description: Built in the 9th/15th century, the only part that remains of Sultan Qaytbay’s house is the door, which while shorter due to its domestic purpose, maintains the traditional Mamluk-period style. It is crowned with a stalactite vault and tri-lobed arch, and has a stone bench on either side taking up the full width. The stone lintel, above which the Sultan’s emblem appears, bears a floral decoration in relief, and on the imposts a foundation text naming Sultan al-Ashraf Sha‘ban Abi al-Nasr Qaytbay.

es.name: Puerta de la casa de Qaytbay en al-Razzaz (opción)
description:
La casa del sultán Qaytbay fue construida en el siglo IX/XV y de ella solo se conserva la puerta, que consiste en la entrada  
típica de la época mameluca aunque menos alta, por tratarse del acceso a una casa. Coronada por un arco trilobulado y  
decorada con mocárabes, está flanqueada por dos bancos de piedra que ocupan todo el ancho. El dintel de piedra, sobre el cual aparece el emblema del sultán, presenta una decoración floral tallada en relieve, y en las impostas un texto fundacional menciona el nombre del sultán: al-Achraf Cha‘ban Abu al-Nasr Qaytbay.

fr.name: Porte de la maison de Qaytbay dans celle de al-Razzaz (option)
description: La maison du sultan Qaytbay fut construite au IXe/XVe siècle, et seule a survécu la porte, qui représente l’entrée typique de l’époque mamelouke, quoique moins haute s’agissant de l’accès à une maison. Couronné d’un arc trilobé et décoré de *mouqarnas*, il est flanqué de deux banquettes de pierre qui en occupent toute la largeur. Le linteau de pierre, au-dessus duquel figure l’emblème du sultan, présente une décoration florale sculptée en relief, tandis que dans les impostes un texte de fondation mentionne le nom du sultan, al-Achraf Cha‘ban Abi al-Nasr Qaytbay.

en.name: Daff
short_description: The *daff*, also known as the *rikk*, is a popular instrument similar to a tambourine. It is made of a round wooden frame, covered on one side with goat or fish skin. Pairs of metal discs are set into the frame to produce a jingling sound when the instrument is struck. It is used to set the rhythm in many traditional Arabic songs, particularly during purely instrumental performances.
holder: Lebanese National Higher Conservatory of Music
keywords: Music; Sound; Percussion; Rhythm

en.name: Coffee-making utensils
description: Traditional preparation involves roasting the green coffee beans over a fire in a pan with a long handle (*mahmas*). A pusher (*yad al-mahmas*) is used to move the beans back and forth in the pan. Once roasted on all sides, the black coffee beans are poured onto the cooling tray (*mubarrad*, at left in the photo). In the large, typically wooden or metal mortar (*mahbash, hawun*) the cooled coffee beans are crushed by using a pestle (*nijr, mudgag*). The physical effort required to do this produces a loud, sonorous noise. It is said that some coffee cooks employed unique beating rhythms.

en.name: *The Grand Mosque in Constanţa*
short_description: The Grand Mosque of Constanţa, the biggest in Romania, was built between 1910–1913 for the Muslim community of the city, on the initiative of king Carol I. It was erected on the place of a 19th century mosque, whose minbar (pulpit from where the imam delivers sermons) was preserved. The monument, a mixture of Byzantine-Egyptian and Romanian architectural elements, is the work of architect Victor Ştefănescu, who before designing it travelled to Istanbul to get acquainted with Islamic architecture. The mosque was inaugurated on 31 May 1913 in the presence of Romania’s king and queen and of Romanian and Ottoman officials. The envoy of sultan Abdul Hamid II brought a Persian rug for the mosque and awarded the orders of “Medjidie” and “Osmanieh” to Victor Ştefănescu and the city’s may.

en.name: Prayer rug (fragment)
description: Although less than half the size of the original rug, the fragment is still one of the most remarkable textiles of the Islamic art collection in the Museum. Following the latest research, the original rug was reconstructed based on several well-preserved details (see the virtual reconstruction of the original design, ill. 1a). The *mihrab*, an essential element of the mosque architecture represented on prayer rugs, has been replaced here with a triple arch reminiscent rather of a gateway or the cross section through a mosque; the dome over the centre arch in the original design supports this hypothesis. The coupled-column motif could be traced back to the architecture of Muslim Spain, and was apparently disseminated by Sephardic Jews. Similar columns, whose bases are rendered in linear perspective, feature on 16th-century Ottoman prayer rugs some of which were imperial court commissions produced in Istanbul; others, as is the case here, were made in Cairo, where the tradition of Mamluk workshops continued long after the Ottoman conquest (1517). The asymmetrical knot is characteristic of Mamluk carpets, whereas the decorative repertoire is typical of Ottoman art. The original rug may have served as a prototype for “Transylvanian” coupled-column carpets dating back to the 17th and 18th centuries, which only comes to highlight the historical significance of this fragment.
holder: The National Museum of Art of Romania
keywords: prayer rug; Ottoman Cairo rug; court rug
partner: The National Museum of Art of Romania

en.name: Castle
description: Its foundation dates back to the period of the Seignory of Malcovenant, the French who came after Count Ruggero. Roberto, the first Baron of Racalmuto, built the castle as his personal residence. The building was enlarged in 1181 by the Barresi family who governed Racalmuto from 1134 and held it for the whole time as long as the Dynasty of the Altavillas. In 1296, Federico II Chiaramonte restored the castle, damaged by an earthquake in 1282, and enlarged it. Finally, in 1929 the castle was greatly transformed in order to receive the Convent of Dominican Sisters. The planimetric structure is of an irregular pentagonal shape. From the main front, across a covered communication trench, there is access to the internal courtyard, around which stands a vast development where there are still some identifiable remains of the original structure, such as the portal now included in the walls of the courtyard.

es.name: Castillo
description:
Su fundación se remonta al periodo del señorío de los Malcovenant, franceses del séquito del conde Ruggero. El Castillo fue construido por Roberto, primer barón de Racalmuto, en 1087, como morada propia. El edificio fue ampliado después, en 1181, por la familia Barresi, que gobernaba Racalmuto desde 1134 y fue propietaria de la localidad durante todo el tiempo de la dinastía normanda de los Altavilla. En 1296, Federico II Chiaramonte restauró el Castillo, dañado en los motines de 1282, y posteriormente lo amplió. Finalmente, en 1929, la fortaleza sufrió una profunda reforma para poder albergar el convento de las monjas dominicas.  
La planta es de forma pentagonal irregular. Desde el frente principal, a través de un pasaje, se tiene acceso al patio interior, en torno al cual se organiza el vasto conjunto edilicio en que se aprecian aún restos de las estructuras originales, como la puerta hoy integrada en el paramento mural del patio.

en.name: Chemin de fer, Postcard, Alep (Aleppo Railway Station)
description: This composite postcard presents Aleppo’s earlier railway complex, generally identified as Damascus Station, together with a separate building labelled Pavillon militaire. Located in the Jamiliyeh district of Aleppo, the station served the French-operated railway Damas, Hama et Prolongements (D.H.P.), linking Aleppo southward through Hama and Homs with Damascus. The Hama–Aleppo extension entered service in 1906. The upper image shows a restrained two-storey masonry station with a long covered platform, regularly spaced windows and numerous chimneys, reflecting its combined passenger, administrative and possibly staff functions. The lower image records the military pavilion, with a raised entrance, deep tiled roofs and an ornamental timber porch distinguish it from the station building.
keywords: Syria; Aleppo; Damascus; Transport; Communication

cs.name: Pohled na klášter
description: Obraz představuje klášter s kostelem na předměstí Brna a náves s kostelíkem sv. Víta, obnovené po švédském vyplenění. Ke kostelu přiléhají cely, z nichž každou obýval vždy jeden otec. U cely byla zahrádka vymezená zdí na výšku dvou podlaží, která znemožňovala komunikaci sousedů (součást askeze) a zaručovala naprosté soukromí. V cele byla místnost na spaní, na studium, modlitbu a dílna. Cely byly spojeny křížovou chodbou uzavírající klauzurní dvůr.

en.name: View of the Monastery
description: The picture shows the monastery and church on the outskirts of Brno, and a village green with the small Church of St. Vitus restored after the ravages of the Swedish campaign. The church is adjoined by cells where one church father lived in each. Outside the cells were gardens demarcated by a two-storey-high wall that made the communication between neighbouring monks impossible (part of their asceticism), and thus guaranteed absolute privacy. The cells contained a room for sleeping, studying and praying and a workshop. These areas were connected by a cloister that closed off the courtyard of reclusion.

en.name: *Susanna and the Old Men*
description:
The painting, signed and dated, was acquired by Marcantonio IV Borghese in 1783 along with other works of the Flemish school. No details are known about the commissioning of the canvas, which, like the Rubens' example (inv.277), handles a subject common to painting of the Counter-Reformation. The account is taken from the Old Testament, specifically the Book of the Prophet Daniel (13, 1–64), and illustrates well the defeat of deception, expressed by the two old men – shown with lustful eyes and faces – and the victory of truth, represented by the naked Susanna.  
Van Honthorst, known in Italy as Gherardo delle Notti, manages to transmit the feelings of surprise, indignation and shame in the Biblical heroine by the fountain, through her open mouth and terrified look. The study of mood is related to experimentation of Gian Lorenzo Bernini and Guido Reni, who rendered it first in marble and then on canvas.  
Although the composition follows a diagonal arrangement, possibly inspired by Emilian painting that he encountered on his long trip to Italy in the 1620s, the canvas belongs to the final productive phase of the artist. He was better known as a painter of “genre scenes” particularly renowned for the extraordinary lighting effects inspired by the Caravaggesque school of Bartolomeo Manfredi, which he frequented when in Rome. Despite connections to a secular theme and culture, van Honthorst, the leader of the Dutch Caravaggists, captures the instrument of Divine Will in the figure of Susanna, who is entirely surrounded by light, and who triumphs only after suffering cruel injustices.

The subject is connected to the representation of the emotions according to the experimentation of Bernini and Reni among others. The theme of the painting relates to the concept of deception being defeated by divine truth.
artist: Gerrit van Honthorst (also known as Gherardo delle Notti )
keywords: Symbol; Christian themes; Counter-Reformation; Bernini; Guido Reni; Rubens; Flemish school; Emilian influence; genre scene; Dutch Caravaggists

it.name: *Susanna e i vecchioni*
description: Il dipinto, firmato e datato, è stato acquistato nel 1783 da Marcantonio IV Borghese, insieme ad altre opere di scuola fiamminga. Non sono note le vicende legate alla committenza della tela che, come quella di Rubens (inv. 277), raffigura un tema usuale nella pittura della Controriforma. Il racconto è tratto dall'Antico Testamento, dal Libro del Profeta Daniele (13, 1-64), e bene illustra la sconfitta della menzogna, espressa nei due vecchioni -  raffigurati con lo sguardo e l'espressione concupiscente - , e la vittoria della verità rappresentata  dalla nuda Susanna. Van Honthorst, noto in Italia come Gherardo delle Notti, è riuscito a trasmettere la sensazione di sorpresa, di sdegno e di vergogna dell'eroina biblica, sorpresa in piedi nella fontana, tramite la bocca aperta e lo sguardo  atterrito. Lo studio degli 'stati d'animo' è legato alle ricerche barocche di Gian Lorenzo Bernini e di Guido Reni, che li hanno resi il primo nel marmo, l'altro sulle tele. La composizione segue una direttrice diagonale -  ispirata forse dalla pittura  emiliana conosciuta nell'importante soggiorno italiano degli anni '20 del '600  - anche se La tela appartiene alla produzione finale dell'artista, più noto come pittore di 'scene di genere', e soprattutto noto per gli straordinari effetti luministici ispirati dalla cerchia caravaggesca di Bartolomeo Manfredi, frequentato a Roma. Caposcuola dei caravaggisti olandesi, van Honthorst pur legato a temi e a una cultura profani, ha colto nella figura di Susanna, completamente avvolta dalla luce, lo strumento della volontà divina, che arriva al trionfo solo dopo aver subito crudeli ingiustizie.

Il soggetto è collegato alla rappresentazione delle emozioni, tra gli altri già sperimentata da Bernini  e Reni. Il tema del dipinto si riferisce al concetto di inganno che viene sconfitto dalla verità divina.
keywords: Simbolo; tematiche cristiane; Controriforma; Bernini;Guido Reni; Rubens; scuola fiamminga; influenza emiliana; scena di genere; caravaggisti olandesi

en.name: Khassaki Sultan Complex
description:
It took four years to complete the complex (959/1552–963/1556), making it the largest charitable institution in the whole city.  
The complex is vast and has two entrances. The northern one lies on Aqabat al-Takiyya, while the southern one lies on Aqabat al-Saraya. In the local language, *al-Takiyya* means “*the place where food is served free of charge*”. *Al-Saraya*, on the other hand, means the seat of the governor or the *wali* and is named after the Ottoman mayor’s residence prior to the British Mandate.  
The complex is attributed to Roxelane, the wife of the Ottoman Sultan Sulayman the Magnificent (926/1520–974/1566), known as Haseki Hürrem (the cheerful, good-humoured one). Ottoman sources refer to her as Khassaki Sultan, in other words the Sultan’s favourite and beloved. Khassaki Sultan endowed generous *waqf*s on her social and charitable project to guarantee the perpetuation of its activities. The revenues of 30 towns and villages in Palestine and other places went into its budget. She added to them a *waqf* of four more villages donated by Sultan Sulayman to support her *waqf* after her death. These villages were located in different regions in Gaza, Nablus, Jerusalem, Sidon and Tripoli.  
The complex consisted of four different sections, some of which have survived: A large *caravanserai* to accommodate travellers and traders. It consists of a large entrance that leads to a corridor with rooms on both sides. The corridor ends in an open courtyard, which is surrounded by more corridors that form the *caravanserai*s. These parts can be seen today from the southern entrance, though some of their functions have changed.  
A mosque for prayer, reciting the Qur’an and praying for the benefactor. It has many domes and arches. However, its exact location is unknown and it is presumed that part of it was demolished and that the current student refectory was built over it.  
A *ribat*55 rooms to house *sufis*, the poor and visitors. Like the mosque, its location is also unknown today. It seems that most of the rooms have been demolished and changed into other utilities, although it was probably east of the southern entrance where the printing shop currently stands.  
A large kitchen, a bakery, a mill, many storage rooms and a fountain to provide water to the residence have all survived and can be seen after entering the courtyard from the northern gate and turning east via some stairs. The kitchen continues to provide delicious soups every morning plus meat and rice during Ramadan and every Tuesday, even though the *ribat*’s *waqf* ceased long ago.  
This active institution was administered by a number of senior Ottoman employees. The Inspector was posted from Istanbul and was helped by approximately 50 members of staff, each having a detailed job description allocated to him in the *waqf*. Among the employees were a person who washed the cups, another who picked the rice, two chefs and their three assistants, a renovator, and a maintenance person who would look after the building. In addition to the running costs, the total annual wage bill was approximately 795.5 silver dirhams.

de.name: Deckenfresko: *Verherrlichung Mariens*
description: Im Chorfresko ist ein reiner Heiligenhimmel dargestellt, der ohne Architekturversatzstücke oder Landschaft auskommt. Die Komposition um die verehrte Maria inmitten der vierzehn Nothelfer besteht aus Personengruppen, die weniger der Kreisform folgen als auf den Wolken wie auf Theaterrängen angeordnet sind. Die irdische Sphäre der westlichen beiden Fresken ist hier verlassen, die Herrlichkeit des Himmels kommt in hellen, duftigen Farben zum Ausdruck.

en.name: Ceiling fresco: *Glorification of Mary*
description: The choir fresco depicts a pristine Heaven of the Saints devoid of architectural set pieces or landscapes. The composition of the venerated Mary in the midst of the Fourteen Holy Helpers consists of groups of figures arranged on the clouds like spectators on the tiers of a theatre, as opposed to tracing a circular form. Here we have left the earthly sphere of the two western frescos and the glory of heaven is expressed in bright, airy colours.

ar.name: قصر المنار (برج محصّن).
description:
يشكل البرج المحصن (المنار) جزءاً من مجمع بأكمله يُعرف بالقصر الذي يحمل الاسم نفسه (قصر المنار)، والذي قد تساعد التنقيبات الأثرية التي يتعين استكمالها، في استجلاء المعلومات عن هذا القصر( القلعة) وعن تسلسل تواريخه المتعلّقة بمجمل قلعة بني حماد، المدينة المحصنة التي تم إنشاؤها على مرتفعات هدنة في أوج ازدهارهم.  
يتخذ البرج المحصن، الذي شيد على حافة جرف صخري يشرف على وادي فرج، شكل برج إشارة قائم على مساحة مربعة، يبلغ ضلعها زهاء العشرين مترا. الواجهات مجوفة على مدى ارتفاعها بمشاكٍ مصمتة ذات قاعدة نصف دائرية، ومغطاة بقبب نصفية على شكل محارة. ويتصدر الواجهات التي تقابل الوادي بناءٌ متقدّم، يبلغ عمقه 1.50 متر، في حين، يخترقُ الجدارَ الشرقيَّ مَرمَيان. ويؤدي انحدار خفيف يدور حول نواة مركزيّة ( تبلغ عشرة أمتار عرضاً) فوق قبو برميلي إلى الأسطح. وقد أُعيد تشكيلُ القاعتين المتراكبتين، ويتأتى التصميم الصليبي الشكل للقاعة العلوية بواسطة تجاويف على شكل مشاكٍ ذات خلفيات مسطحة يعلوها في كل واجهة عقد حدوي. وفي الزوايا، تفصح بقايا حنيات ركنية عن القبة التي كانت تغطي هذه القاعة.

هذا البرج هو كل ماتبقى من قصر المنار المشيد داخل مدينة بني حماد المحصنة. ترتفع البناية التي شيدت فوق منحدر صخري يشرف على وادي فرج فوق تصميم مربع، يصل ضلعه إلى حولي 20 متر. وقد كانت واجهاته مجوفة بمشاكي مصمتة؛ وكان البرج محميا من جهة الوادي بخندق. وفي الشرق، جرى اختراق الجدار بمرميين؛ بينما أعيد في الداخل تشكيل قاعتين متراكبتين. وتمت تهيئة انحدار خفيف فوق قبو نصف أسطواني يدور حول محور مركزي ليؤدي إلى السطوح.
keywords: بنو حمّاد؛ زخرفة تصويرية؛ زخرفة زهريّة؛ زخرفة هندسيّة؛ عمارة بلاطية / عمارة أميرية / عمارة قصرية؛ عمارة عسكريّة؛ ماء.
tags: عمارة بلاطية / عمارة أميرية / عمارة قصرية

en.name: Qasr al-Manar (Fortress of the Keep).
description:
The keep (*manar*) forms part of a complex known as the Qasr al-Manar. Excavations still need to be undertaken to shed light on this *qasr* (fortress) and on its chronology in relation to the site of Qal'at Bani Hammad, the fortified town that was founded by the Hammadids on the Hodna hills at the height of their prosperity.  
Built on the edge of the cliff that descends into the Oued Fradj, the keep takes the form of a raised signal tower on a square plan whose sides have an approximate length of 20 metres. The façades have been indented, from top to bottom, with blind niches that have semi-circular platforms and are covered by scalloped half-domes. The façades facing the *oued* are preceded by a built projection 1.5 m in depth. Two loopholes pierce the eastern wall. Inside, encircling a central area that measures 10 m on each side, a gentle slope on barrel vaults leads onto the terraces. Two rooms, one above the other, could have been reconstructed. The cruciform layout of the room above was achieved by hollowing out niches with flat backs, surmounted on each side by a horseshoe arch. The remains of pendentives in each of the corners indicate the existence of the dome that would have once covered this room.

The keep is all that remains of Qasr al-Manar, which was erected in the fortified town of Qal'at Bani Hammad. Built on a cliff overlooking the Oued Fradj, it rises from a square base with sides some 20m long. Its side are punctuated with blind niches. It was protected on the wadi side by a ditch, and the eastern wall includes two arrow loops. Inside, two superposed rooms have been rebuilt and a barrel-vaulted passageway slopes gently around a central axis to the terraces.
keywords: Military architecture; palatine architecture; water; geometric decoration; floral decoration; figurative decoration; Hammadids

es.name: Palacio de la Torre (Qasr al-Manar).
description:
La torre era la parte principal del palacio al que da nombre, cuyas excavaciones, aún pendientes, podrían aclararnos la configuración de este *qasr* y su cronología con respecto al conjunto de la Qalaa de los Banu Hammad, la ciudad fortificada que fundaron los hammadíes en los montes Hodna en el apogeo de la dinastía.  
Edificada en el borde del acantilado que domina el río Fredj, esta torre se asemeja a una torre de señales o atalaya, con una planta cuadrada de unos 20 m de lado. Las fachadas muestran, en toda su altura, nichos ciegos con base semicircular y cubiertos con medias cúpulas en forma de concha. Las fachadas sur y este, frente al río, presentan cuerpos de 1,50 m de profundidad que se proyectan al exterior. El de la fachada oriental dispone de dos troneras accesibles desde una pequeña habitación encajada en el espesor del muro. En el núcleo central (de 10 m de lado) se ubican dos salas superpuestas y enlazadas por una rampa sostenida por bóvedas de cañón, que desemboca en la terraza. La primera, de forma cuadrada y situada en el sótano, está cubierta por una bóveda y puede haber tenido la función de cárcel o almacén. A la segunda sala se accede directamente desde el exterior, por una puerta situada en la fachada oeste de la torre. Superpuesta a la primera, presenta una planta cruciforme configurada por los rehundimientos situados en medio de cada uno de los lados de 5 m de ancho, que muestran un fondo plano rematado con un arco de herradura. En los ángulos, restos de pechinas revelan que la cubierta estaba constituida por una cúpula sostenida por un tambor octogonal o cilíndrico, en el que puede haber habido una serie de ventanas para la iluminación.

Esta torre (*manar*) es lo que queda del Qasr al-Manar, construido en la ciudad fortificada de los Banu Hammad. Edificada sobre el acantilado que domina el río Fredj, se levanta sobre una planta cuadrada de unos 20 m de lado y sus fachadas presentan, en toda su altura, nichos ciegos. Por el lado del río estaba protegida con un foso. En el este, el muro dispone de dos troneras. En el núcleo central se ubican dos salas superpuestas y comunicadas por una rampa, sostenida por bóvedas de cañón, que desemboca en la terraza.
keywords: Arquitectura militar; arquitectura palatina; agua; decoración geométrica; decoración floral; decoración figurativa; hammadíes

fr.name: Qasr al-Manar (donjon).
description:
Le donjon (*manar*) fait partie de tout un ensemble, le Qasr du même nom (Qasr al-Manar), dont les fouilles, qui restent à faire, pourraient nous éclairer sur ce *qasr* (forteresse) et sur sa chronologie relative par rapport à l'ensemble de la *qalaa* des Beni Hammad, la ville fortifiée qu'ils fondèrent sur les monts Hodna à l'apogée de leur prospérité.  
  
Bâti au bord de la falaise qui surplombe l'oued Fredj, le donjon se présente sous la forme d'une tour à signaux élevée sur un plan carré d'environ 20 mètres de côté. Les façades sont creusées, sur toute leur hauteur, de niches aveugles à base semi-circulaire et couvertes par des demi-coupoles en coquille. Les façades, qui font face à l'oued, sont précédées d'un avant-corps de 1,50 m de profondeur. Le mur oriental est percé de deux meurtrières. à l'intérieur, tournant autour d'un noyau central (de 10 m de côté), une pente douce sur voûte en berceau conduit aux terrasses. Deux salles superposées ont pu être reconstituées. Le plan cruciforme de la salle supérieure était obtenu par des défoncements en forme de niches à fond plat surmontées sur chaque face d'un arc en fer à cheval. Aux angles, des vestiges de trompes d'angle annoncent la coupole qui couvrait cette salle.

Le donjon est ce qui reste de Qasr al-Manar, édifié dans la ville fortifiée des Beni Hammad. Bâti sur une falaise dominant l'oued Fredj, il s'élève sur un plan carré d'environ vingt mètres de côté. Ses façades étaient creusées de niches aveugles. Il était protégé du côté de l'oued par un fossé. à l'est, le mur est percé de deux meurtrières. à l'intérieur, deux salles superposées ont été reconstituées ; une pente douce sur voûte en berceau tournant autour d'un axe central donnait accès aux terrasses.
keywords: architecture militaire ; architecture palatine ; eau ; décoration géométrique ; décoration florale ; décoration figurative ; Hammadides

cs.name: Zázrak Panny Marie Sněžné
description:
Zasvěcení kostela se váže k příběhu ze života zakladatele řádu: Sv. Ignác  
z Loyoly sloužil svou první mši v římském kostele P. Marie Sněžné (Sta Maria Maggiore). Scéna ilustuje legendu o zažehnání morové epidemie v Římě r. 590: papež Řehoř Veliký vede procesí k bazilice a s prosbou o pomoc se obrací  
k zázračnému obrazu Madony. Při vyzdvižení obrazu se nad Andělským hradem objevil anděl, zasunul meč do pochvy a morová rána ustoupila.  
V presbytáři navazuje výjev Apoteóza P. Marie, královny nebes. Plastickou dekoraci vytvořil podle malířových pokynů italský, v Olomouci usedlý štukatér  
A. Ricca. Oltářní obrazy zasílal Harringer později z Vídně.

en.name: Miracle of the Virgin Mary of the Snows
description:
The dedication of the church is associated with a story from the life of St. Ignatius of Loyola, the founder of the Jesuit order, who held his first service in the Sta. Maria Maggiore Church (Church of the Virgin Mary of the Snows), in Rome. The scene illustrates a plague epidemic averted from Rome in 590: Pope Gregory the Great leads a procession to the basilica, praying to the miraculous picture of the Madonna. When the picture was lifted an angel appeared above Saint Angelo Castle; put his sword in its sheath, and the plague subsided.  
The church presbytery contains a scene of the Apotheosis of the Virgin Mary, Queen of Heaven. The relief decoration was created by the Italian stucco artist, A. Ricci, to the designs of K. J. Harringer, who sent the altarpieces to Olomouc from Vienna.

cs.name: Nástropní malba
description: Klenbu jednolodní stavby otevírá do nebeské sféry monumentální freska s výjevy ze života sv. Janů. Iluzivní architektura plynule přechází ve skutečné pilastry a štukovou výzdobu. Hlavní pole představuje Narození sv. Jana Křtitele, klenbu presbytáře odděleného pasem ve funkci triumfálního oblouku znamení na nebi podle Zjevení sv. Jana.

en.name: Minorite Church of Saints John and Loreto, Brno
description: The vault of the single-nave building opens onto a celestial sphere with a monumental fresco and scenes from the lives of the Saints John and Loreto. The illusionary architecture graduates into genuine pilasters and stucco decoration. The main section depicts the Birth of St. John the Baptist, while the presbytery vault, separated by a “triumphal arch”, features the signs in the sky described in the Revelation of St. John.
place: Minorite Church of Saints John and Loreto, Brno

en.name: Memorial of Sultan Husayn Kamil’s visit to the Islamic Arts Museum
short_description: The Islamic Arts Museum in Cairo is the biggest Islamic museum in the world, and it encompasses a wide collection of Islamic arts from India, China, the Arab Peninsula, the Levant, Egypt, North Africa and Andalusia. Sultan Husayn Kamil’s visit to the Museum in 1916 is considered one of the more important visits received by the Museum.
keywords: Sultan Hussein Kamel; Arabian Archeology Museum; Islamic Arts Museum

en.name: *Kama’ Al Sahra* (Desert truffles)
description: *Kama’ Al Sahra* (desert truffle, *Tirmania nivea*) are subterranean fungi rather than true truffles. They are a delicacy eaten on their own or prepared in traditional dishes. People collect the fungi soon after rainfall in spring. *Kama' Al Sahra* grows close to *Ragroog* (rock rose, *Hellanthemum lippil*) bushes, which is perhaps how people locate the hidden truffles.
dates: Hegira mid 14th century / AD mid 20th century
keywords: desert truffles; truffleas; desert

ar.name: سلسلة نامة (سلسلة النسب)
description: هذه الصفحات تنتمي لواحدة من مجموعة مخطوطات منتجة في أواخر القرن السادس عشر وبداية القرن السابع عشر ، ربما في بغداد ، لسادة من الأتراك العثمانيين. وهذه المخطوطات تصنف عموما كمخطوطات في علم الأنساب ( بالرغم من أنها ليست حصريا في مثل هذا الموضوع)  وهي معروفة باسم سلسلة – نامة. وهي تبدأ عادة بقصة النبي محمد ويليها تاريخ العالم منذ آدم إلى السلطان العثماني الحاكم وهي معززة بصور توضيحية ذات بورتريهات عديدة وصغيرة تشبه الرصائع للأنبياء والملوك. وكل شخص مصور معرّف بنقش كتابي. والمخطوطة تفتتح بواجهة مصورة.
keywords: رسم توضيحي ، لوحة منمنمة ، تخطيط ، نص مكتوب ، تذهيب
tags: رسم توضيحي ، لوحة منمنمة ، تخطيط ، نص مكتوب ، تذهيب

en.name: *Silsila-nama* (‘Genealogy’)
description: These folios belong to one of a small group of manuscripts produced in the late sixteenth and early seventeenth centuries, probably in Baghdad, for Ottoman Turkish patrons. These manuscripts are generally classed as genealogies (though they in fact do not function strictly as such) and are known by the name *silsila-nama*. They usually begin with an account of the Prophet Muhammad, followed by a history of the world from Adam to the reigning Ottoman sultan, and are illustrated with numerous small, medallion-like portraits of prophets and kings. Each individual depicted is identified by an inscription. The manuscript opens with an illuminated frontispiece.
keywords: illustration; miniature painting; calligraphy; script; illumination
materials: Coloured pigments and gold on paper
tags: Coloured pigments and gold on paper

en.name: Mihrişah Sultan Fountain
description: Westernisation brought about a change of form and decoration for fountains, which contributed to the urban structure of Istanbul.

en.name: *Caryatids* candlesticks
description: Candlesticks of pressed and patined clear glass in the form of caryatids. Classical inspiration is a recurrent motif in the production of Lalique glassmaking.

ar.name: جامع سيدي الحلوي.
description: قاعة الصلاة مماثلة لتلك المتواجدة في سيدي بو مدين، والتي يتم الدخول إليها من أبواب جانبية أيضاً. تضم هذه القاعة خمس بلاطات متعامدة مع حائط "القبلة". تَحملُ ست عشرة دعامة وثماني أعمدة، مصنوعة من عقيق يمان (الجزع) مدهش ذو عروق ورديّة، جُلبتْ من قصر النصر في المنصورة، عقوداً منكسرة متجاوزة. وبُنيت الأسقف من خشب الأرز المنحوت المجمّع بشكل ظاهر، وزُخرفَ قسمٌ كبيرٌ من الجدران والعقود بالجبس، وبشكل خاص على مستوى الأروقة المتاخمة للصحن حيث الزخرفة شديدة البساطة، ويصل ارتفاعها إلى 1.20 متر، وتعلوها أفاريز جميلة جداً عليها نقائش كتابيّة بالخط الكوفي. يتخذ "المحراب" شكل ثماني الأضلاع، ويحتوي على قبيبة مزيّنة بالمقرنصات وألواح مستطيلة. فَقَدَ إطارُه كل زخرفته ويستند على عمودين مصنوعين كذلك من نفس الجزع المستعمل في قاعة الصلاة. تحمل تيجانُ الأعمدةِ نقائشَ كتابيّةً، تخص تلك المتواجدة على التاج الأيمن الوليَّ الذي أُقيم له الجامع، وتخص الأخرى المتواجدة على التاج الأيسر الأمير الذي أمر ببنائه. تتألف المئذنة رباعية الزوايا التي يصل ارتفاعها إلى 25 متر من قسمين: البرج والقبة القنديلية، وتعتبر قطعة معمارية بارزة. وبما أن قاعدتها مكشوفة، فيتبين أن زخارف الواجهات تمتد إلى مستوى أدنى من حافة سطح المسجد. يحيط بالصحن، الذي تبلغ مساحته حوالي 10 × 10 أمتار، رواق من الشرق والغرب. الميضأة عبارة عن مربع ذو سبع مقصورات وحوضين، ومنفصلة عن الجامع بشارع، وتقع قبالة المئذنة حيث تؤدي إليها دَوْرةٌ مكونة من تسع درجات. الميضأة مغطاة بقبة مرئية من الخارج.

يشتملُ هذا المسجد على قاعة للصلاة ذات خمس بلاطات محاطة بأعمدة من عقيق اليمان وبدعامات تسندُ عقودا منكسرة ومتجاوزة. شُيدت السقوف من خشب الأرز؛ وعلى الدعامات والجدران، تغتني الزخرفة الجصية، البسيطة في الجزء السفلي، بأفاريز مزينة بنقائش كوفية في الجزء العلوي. وتعلو مدخلَ المحراب قبةٌ مقرنصة، ترتكز على عمودين من عقيق اليمان، تحملُ تيجانهما نقائش كتابية. وتقدم المنارة ذات القاعدة المربعة الزوايا واجهات مزخرفة وقبة قنديلية.
dynasty: الفترة المرينية، 592 ـ 956 هجري / 1196 ـ 1549 ميلادي.
keywords: جامع ؛عمارة دينية؛ ماء.

en.name: Sidi al-Haloui Mosque.
description: The prayer hall is identical to that of Sidi Boumadyan, which one also accesses through side doors. It features five *balatat* (naves) that are perpendicular to the *qibla* wall. Sixteen pillars and eight columns, made of an attractive pink-veined onyx that came from the Palace of the Victory of Mansura, support semi-circular pointed arches. The ceilings are made of carved cedarwood with visible joints. A large area of the walls and arches are decorated in plaster, noticeably at the level of the *riwaq* (galleries) surrounding the *sahn* (courtyard), where the very simple decoration, up to a height of 1.2 m, is crowned by beautiful friezes with *kufic* inscriptions. The *mihrab* is hexagonal in shape and features a small *muqarnas* (stalactite) cupola and rectangular panelling. The frame has completely lost its ornamentation, and rests on two columns made of the same onyx as those in the prayer hall. The capitals feature inscriptions: the ones on the right-hand capital refer to the saint to whom the mosque is consecrated; those on the left one refer to the prince who built it. The quadrangular minaret, 25 m high, consists of two parts – the tower and the lantern – and is a remarkable piece of architecture. Once its base had been cleared, the decoration on its façades could be seen to extend below the edge of the mosque's roof. The *sahn*, approximately 10 m x 10 m, is bordered by a *riwaq* to the east and to the west. The ablutions hall, a square with seven boxes and two basins, is separated from the mosque by a street, located opposite the minaret. A flight of nine steps leads up to it. The ablutions hall is covered by a dome that can be seen from the outside.

This mosque has a five-nave prayer room lined with onyx columns and pillars bearing pointed horseshoe arches. The ceilings are made of cedarwood. The plasterwork decoration on the pillars and walls is plain at the bottom and enhanced with friezes with *kufic* inscriptions higher up. The opening to the *mihrab*, crowned with a *muqarnas* (stalactite) dome, rests on two onyx columns whose capitals are decorated with inscriptions. The façades of the square-plan minaret are decorated and it has a lantern.
keywords: Religious architecture; water; mosque

es.name: Mezquita de Sidi al-Halwi.
description: La sala de oración es idéntica a la de Sidi Bumadian, que también dispone de puertas laterales. Consta de cinco naves perpendiculares al muro de la *qibla*. Dieciséis pilares y ocho columnas de ónice venado de color rosa, procedentes del Palacio de la Victoria de al-Mansura, sostienen los arcos de herradura apuntados. Los techos son de madera de cedro esculpido, cuya trabazón es visible. Gran parte de los muros y de los arcos están decorados en estuco, particularmente a la altura de las galerías que rodean el patio, donde la decoración, muy sencilla y de 1,20 m de altura, está rematada por bonitos frisos con inscripciones cúficas. El *mihrab* es de forma hexagonal y consta de una pequeña cúpula de mocárabes y unos paneles rectangulares. El alfiz ha perdido toda su decoración y el arco descansa sobre dos columnas del mismo tipo de ónice que el de las columnas de la sala de oración. Los capiteles incluyen inscripciones: en el de la derecha, se refieren al santo a quien está dedicada la mezquita; en el de la izquierda, al príncipe que la mandó edificar. El alminar cuadrangular, de una altura de 25 m, se compone de dos partes –la torre y la linterna– y es considerado una joya de la arquitectura de su época. Al tener su base despejada, la decoración de sus fachadas se prolonga por debajo de la altura de la techumbre de la mezquita. El *sahn* (patio), de unos 10 x 10 m, está flanqueado por galerías en los lados este y oste. La sala de abluciones, un cuadrado de siete compartimentos y dos pilas, está separada de la mezquita por una calle, frente al alminar. Se accede a ella por nueve escalones. Está cubierta por una cúpula que se distingue desde el exterior.

Esta mezquita incluye una sala de oración con cinco naves, constituidas con columnas de ónice y pilares que sostienen arcos de herradura apuntados. Los techos son de madera de cedro. Sobre los arcos y los muros, la decoración en yeso, sencilla en la parte inferior, se enriquece de frisos con inscripciones cúficas en la parte superior. El *mihrab*, de forma hexagonal, está coronado por una cúpula de mocárabes, y el arco de entrada descansa sobre dos columnas de ónice cuyos capiteles lucen inscripciones. El alminar, de base cuadrangular, presenta fachadas decoradas y una linterna.
keywords: Arquitectura religiosa; agua; mezquita

fr.name: Mosquée Sidi el-Haloui.
description: La salle de prière est identique à celle de Sidi Boumediène, à laquelle on accède aussi par des portes latérales. Elle comporte cinq *balatat* (nefs) perpendiculaires au mur de *qibla*. Seize piliers et huit colonnes d'un admirable onyx veiné de rose, provenant du palais de la Victoire de Mansourah, supportent les arcs brisés outrepassés. Les plafonds sont en bois de cèdre sculpté à assemblage apparent. Une grande partie des murs et des arcs sont décorés en plâtre, ceci notamment au niveau des *riwaq* (galeries) bordant le *sahn* (cour)où le décor, très simple, haut de 1,20 m, est surmonté de très belles frises avec des inscriptions coufiques. Le *mihrab* est de forme hexagonale et comporte une coupolette à stalactites et des panneaux rectangulaires. L'encadrement a perdu toute décoration et repose sur deux colonnes du même onyx que celui de la salle de prière. Les chapiteaux comportent des inscriptions : sur celui de droite, elles concernent le saint auquel est consacrée la mosquée ; sur celui de gauche, le prince qui la fit édifier. Le minaret quadrangulaire, d'une hauteur de 25 mètres, se compose de deux parties – la tour et le lanternon –, et passe pour un morceau d'architecture remarquable. Sa base étant dégagée, la décoration de ses façades se prolonge plus bas que le bord de la toiture de la mosquée. Le *sahn*, d'environ 10 x 10 m, est bordé d'un *riwaq* à l'est et à l'ouest. La salle d'ablutions, un carré de 7 loges et de 2 bassins, se trouve séparée de la mosquée par une rue, en face du minaret. Une volée de 9 marches y conduit. La salle d'ablutions est couverte d'une coupole visible de l'extérieur.

Cette mosquée comporte une salle de prière à cinq nefs bordées de colonnes d'onyx et de piliers soutenant des arcs brisés outrepassés. Les plafonds sont en bois de cèdre. Sur les piliers et les murs, le décor en plâtre, simple dans la partie inférieure, s'enrichit de frises à inscriptions coufiques dans la partie supérieure. L'entrée du *mihrab* surmonté d'une coupole à stalactites repose sur deux colonnettes en onyx dont les chapiteaux portent des inscriptions. Le minaret à base quadrangulaire présente des façades décorées et un lanternon.
keywords: architecture religieuse ; eau ; mosquée

cs.name: Sál předků
description: Kancléř Václav Antonín dokončil úpravu bývalé jídelny s nástropní malbou Bohu na Olympu na tzv. Sál předků, kde umístil portréty svých rodičů, prarodičů a své manželky v nadživotní velikosti. Sál je propojen s oválným tzv. Historickým sálem s iluzivně malovanou architekturou, v němž bylo po bitvě u Slavkova podepsáno příměří mezi Rakouskem a Francií. Lanzani, žák C. Marraty, pracoval pro Habsburky a vídeňskou šlechtu.

en.name: Hall of the Ancestors
description:
Chancellor Václav Antonín completed reconstruction of a former garden room with a ceiling painting of the Gods on Mount Olympus and displayed larger-than-life portraits of his parents, grandparents and his wife.  
The Hall of the Ancestors is connected to the oval Historical Hall by illusionary painted architecture. It was here that the truce between Austria and France was signed after the Battle of Austerlitz.

en.name: Mohamed V Mausoleum
description:
Inside the enclosure of what was the Great Mosque, opposite the Hassan Tower, is the Mohamed V Mausoleum, which keeps alive the memory of the sovereign (1927–1961) who regained his country’s independence. This monument, built between 1961 and 1969, draws its inspiration from traditional royal *necropoli*. Placed on a 3.5 m.-high plinth, it is sheltered by a pyramidal green-tiled roof. One can access the funeral room in which Mohamed V’s tomb is located via a “gallery-balcony” ; his mortal remains, along with that of his son’s, who died in 1983, were transferred in 1971. The entire wealth of Moroccan decorative art of Andalusian origin is present in this monument: the 12-piece dome composed of sculpted mahogany and stained glass, the great bronze chandelier measuring 2.3 m. in diameter and weighing 1.5 tons, walls covered in *zellij* and in stucco, white onyx tombstones engraved by the great *m‘allem* Ibn ‘Abdelkrim, and granite floors, so thoroughly and perfectly polished, that the royal sarcophagus looks as if it is floating on a turquoise lake.  
Below the paved square of Hassan Tower, a new mosque, with a surface area covering 2,200 sq. m., adjoins the mausoleum. Its floor was set 1.2 m. into the ground in order to provide its prayer hall with sufficient height (7 m.) without overshadowing the majestic quality of the neighbouring mausoleum. This mosque contains two prayer rooms: one for men and one for women, which are separated by *mashrabiyya* and an interior courtyard paved in marble and framed by a portico of sculpted stone. The entire monument, dedicated to the memory of Mohamed V, is completed by a museum whose surface area amounts to 1,500 sq m., which traces the history of the ‘Alawite Dynasty from the 11th/17th century right up to the reign of Mohamed V. This museum contains a portico, unique of its kind, made of colonnades and arcades exposed to all kinds of winds; a completely novel idea, although conceived in a very traditional style. This portico is built on an esplanade identical to that on which the mausoleum is built, and access to the museum is provided by four staircases which lead to various exhibition rooms decorated in *zellij*, wood and plaster, each with its own particular character.  
The Hassan Tower and the Mohamed V Mausoleum, both situated on this same esplanade, cover between them over eight centuries of history.

es.name: Mausoleo de Mohamed V
description:
En el interior del recinto de la desaparecida Mezquita Mayor, frente a la Torre Hassan, el Mausoleo de Mohamed V (1927-1961) perpetúa el recuerdo del soberano que logró que el país recobrara su independencia. Este monumento, construido entre 1961 y 1969, se inspira en la arquitectura tradicional de las necrópolis reales. Situado sobre un zócalo de 3,50 m, está coronado por una techumbre piramidal cubierta de tejas verdes. Por una “galería-balcón” se accede a la sala funeraria donde se encuentran los restos del monarca —trasladados allí en 1971— y, en una esquina, los de su hijo Mulay Abdallah, fallecido en 1983. Toda la riqueza de la decoración marroquí tradicional, de origen andalusí se concentra en este lugar: una cúpula de 12 caras compuesta de madera de caoba tallada y vitrales de diversos colores, una gran lámpara de bronce de 2,30 m de diámetro y una tonelada y media de peso, muros recubiertos de *zelish* y estuco, la losa sepulcral en ónice blanco esculpida por el gran *m‘allem* Ibn Abdelkrim, y el suelo de granito con un pulido tan perfecto que el sarcófago real parece flotar en un lago turquesa.  
Más abajo del atrio embaldosado de la Torre Hassan hay una nueva mezquita con una superficie de 2.200 m2. El suelo se ha rebajado 1,20 m para proporcionar a la sala de oración altura suficiente (7 m) sin restar majestuosidad al vecino mausoleo. Esta mezquita cuenta con dos salas de oración separadas por celosías —una para los hombres y otra para las mujeres— y un patio interior enlosado en mármol, rodeado por un pórtico de piedra esculpida. El conjunto monumental dedicado a la memoria de Mohamed V se completa con un museo de una superficie de 1.500 m2, que recoge la historia de la dinastía alauí desde el siglo XI/XVII hasta el reinado de Mohamed V. El pórtico del museo, con sus arcadas abiertas a todos los vientos, es único en su género: su concepción es totalmente inédita, pero el estilo es puramente tradicional. Se alza sobre una explanada idéntica a la del mausoleo, y el acceso al museo se realiza por cuatro escaleras que conducen a las diversas salas de exposición, decoradas con *zelish*, madera y estuco, cada una con su sello particular. Con la Torre Hassan y el Mausoleo de Mohamed V, ocho siglos de historia se concentran en este explanada.

fr.name: Mausolée Mohammed V
description:
À l’intérieur de l’enceinte de la Grande Mosquée disparue, en face de la tour Hassan, se dresse le Mausolée Mohamed V qui perpétue le souvenir du souverain (1927-1961) qui fit retrouver au pays son indépendance. Ce monument, édifié entre 1961 et 1969, s’inspire de l’architecture traditionnelle des nécropoles royales. Placé sur un socle de 3,50 m de haut, il est surmonté d’un toit pyramidal recouvert de tuiles vertes. Par une “galerie- balcon”, on accède à la salle funéraire où se trouvent le tombeau de Mohamed V, dont la dépouille a été transférée en 1971, ainsi que celle de son fils Moulay Abdallah, décédé en 1983.Toute la richesse de la décoration marocaine traditionnelle, d’origine andalouse, y est concentrée: coupole à douze pans composée de bois d’acajou sculpté et de vitraux colorés, grand lustre en bronze de 2,30 m de diamètre et d’un poids d’une tonne et demie, murs couverts de *zellige* et de stuc, pierre tombale en onyx blanc sculptée par le grand *m‘allem* Ibn Abdelkrim, sol en granit dont le polissage est si parfait que le sarcophage royal semble flotter sur un lac de turquoise.  
En contrebas du parvis dallé de la tour Hassan, une nouvelle mosquée d’une superficie de 2 200 m2 jouxte le mausolée. Son sol a été abaissé de 1,20 m pour donner à la salle de prière une hauteur suffisante (7 m) sans rien enlever à la majesté du mausolée avoisinant. Cette mosquée comprend deux salles de prière: l’une pour les hommes et l’autre pour les femmes, séparées par des moucharabiehs, et une cour intérieure dallée de marbre et encadrée d’un portique en pierre sculptée. L’ensemble monumental, dédié à la mémoire de Mohamed V, est complété par un musée d’une superficie de 1 500 m2 qui retrace l’histoire de la dynastie alaouite depuis le XIe/XVIIe siècle jusqu’au règne de Mohamed V. Ce musée comporte un portique, unique en son genre, formé de colonnades et d’arcades ouvertes à tous les vents, d’une conception totalement inédite mais d’un style purement traditionnel. Ce portique est bâti sur une esplanade identique à celle qui supporte le mausolée, et l’accès au rez-de-chaussée intérieur du musée est assuré par quatre escaliers menant vers plusieurs salles d’exposition décorées de *zellige*s, de bois et de plâtre, chacune avec un cachet particulier.  
Avec la tour Hassan et le Mausolée Mohamed V, huit siècles se rejoignent sur cette esplanade.

en.name: Covered al-Buzuriyya Market
description: Apricot paste can be consumed in two ways. It can be eaten raw after cutting it into small pieces, or – especially during Ramadan – a syrup can be made from *Qamr ad-Din* after soaking it in water for several hours, straining, then cooling it. Sometimes orange blossom or rose water is added to the syrup. *Qamr ad-Din* is traditionally served thick and cold, and is thought to be particularly fortifying and a good energy source after a day of fasting. Some Damascenes add pine and ice cubes.

en.name: *Zafarnāmah by Sharaf al-Din ʿAli Yazdi* (Timur's Return to Samarkand and the Festive Celebrations in the Garden of Bagh-ı Behesht)
description: *Zafarnāmah* is a significant historical text from the 15th century that describes Timur's leadership and achievements. Written by Şerafeddin Ali Yezdî (Hegira 858 / AD 1454), the work was commissioned by Timur's grandson, Ibrahim Sultan. As a historical source, *Zafarnāmah* is invaluable for its comprehensive information about Timur's life. The book was compiled using notes taken by Timur's royal scribes and secretaries, indicating that its contents were meticulously selected. Its most significant source is the biography of Timur, *Zafarnāmah*, written by Nizāmeddīn-i Sāmī in 1404. The primary distinction between Şerafeddin's *Zafarnāmah* and Sāmī’s earlier *Zafarnāmah* lies in the novel information presented in Şerafeddin's later version, and the more elaborate embellishments, including miniatures, in Sāmī’s earlier one.  The later work was inscribed by Hamdullah ibn al-Sheikh Murshid al-Kātib in Hegira 891 / AD 1486–1487, and is written in Persian with black ink in *taliq* calligraphy on fine paper. The work contains ten miniature scenes of rich workmanship, most of which depict Timur. The miniatures generally portray battles, council meetings and festivities that took place during the Timurid period. The first page contains the foundation seal of Hacı Mehmed Aga, the trustee of Teke Sancağı (Antalya region). The following page displays an illumination comprising geometric and floral motifs on blue and gilt backgrounds. The titles of the chapters and some of the prayers are written in gilt, red and blue ink.
holder: Museum of Turkish and Islamic Arts
materials: Finished (*aharli*) paper, ink, gilding, leather binding
tags: Finished (aharli) paper, ink, gilding, leather binding
partner: Museum of Turkish and Islamic Arts

en.name: Photo – Banquet of the society Junimea
*Interior of a Harem*
short_description: Preziosi probably used models to recreate this harem scene which as an infidel Frank he would not normally be allowed to witness. However, there is nothing in this decorous interior which is impossible or unlikely and it may be based on a visit to the house of one of his Turkish friends. The furniture and fittings show western European influence, particularly in the curious rococo wall bracket and the fringed sofa in place of the traditional raised wooden platform covered with carpets. By the middle of the 19th century French style in interior design was fashionable in Turkey, especially a degenerate form of the rococo. A version of this composition, dated 1852, is much less restrained, its details deliberately pandering to the popular western idea of a harem, based on Arabian Nights imagery.
keywords: costume; coffee; tobacco; rococo; Ottoman Baroque; Orientalism; women; Ottoman interior decoration; fashion

en.name: Building a bridge near Haifa
description: This album of 39 images documents the construction of the Hijaz Railway. It photographs two important stretches of the network: the route between Damascus and Maʿan, and the line connecting Daraʿa with Haifa. Its photographs record the remarkable engineering achievements required to negotiate difficult and varied terrain, while also illustrating the railway’s role in strengthening connections across the empire. Alongside tunnels, bridges and stations, the images capture the engineers, officials and labourers whose work made the project possible.
holder: The Nasser D. Khalili Collection of Hajj and The Arts of Pilgrimage
keywords: Construction; engineering; communication; labour; bridge
materials: Photographic prints bound in an album
tags: Photographic prints bound in an album
partner: Khalili Family Trust – Hajj and the Arts of Pilgrimage Collection

en.name: Revolver
description: Revolver of Leopold Gasser (serial number 8106) used for land/terrestrial defence as opposed to the navy. It is also known as “Montenegrin” as it was used not only by the Austrian army but also by the army of Montenegro. The exterior was nickelled, but the nickel finish has mostly worn away leaving only traces on the barrel and the frame. The revolver is fitted with genuine ivory grips. The absence of any indication for Austria and the presence of the crown “R” might indicate to its production in Liege/Belgium.
holder: Jordan Folklore Museum, Department of Antiquities
place: Belgian copy of Leopold Gasser revolver

en.name: Qasr al-Banat
description:
Going inside the city wall, about 400 m north of the Gate of Baghdad and 150 m from the eastern wall, we find the Qasr al-Banat, “The Maidens’ Palace”. There is no reference to a palace inside the city walls in the historical sources, and the name is supposed to have come from a local tradition that bears no relation to the original structure. The lack of historical information also makes the dating and the attribution to a certain ruler impossible. According to the ceramic material and the coinage found in sondages in the palace, the foundation of the building was conducted in Abbasid times, probably during the reign of Abu Ja‘far al Mansur or Harun al-Rashid, followed by several later phases of renovations. References to a Zangid palace in the historical sources, along with stylistic criteria relating to the stucco decoration and the four-*iwans*\-in-axial-symmetry layout that later became a distinctive feature of Ayyubid palatial architecture, point to a date some time in the Zangid period.  
The roughly square structure measuring 42 m x 44 m contains 40 so far excavated rooms. The entrance is on the north wall; after crossing two rooms, one turns left and reaches the core of the monument: a square courtyard provided with an *iwan* on each side. A brick-built well that probably had a marble basin furnishes the centre of the courtyard, itself paved with stone slabs. The west, south and east sides comprise a single *iwan*, while a tripartite *iwan* accentuates the north side of the courtyard.  
Most remarkably in the western part of the palace, there is a square room with a row of decorative stucco niches on the upper part of the 8.7 m-high walls, still extant. A similar room exists in the eastern part of the monument where most of the rooms are paved with stone slabs. Exceptional also is the additional room to the north-west of the entrance that was paved with octagonal and round, glazed tiles. Remains of stucco-decorated windows and wall decorations, as well as wall paintings found during excavation works, give some idea of the once lavish decoration of the palace.

en.name: Hand carder
description: Carding is the preparation of raw, unordered or washed fibres to prepare them for spinning into long spirals. Carding can be used to create blends of different fibres or colours. Once carded, fibres can be used in a variety projects including spinning, weaving and felt making.
holder: Jordan River Foundation Bani Hamida Weaving Project

en.name: City bus
description: This bus was produced by the Gürel Toy Company in 1969, which was one of the most important tin toy manufacturers of the time. The company started manufacturing toys in 1944. The company is renowned for its huge variety of tin toys such as buses, planes, trucks, tanker trucks, vans, rattles, whistles, strollers, police cars, military vehicles and much more.
