description: The spiral part of the sceptre is covered with acanthus leaves and multi-coloured cut glass. In the central halo there is an image of the Madonna of Old Brno transferred into relief form as a cast statue.

ar.name: محبرة.
description:
أداة كتابة صغيرة ذات شكل أسطواني مزخرفة بإفريز مزود بأربعة رسوم منقوشة بارزة ومستديرة. وتمثل إحدى الرسوم على هذه النقوش البارزة فارساً مع فهد. وقد دربت هذه الحيوانات للصيد ولترافق الحاكم في رحلات الصيد. وهناك فارس يصطاد بالقوس والسهم، وآخر يظهر مع باز صيد يقف مستريحاً على ذراع الصياد، وثالث يظهر مع أسد يهاجمه. أما القاعدة الزخرفية لرموز الحكام هذه في القوة والسلطة فهي عبارة عن زخارف مع الأرابيسك مرتبة بشكل متناظر وعليها مشاهد حيوانية مع رسم للشمس. ويتشكل المحور الوسطي من رأس أسد ورأس ثور ورمز للشمس. كما تنتهي الأغصان بأزواج من الأسماك والطيور والسفينكس (كائن خرافي) والجديان تظهر بشكل خيالي رائع. ويزدان القعر بزخرفات من أشرطة مضفرة. وتعود الأغصان النباتية مع الرؤوس الحيوانية إلى القرن الثاني عشر في الأصقاع الشرقية من العالم الإسلامي، ولكنها وجدت أيضاً في القرن الثالث عشر في مناطق نفوذ الأيوبيين وفي شمال العراق تحت حكم الأمير بدر الدين واستخدمها الفنانون هناك في أعمالهم. وكان هذا النوع من الرسوم بعد ذلك هاماً أيضاً في الفن المعدني في العهد المملوكي.  
توجد على السطح الأعلى لأداة الكتابة هذه فتحة نصف دائرية ذات غطاء وتستخدم لوضع وعاء الحبر وهناك فتحتان أخريان مستديرتان لوضع ريش الكتابة. ويعتقد أن هذا الجزء هو ترميم من عهد المماليك، وقد استخدمت في ذلك زخرفات من الزهور لا تتناسب مع نوعية التصميم الفني للأجزاء الأخرى من الوعاء.  
يعتبر مالك أداة كتابة كهذه رجلاً مثقفاً لأنه كان يجيد فن الكتابة الذي كان له تقدير كبير في العالم الإسلامي نظراً لارتباطه بالمصحف الشريف. فالقرآن وحي أنزل على الرسول محمد (ص) ولا يزال يكتب حتى الآن باللغة العربية.

كانت هذه المحبرة الأسطوانية تُستخدم في الكتابة. وهي تشتمل على جيوب للحبر، وأدوات الكتابة، ومُزيَّنة بزخرف مُطعَّم بالفضّة يعرض مشاهد للقنص الملكي. كَتَبَةُ العصر المثقفون كانوا يتباهون بمحابرهم المُزخرفة؛ لذا فإن هذه ـ ربما ـ نُفِّذت تلبيةً لطلب أحد هؤلاء.
dates: النصف الثاني من القرن السابع/النصف الثاني من القرن الثالث عشر.
keywords: أداة كتابة؛ أرابيسك؛ عهد أيوبي؛ توشية؛ مماليك.
partner: متحف الفن الإسلامي في متحف بيرغامون ، المتاحف الحكومية

de.name: Tintenfaß, (Schreibzeug).
description: Das zylindrisch geformte kleine Schreibzeug hat einen Dekor, der als Fries mit vier Rundmedaillons gestaltet ist. Eine der Darstellungen in den Medaillons zeigt einen Reiter mit Geparden. Diese Tiere wurden für die Jagd regelrecht ausgebildet, um den Herrscher bei der Jagd zu begleiten. Ein Reiter jagt mit Pfeil und Bogen, einer erscheint mit auf der Hand des Jägers ruhendem Jagdfalken, einer mit angreifendem Löwen. Der dekorative Untergrund für diese Herrschersymbole der Macht sind symmetrisch angelegte Arabesken mit Tiermotiven und der Darstellung der Sonne. Die Mittelachse ist aus Löwen- und Stierkopf und dem Sonnensymbol aufgebaut. Die Ranken enden in Paaren von Fischen, Vögeln, Sphingen und Steinböcken. Sie erscheinen sehr phantasievoll. Der Boden ist mit einem Flechtbandornament versehen. Die Pflanzenranke mit Tierköpfen entstand im 12. Jahrhundert in östlichen Teilen der islamischen Welt, sie wurden aber auch im 13. Jahrhundert im Herrschaftsgebiet der Ayyubiden und des nordirakischen Fürsten Badr ad-Din von den Künstlern benutzt. Später war sie auch wichtig für die Metallkunst der Mamluken. Das Schreibzeug hat an der Oberseite eine halbkreisförmige Öffnung mit Deckel für den Einsatz eines Tintenfasses und zwei kreisförmige Öffnungen für die Aufbewahrung der Schreibfedern. Dieser Teil ist vermutlich eine Restaurierung aus mamlukischer Zeit. Dabei wurde ein Blütendekor verwendet, der der Qualität des künstlerischen Entwurfs des übrigen Teils des Gefäßes nicht entspricht. Der Besitzer eines Schreibzeuges wie dieses, galt als gebildeter Mann, da er die Kunst des Schreibens beherrschte, die wegen ihrer koranbezogenheit in der islamischen Welt eine besondere Wertschätzung genoß. Der Koran galt als die Offenbarung des Propheten Mohammad, die bis heute in arabischer Schrift geschrieben wird.

Dieser zylindrische Tintenhalter verfügt über Behälter für Tinte und Schreibgerät und ist mit Silbereinlegearbeiten versehen, die Szenen einer königlichen Jagd zeigen. Gelernte Schreiber dieser Zeit waren stolz auf ihre verzierten Tintenhalter. Dieses Exemplar könnte also von einem Schreiber in Auftrag gegeben worden sein.
keywords: Ayyubiden; Schreibzeug; Tauschierung; Arabeske; Mamluken
partner: Museum für Islamische Kunst, Pergamon Museum

en.name: Inkstand.
description:
The decoration on this small cylindrical writing implement consists of a frieze composed of four round medallions. One of the medallions shows a depiction of a rider with cheetahs. These animals were especially trained for hunting, in order to accompany the rulers on their hunts. One of the riders hunts with bows and arrows, another appears with a hunting falcon resting on his arm, and another with an attacking lion. Symmetrical arabesques featuring animal motifs and a depiction of the sun provide the decorative backdrop to these symbols of power of the ruling class. The horizontal (middle) axis depicts heads of lions and bulls (Leo and Taurus) and the sun. The tendrils end in pairs of fish (Pisces), birds, sphinxes and ibexes (Capricorn). They are highly fantastical. The bottom part is decorated with a plaited ornamental band. The imagery of plant tendrils ending in animal heads originated during the AH 6th / AD 12th century in the eastern part of the Islamic world, but it was also used by artists in the AH 7th / AD 13th century in the lands ruled by the Ayyubids, and in the kingdom of the northern Iraqi prince Badr ad-Din. Later, it was also of importance in the metalwork of the Mamluks.  
On the top of the inkstand there is a semi-circular opening with a lid in which to fit an inkwell, and two circular openings to hold feather quills. This part is most probably a work of restoration done during the Mamluk period. It is decorated with a blossom motif, but the quality of this decoration does not match that of the rest of the receptacle in terms of artistic skill.  
The owner of such an inkstand would be considered to be an educated man who had mastered the art of writing, which, due to its use in the Qur’an, was highly esteemed in the Islamic world. The Qur’an was believed to be the revelation of the Prophet Muhammad, and is still written in Arabic script today.

This cylindrical inkstand was used as writing tool. It has receptacles for ink and writing implements and is decorated with silver inlay showing scenes of the royal hunt. Learned scribes of the period were proud of their decorated inkstands and so this may have been commissioned by a scribe.
holder: Museum of Islamic Art at the Pergamon Museum
Museum of Arts and Crafts, Berlin.
dates: Hegira second half of the 7th century / AD second half of the 13th century.
keywords: Ayyubid; inkstand; inlay; arabesque; Mamluk
partner: Museum of Islamic Art at the Pergamon Museum, State Museums

es.name: Tintero.
description:
Pequeño utensilio cilíndrico de escritorio, decorado con un friso de cuatro medallones redondos. En uno de ellos aparece representado un jinete con guepardos, animales que se adiestraban para acompañar a los gobernantes en las cacerías; el jinete de otro medallón está representado con arco y flechas; otro, con un halcón sobre su brazo; por último, el cuarto está siendo atacado por un león. Estos símbolos del poder de la clase gobernante están dibujados sobre un fondo de arabescos simétricos con motivos animales y soles. El eje horizontal medio está decorado con representaciones fantásticas que aluden a los signos del Zodiaco: cabezas de leones y toros (Leo y Tauro) y el sol. Los tallos terminan en fantasiosas parejas de peces (Piscis), aves, esfinges y cabras monteses (Capricornio). La parte inferior del tintero está decorada con una banda de ornamentos trenzados. Las imágenes de zarcillos terminados en cabezas de animales proceden del oriente del mundo islámico, donde surgieron en el siglo VI / XII, aunque los artistas de los dominios ayyubíes y del príncipe Badr ad-Din (norte de Irak) las seguían utilizando en el siglo VII / XIII. Los mamelucos también las emplearon mucho en la metalistería.  
En la parte superior presenta una abertura semicircular con tapa para la tinta y dos orificios circulares para las plumas. Lo más probable es que esta parte de la pieza fuera restaurada en periodo mameluco, su decoración floral no alcanza la calidad de la del resto de la pieza.  
El dueño de este tintero debió de ser un hombre instruido que dominaba la escritura, muy apreciada en el mundo islámico debido al Corán, considerado como revelación al Profeta y que aún los fieles siguen leyendo en árabe.

Tintero cilíndrico con un depósito para la tinta y dos orificios para utensilios de escritura. Está decorado con incrustaciones de plata que representan escenas de cacerías reales. Los cultos escribas de la época estaban orgullosos de sus tinteros decorados, así que seguramente este fue encargado por uno de ellos.
holder: Museo de Arte Islámico del Museo Pergamon
dates: Segunda mitad del siglo VII de la Hégira / XIII d. C.
keywords: Ayyubíes; tintero; incrustación; arabesco; mamelucos.
partner: Museo de Arte Islámico en el Museo de Pérgamo, Museos Estatales

fr.name: Écritoire.
description:
Ce petit ustensile à écriture de forme cylindrique présente un décor de frise à quatre médaillons. L'un de ces médaillons montre un cavalier avec des guépards. Ces animaux étaient spécialement dressés pour accompagner le souverain à la chasse. Un cavalier chasse à l'arc, un autre apparaît un faucon au poing, le dernier est attaqué par un lion. Ces symboles de pouvoir se lisent sur un fond décoratif d'arabesques symétriques avec motifs animaliers et image du soleil. L'axe médian est constitué de têtes de lion et de taureau et du symbole solaire. Les rinceaux se terminent par des couples de poissons, d'oiseaux, de sphinges et de béliers, dans une facture pleine de fantaisie. Les rinceaux végétaux accompagnés de têtes d'animaux apparurent au VIe siècle H (XIIe siècle J.-C.) dans la partie orientale du monde islamique, mais ils furent aussi utilisés au VIIe siècle H (XIIIe siècle J.-C.) dans le royaume des Ayyoubides et du prince Badr al-Din au nord de l'Irak. Ils eurent ensuite une grande importance dans l'art du métal des Mamelouks.  
Cet ustensile présente une ouverture en demi-cercle pour le pot à encre et deux trous circulaires pour les plumes. Cette partie est probablement une restauration d'époque mamelouke, le décor floral employé ne correspondant pas au niveau esthétique du reste de l'ustensile.  
Le propriétaire d'un écritoire de ce type était un homme cultivé, puisqu'il possédait l'art de l'écriture, qui était particulièrement respecté, l'islam étant fortement attaché au Coran. Le Coran était considéré comme la révélation du prophète Muhammad, une révélation aujourd'hui encore rédigée en écriture arabe.

Cet écritoire cylindrique était utilisé comme ustensile d'écriture. Il comporte des réceptacles pour l'encre et les instruments d'écriture et est décoré d'incrustations d'argent représentant des scènes de chasse royale. Les scribes cultivés de l'époque étaient fiers de leurs écritoires décorés, ce qui permet de penser que celui-ci a été commandité par un scribe.
dates: Seconde moitié du VIIe siècle de l’Hégire (XIIIe siècle J.-C.).
keywords: Ayyoubide ; mamelouk ; écritoire ; damasquiné ; arabesque
partner: Musée d’art islamique du Pergamon Museum (Museum für Islamische Kunst)

en.name: L'École de la Rue du Pacha (inside the classroom)
short_description: This photograph shows a classroom of young Muslim girls at l'École Louise-Renée-Millet (renamed l'École de la Rue du Pacha in 1911/1912) in 1908. The presence of a *moueddeb* and a French teacher is notable. The *moueddeb* would have taught the principles of the Quran and elementary Arabic (reading, writing, arithmetic), whereas the French teacher would have covered the French education (literature, history, science and hygiene), as well as needlework (embroidery, sewing, lace). For the younger pupils of the school this classroom was the door to the world and one which allowed them to explore life. Young girls of this time often lived very sheltered lives, shut away in their homes without the opportunity to learn. Their education was usually limited to housework and needlework, either at home or at a Dar el-Maalma, a local atelier run by an old housewife.
holder: Institut Supérieur d’Histoire Contemporaine de la Tunisie
keywords: Young girls' education; schools
partner: Higher Institute for the Study of Contemporary History of Tunisia, University of Manouba

fr.name: Ecole de la rue du Pacha (en classe)
short_description: Classe de jeunes musulmanes de l’école Louise-Renée-Millet en 1908 (école de la rue du Pacha depuis 1911-1912) ; on note la présence du *moueddeb* et de la maîtresse française. Le *moueddeb* enseignait les principes du Coran et les premiers éléments d’instruction arabe (lire, écrire, calculer) tandis que l’institutrice française dispensait une instruction française (littérature, histoire, science et hygiène) complétée par des travaux d’aiguille (broderie, couture, dentelle). Pour les premières générations de l’école, la classe fut la découverte de la vie, la première ouverture sur les horizons du monde. En effet, des siècles durant, la jeune musulmane restait cloîtrée chez elle, il n’était pas admis qu’elle s’instruise. Son éducation se limitait à l’apprentissage du ménage et à quelques travaux d’aiguille à la maison ou à Dar el-Maalma, un atelier dans le quartier sous la direction d’une vieille ménagère.
holder: Institut supérieur d’Histoire contemporaine de la Tunisie
keywords: Enseignement de jeunes filles; Ecoles
partner: Institut Supérieur d’histoire contemporaine de la Tunisie, Université de la Manouba

en.name: Noria Jisriyya and Ma‘muriyya
description:
These norias have been carefully restored in recent years. The Jisriyya is known to have irrigated a wide expanse of orchards called Bustan al-Shahiqa and a long part of its aquaduct arcade is still standing. The Ma’muriyya is the largest noria on the Orontes, second only to the Muhamaddiya located to the north of the city. It measures a diameter of 21 meters with a total of 120 buckets. All these norias are known to have been used since early Roman times, as indicated by archaeological findings at the tower bases below the water, and they were certainly strengthened and restored during Nur al-Din's reign, and continued to be resoterd regularly to this day. But unlike most of the noria, this one carries an inscription commemorating the noria’s renovation by an Ottoman governor in 857/1453.  
Next to the Ma’muriyya are two smaller norias called al-Uthamaniyya and al-Mu’ayadiyya. These smaller wheels are some of the smallest on the Orontes, the former has a diameter of 11 m while the latter a mere 7. They were originally meant to function as mills and, in more recent times, serve as workshops for the water-wheel carpenters.

en.name: Hamidi Hospital (Mashfa al-Ghuraba)
description: The Hamidi Hospital (Mashfa al-Ghuraba, or Hospital of Strangers) was established in Damascus during the reign of Ottoman Sultan Abdülhamid II. The hospital opened in 1317 AH (1900), west of the Suleymaniye Takiyya. It was built by the Damascus municipality, financed through public donations, municipal revenues, and endowments previously supporting the Nuri Hospital. Its establishment formed part of the expansion of modern medical institutions in late Ottoman Damascus. The hospital was associated with medical provision for Ottoman soldiers and workers on the Hijaz Railway. In 1903, an imperial decree authorised the establishment of a medical school on the hospital's grounds, and the school was later moved into its own building in 1914.  The Hospital was renamed the National Hospital during the period of the short-lived Arab government following Ottoman rule. The building was subsequently restored and adapted into the Rida Said Conference Centre of Damascus University, opened in September 2003.
keywords: Damascus; Hamidi Hospital; Hospital of Strangers; Ottoman Empire; Abdülhamid II; Ottoman healthcare; Hospitals; Damascus School of Medicine; Rida Said Conference Centre
partner: Ministry of Culture, Directorate General of Museums and Antiquities

en.name: "The Castle Water Clock" from al-Jazari's "Book of Knowledge of Ingenious Mechanical Devices"
description:
In the early AH 8th / AD 13th-century, a scholar and engineer named Isma‘il Ibn al-Razzaz al-Jazari wrote a famous treatise called *Kitab fi ma‛rifat al-hiyal al-handasiyya*, or The Book of Knowledge of Ingenious Mechanical Devices. The text offered detailed descriptions of a series of elaborate machines designed to delight and impress the elites at the court where he served, in eastern Anatolia. Al-Jazari’s text and its illustrations belong to a long tradition of studies about these kinds of devices, including Greek compendia on mechanics and mathematics. This page belongs to a copy of the text that was produced in Mamluk Egypt in AH 755 / AD 1354, and was copied by Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Izmiri for a Mamluk ruler.  
  
This folio illustrates elaborate hydraulic clock in the form of a palace gateway.
keywords: Water; Mamluks; Technical Manuscripts; folio.
materials: Ink, watercolour and gold on paper

en.name: Advertisement from the International Exhibition in Rome 1911
short_description: During the International Exhibition of Fine Arts in 1911, in a green area near the Tiber river within Rome’s boundaries, exhibitions of regions and ethnography were staged. This show was meant to celebrate ethnography as a new science and, at the same time, to highlight the habits and customs of the different regions of Italy, especially on the occasion of the 50th anniversary celebrations of the unification of the Italian state. A consequence of the exhibition was an enlargement of the city of Rom and massive urban growth. At the same time, upon the Rassegna Illustrata dell’Esposizione commercial pavilions were destined to later become restaurants, shops and pubs. All of them were clearly inspired by the popularity of orientalism.

en.name: Municipal Building
description:
The town hall building can be found in Piazza San Nicola at the end of the Corso; it was built in 1997–1998 in post-modern forms according to the design of architect Francesco Petrucci. The area used to host a monastery of the Christian Doctrine Fathers, which had been built in 1668, transformed into a town hall in 1870 (after the final defeat of the Papal State in Rome and the unification of Italy) and destroyed during the Allied bombing of 1944. On the balcony you may appreciate the terracotta reliefs representing Rural Work (the grape harvest) and Industrial Work, symbols of ancient and modern Ariccia; while on the side facing the Church of Saint Nicholas one might see the terracotta finial depicting Diana Aricina and the inscription with the famous quote of Cicero about Aricia (Philippica, 3): "\[Aricia\] municipium vetustate antiquissimum, jure foederatum, propinquitate paene finitimum, splendor municipium honestissimum". These reliefs were made by the sculptor Claudio Cottiga.  
  
The Town Hall is connected to a pre-existing building that looks onto Piazza della Repubblica and Piazzale Mazzini, previously used as an elementary school and today as municipal offices. Walls in *opus quadratrum* of the Republican age, which were part of the substructures to the republican temple, can be seen through openings on the street level. Other similar walls are visible inside the building and in particular at the headquarters of the Municipal Treasury on Via Laziale.  
(Bibliography: A. Martorelli, 1930; A. Mancini, 1982; F. Guglielmi, 1985; F. Petrucci, 1998c; id., 2004)

it.name: Palazzo Municipale
description:
L’edificio di Piazza San Nicola alla fine del Corso, adibito a sede comunale, è stato costruito nel 1997-1998 in forme post-moderne su progetto dell’arch. Francesco Petrucci. Sul luogo preesisteva un monastero dei Padri della Congregazione della Dottrina Cristiana edificato nel 1668, trasformato dopo il 1870 in municipio e distrutto durante i bombardamenti alleati del 1944. Sul balconcino rilievi in terracotta illustranti il *Lavoro contadino* (la raccolta dell’uva) e il *Lavoro industriale*, emblemi di Ariccia antica e moderna. Sul lato verso la chiesa di San Nicola fastigio in terracotta raffigurante Diana Aricina e iscrizione riferita al noto passo di Cicerone (Philippica, 3): “*\[Aricia\] municipium vetustate antiquissimum, jure foederatum, propinquitate paene finitimum, splendore municipium honestissimum*”. Tali rilievi sono stati realizzati dallo scultore Claudio Cottiga.  
La costruzione è saldato ad un preesistente fabbricato che prospetta su piazza della Repubblica e piazzale Mazzini, già adibito a scuola elementare ed oggi ad uffici comunali. Sono visibili attraverso aperture al piano strada, murature in opera quadrata di età repubblicana, facenti parte delle sostruzioni del tempio repubblicano. Altre simili murature sono visibili all’interno del fabbricato e in particolare nella sede della Tesoreria Comunale su via Laziale.  
(Bibliografia: A. Martorelli, 1930; A. Mancini, 1982; F. Guglielmi, 1985; F. Petrucci, 1998c; id., 2004)

en.name: *David with the Head of Goliath*
description:
This painting was probably part of the collection of Cardinal Scipione Borghese, and in fact there is a 1612 document making reference to the biblical subject, concerning the acquisition of a frame for the work.  
The picture is attributed to the Neapolitan Giovanni Battista Caracciolo, also known as Battistello, but over the centuries the inventories have attributed it to many different artists. Apart from one entry in 1650, where the canvas was ascribed to Giulio Romano, it has usually been attributed to Caravaggesque artists.  
The young David is central and isolated, holding the decapitated head of the giant, Goliath, which rests on a marble base decorated with floral motifs.  
The biblical hero stands out from the dark background, appearing in the foreground bathed in an almost violent light, in a relaxed pose, apparently detached from the bloody deed he has just committed. His crossed legs, austere but serene face, and feathered red hat, an ostentatious show of contemporaneousness: all of the details in the composition are constructed using a “masking” technique. Battistello uses a traditional dark preparation of the picture for the background and the shadows. The shapes are rendered using a few, mainly earth colours, with strong highlights for emphasis.  
The young Battistello was influenced by the style of Caravaggio, who, in 1607, fled Rome for Naples having been condemned to death. He expanded on the Lombard master's study of nature and light, something which is evident in the painting. His style evolved further after 1612 with his experience in Rome, which enabled him to see the paintings of Carracci and his followers. Later visits to Genoa and Florence also helped to mould his style.

The Neapolitan painter was one of the greatest of Caravaggio's followers, and his powerful work was an important factor in making Naples a stronghold of the Caravaggesque style. In this painting David, wearing a red hat, triumphs beside the severed head of Goliath.  
His crossed legs, austere but serene face, and feathered red hat, an ostentatious show of contemporaneousness, contrast with the bloody aspect of the traditional iconography.
keywords: Caravaggio; realism; Neapolitan painters; Christian themes

it.name: *David con la testa di Golia*
description:
Il dipinto faceva probabilmente parte della collezione del cardinale Scipione Borghese; esiste difatti un documento del 1612 che fa riferimento al soggetto biblico, relativo all'acquisto di una cornice di misure corrispondenti all'opera.  
Il quadro è riferito al pittore napoletano Giovan Battista Caracciolo, detto Battistello, ma è stata ascritto negli inventari, nel corso dei secoli, a molteplici artisti. A parte una citazione del 1650, dove la tela era attribuita a Giulio Romano, è stata normalmente assegnata ad artisti di ambito caravaggesco.  
Il giovane David rimane isolato e centrale, tiene con la mano la testa decapitata del gigante Golia, poggiata su di una base in marmo decorata a motivi floreali.  
L'eroe biblico si staglia dal fondo scuro e appare in primo piano sotto una luce quasi violenta, che lo mostra in una posa tranquilla, apparentemente distaccato dall'evento cruento appena compiuto. Le gambe incrociate, il volto severo, ma sereno, il cappello rosso piumato, appariscente attributo della contemporaneità, tutti i dettagli della composizione sono pittoricamente costruiti con la tecnica “a risparmio”. Battistello si servì della tradizionale preparazione scura del quadro per lo sfondo e per le ombre, mentre le forme sono realizzate con pochi colori, in prevalenza a base di terre, su cui le forti lumeggiature danno risalto ai volumi.  
Battistello giovane fu influenzato dallo stile di Caravaggio, che nel 1607 soggiornò a Napoli in fuga da Roma a seguito della condanna a morte nei suoi confronti. Del grande maestro lombardo approfondisce lo studio del naturalismo e del luminismo che appare ben evidente nel dipinto. Il suo stile ebbe un'ulteriore evoluzione con l'esperienza romana del 1612 che gli diede la possibilità di conoscere sia la pittura dei Carracci che degli artisti caraveggeschi; anche i successivi soggiorni a Genova e Firenze contribuirono nella elaborazione del suo stile.

Il pittore napoletano fu uno dei più grandi seguaci di Caravaggio e la potenza delle sue opere fu un fattore importante che rese Napoli una roccaforte dello stile caravaggesco.  
In questo dipinto David che indossa un cappello rosso, trionfa dietro la testa mozzata di Golia.  
Le gambe incrociate, il volto severo, ma sereno, il cappello rosso piumato, appariscente attributo della contemporaneità, sono in contrasto con l'aspetto cruento della icografia tradizionale.
keywords: Caravaggio; realismo; pittori napoletani; tematiche cristiane

en.name: Pair of Doors with Design of Ten-Pointed Stars and Geometric Motifs
description: Double doors of hollow-core construction. Posterns are centered in the lower section of each door. Decorated overall with elaborate marquetry of small inlaid wood pieces (lazo-work). Each piece is decorated with an arabesque in white and black, painted on an overall red ground in a ten-pointed star motif with an infinite geometric design. The doors and each postern are secured with a iron throw-bolt lock. Each throw-bolt is made of three iron eyelets connected to a hanging lever. The main throw-bolt is large and elaborate, forged with a twisted spiral lever joined at a square panel with a carved crest on the surface. The postern bolts are smaller and plain. Studded iron rivets fasten wide iron strapwork that reinforces the doors horizontally. Some traces of gilding remain on the iron rivets.
dates: Hegira Mid 9th to early 11th century / AD 15th–16th century
keywords: Door; Architecture; Sculpture; Paint; Wood; Gilding; Toledo; Spain; Europe; Mudéjar

ar.name: قلعة الوعيرة.
description:
الوعيرة أو وادي موسى كما وُصفت عند الفرنجة واحدة من عدة قلاع شيِّدت في البتراء وما حولها سنة 508 - 509 / 1115 - 1116من قِبَل بلدوين الأول - ملك مملكة اللاتين في القدس. تتخذ القلعة التي شيِّدت من كتل حجرية من الصخر الرملي شكلاً مستطيلاً غير متساوي الأضلاع تتراوح أبعاده ما بين 100 م طولاً و 65 - 80 م عرضاً. يعود السبب في عدم انتظام شكل القلعة إلى طبوغرافية المنطقة، فالجدران المحيطة تتبع في امتدادها الهضبات الصخرية الناتئة. يدعم الجدران المحيطة مجموعة من الأبراج الصغيرة، ويقع أحد البرجين الرئيسيين في منتصف الجدار الشرقي والثاني عند الزاوية الشمالية الغربية المطلة على وادي الوعيرة. كان الدخول إلى القلعة يتم عبر نفق حُفر في الصخر الرملي ورُبط بجسر أقيم فوق وادي الوعيرة. يحتل الزاوية الشمالية الغربية كنيسة صغيرة مسقوفة بقبو برميلي، أبعادها 14 X 7 م.  
  
كانت القلعة واحدة من المنشآت والأبنية التي شيِّدت لحماية الموقع، وكانت تشتمل على جدران طويلة، وأبراج مراقبة، بالإضافة إلى عدة خزانات مائية حُفرت في الصخر الرملي. كان الغرض من بناء هذه القلعة والقلاع المعاصرة لها في الشوبك والحبيس داخل البتراء حماية المنطقة الواقعة جنوب شرق البحر الميت، وإعاقة قوافل الحج والتجارة التي تنتقل ما بين سورية ومصر والحجاز.  
  
انتهت سيطرة الفرنجة على القلعة سنة 584 / 1188إثر سقوطها بيد جنود صلاح الدين الأيوبي قبل فترة قصيرة من سقوط قلعة الشوبك. أدخل الأيوبيون تعديلات بسيطة على القلعة، لكنهم لم يضيفوا إليها أي بناء مهم.

كانت قلعة العيرة؛ "عجل موسى" حسب التسمية الفرنجية، جزءاً من نظام الدفاع عن البتراء، الذي أسَّسه بالدوين الأول، ملك مملكة القدس اللاتينية، في عام 509 – 510 هـ/1115 – 1116م. جنباً إلى جنب مع قلعة الشوبك، الواقعة على بعد نحو 34 كم إلى الشمال، وفَّرت تحصينات البتراء للفرنجة قدراً من التحكم بالمنطقة المُمتدَّة جنوب شرق البحر الميت، وعطَّلت الصلة التجارية والعسكرية بين سورية، ومصر، والحجاز. ما لبثت قلعة العيرة هذه أن سقطت بيد قوات صلاح الدين في عام 84 هـ/1188م، بُعيد سقوط الشوبك. ليس ثمَّة أيّ إنشاءات أيوبية رئيسية في القلعة، التي شُيِّدت على امتداد جروف صخرية رملية طبيعية، شديدة الانحدار.
keywords: برج؛ صلاح الدين؛ قلعة؛ مصلى.

en.name: Wu’ayra.
description:
Wu'ayra, Frankish 'Les Vaux Moises' is one of several fortresses and installations built in and around Petra by Baldwin I, King of the Latin Kingdom of Jerusalem, in 1115–16. The castle, an irregular rectangle measuring approximately 100 m x 65–80 m, and built of sandstone blocks of various sizes and shapes, is located about 34 km to the south of Shawbak (Montreal) and 1 km north of the main entrance to Petra. The irregularity of the plan is due to the nature of the terrain since the walls of the castle are built along natural sandstone ridges.  
The outer enclosing walls were combined with a series of small towers, the two primary ones being near the middle of the west side, and the other in the northeast corner overlooking wadi Wu'ayra. Entrance to the castle was through a narrow rock-hewn tunnel southeast of the castle which was connected to a bridge spanning wadi al-Wu'ayra. The northwestern corner is occupied by a single nave chapel (14 m x 7 m) with a barrel-vaulted roof.  
The castle was part of an elaborate system of defensive installations which included long walls, observation towers and cisterns dug out of the sandstone rock. The three contemporaneous Crusader castles of Shawbak, Wu'ayra and Habis in the Petra basin were meant to secure the region southeast of the Dead Sea for the Franks in Jerusalem, and had the further advantage of hindering both the commercial and military connections between Syria, the Hijaz and Egypt.  
Crusader occupation of Wu'ayra came to an end when it fell to the soldiers of Salah al-Din (Saladin) in AH 584 / AD 1188 shortly before the fall of Shawbak.  
There is no evidence of major Ayyubid constructions; only minor modification and additions are attested for this period.

The castle at Wu‘ayra, Frankish ‘Les Vaux Moises’, was part of a defensive system built at Petra in AH 509–10 / AD 1115–6 by Baldwin I, King of the Latin Kingdom of Jerusalem. Together with Shawbak, about 34 km to the north, the Petra fortifications gave the Franks loose control over the area southeast of the Dead Sea, and hindered the commercial and military connection between Syria, Egypt and the Hijaz. Wu‘ayra fell to the forces of Salah al-Din in 584 / 1188 shortly before Shawbak. There are no major Ayyubid constructions at the castle, which was built along steep natural sandstone ridges.
keywords: Castle; chapel; fortress; Salah al-Din (Saladin); tower
partner: Ministry of Tourism & Antiquities, Department of Antiquities

es.name: Al-Wuayra
description:
Al-Wuayra, Li Vaux Moyse para los francos, es una de las varias fortalezas y establecimientos que Balduino I, cabeza del reino latino de Jerusalén, construyó en Petra y alrededores en 1115-1116. El castillo, un rectángulo irregular de unos 100 × 65-80 m, se construyó con bloques de piedra arenisca de varios tamaños y formas. La irregularidad del trazado responde a la naturaleza del terreno, dado que los muros se construyeron a lo largo de protuberancias naturales de piedra arenisca.  
Los muros de cierre se combinaron en el exterior con una serie de pequeñas torres; una de las dos principales está situada hacia la mitad de la fachada occidental y la otra está en la esquina noreste, desde donde se domina el valle de al-Wuayra. Al castillo se entraba por el sureste del edificio, a través de un estrecho túnel excavado en la roca que se comunicaba con un puente que se extendía por el valle de al-Wu’ayra. En la esquina noroccidental hay una capilla de una sola nave (14 × 7 m) con bóveda de cañón.  
Este castillo formaba parte de un complejo sistema de construcciones defensivas que englobaba largas murallas, atalayas y aljibes excavados en rocas de piedra arenisca. En la cuenca de Petra hay tres castillos cruzados de la misma época (al-Shawbak, al-Wuayra y al-Habis) construidos por los francos de Jerusalén para proteger la región sureste del mar Muerto; contaban con la ventaja añadida de que entorpecían las conexiones comerciales y militares entre Siria, el Hiyaz y Egipto.  
La ocupación cruzada de al-Wuayra llegó a su fin con la derrota frente a los soldados de Salah al-Din (Saladino) en el año 584 / 1118, poco después de la toma de al-Shawbak. No existen vestigios de edificios ayyubíes importantes, de la época sólo queda constancia de ligeras modificaciones y ampliaciones.

El castillo de al-Wuayra (Li Vaux Moyse para los francos) formó parte de un sistema defensivo construido en Petra en 509-510 / 1115-1116 por el rey Balduino I de Jerusalén. Junto con Shawbak, 34 km al norte, los castillos de Petra otorgaron el control a los francos sobre la región sureste del mar Muerto y obstaculizaron las conexiones comerciales y militares entre Siria, Egipto y el Hiyaz. Al-Wuayra se rindió a Saladino en 584 / 1188, poco antes que Shawbak. No hay construcciones ayyubíes importantes en el castillo, levantado sobre un cerro de piedra arenisca.
keywords: Castillo; capilla; fortaleza; Salah al-Din; torre.

fr.name: Al-Wu’ayra.
description:
Al-Wu'ayra, de l'ancien français “Li Vaux Moyse”, est au nombre des forteresses et établissements édifiés dans et autour de Pétra par Baudouin Ier, souverain du royaume latin de Jérusalem en 1115-1116. Situé à 34 km au sud de Shawbak (Montréal) et 1 km au nord de l'entrée principale de Pétra, le château est en forme de rectangle irrégulier de 100 x 65-80 m environ, édifié en moellons de grès de formes et dimensions diverses.  
Les remparts présentent une série de petites tours dont les deux principales se dressent près du centre du flanc droit et une autre à l'angle nord-ouest dominant le *wadi* al-Wu'ayra. L'entrée se faisait par un étroit tunnel creusé dans le roc que l'on atteignait par un pont franchissant ce *wadi*. L'angle nord-ouest est occupé par une chapelle à nef unique de 14 x 7 m à voûte en berceau.  
Le château faisait partie d'un système défensif perfectionné qui comprenait de longs murs, des tours de guet et des citernes creusées dans le grès. Les trois châteaux croisés de la même époque, al-Shawbak, al-Wu'ayra et al-Habis, dans le bassin de Pétra, avaient pour fonction de sécuriser la région sud-ouest de la mer Morte afin de protéger Jérusalem ; par ailleurs, ils présentaient le double avantage d'entraver les communications tant commerciales que militaires entre la Syrie, le Hedjaz et l'égypte.  
La présence militaire des Croisés à al-Wu'ayra prit fin lorsque la forteresse tomba aux mains de Salah al-Din (Saladin) en 584 H / 1188 J.-C., peu avant la chute d'al-Shawbak.  
On ne trouve pas de traces de constructions ayyoubides importantes, seules quelques modifications et des additions sont attestées pour cette période.

Le château d’al-Wu’ayra, de l’ancien français “Li Vaux Moyse”, faisait partie du système défensif édifié à Pétra en 509-510 H / 1115-516 J.-C. par Baudouin Ier, souverain du royaume latin de Jérusalem. Avec le château de Shawbak, situé à environ 34 km au nord, les fortifications de Petra donnaient aux Francs le contrôle total sur la région sud-est de la mer Morte, et entravaient les communications tant commerciales que militaires entre la Syrie, l’Égypte et le Hedjaz. Al-Wu’ayra tomba aux mains de Salah al-Din (Saladin) en 584 H/ 1188 J.-C. Il n’y a pas de construction ayyoubide d’importance au château, qui fut bâti le long d’une dorsale naturelle gréseuse.
keywords: châteaux ; forteresses ; Salah al-Din (Saladin) ; tours

en.name: Main Chapel, interior
description: Main altarpiece with a huge retable decorated in *azulejos* in the so called National style. In the centre of the retable there is a reliquary in gilt silver donated by the pilgrims of Lisbon in 1680, it holds the image of Our Lady of Cape Espichel.
place: Sanctuary of Our Lady of Cape Espichel
partner: Institute for the Administration of Architectural and Archaeological Heritage -  IGESPAR

pt.name: Interior da Capela-mor
description: O altar-mor, decorado com um enorme retábulo e azulejos no Estilo Nacional, tem, no seu centro, um relicário em prata dourada contendo uma imagem da Nossa Senhora do Cabo Espichel, que foi doado pelos peregrinos de Lisboa, em 1680.

ar.name: مصبنة طوقان.
description:
تتكون المصبنة من بناء حجري كبير ذي مسقط مستطيل يتكون من طابقين. الواجهة الرئيسية للمبنى قليلة الزخارف، وفُتح في وسط القسم السفلي منها مدخل كبير لتسهيل إدخال أحمال الزيت الذي يصنع منه الصابون وخروج أحمال الصابون. ويعلو فتحة هذا المدخل عقد مدبب فُتح على جانبيه العديد من النوافذ صغيرة الحجم. يشغل الجزء العلوي من هذه الواجهة شبابيك كبيرة الحجم تنتهي بعقود مدببة، قُصِد منها إنارة وتهوية الطابق الثاني من المصبنة للمساعدة في تجفيف وتهوية الصابون.  
يمكن الوصول إلى الطابق الأول (الأرضي) من المصبنة من خلال باب كبير (تقدَّم وصفه). يتكون هذا الطابق من قاعة طويلة ذات سقف عالٍ يستند على عقود متقاطعة تستند بدورها على دعامات حجرية. يصنع الصابون في هذا الطابق، في مكان رحب يسمَّى بالبلاط. وتتم عملية صنع الصابون في قدر نحاسي كبير. ويوجد بئر يتم فيه حفظ وتخزين الزيت المستخدم لصناعة الصابون. وهناك سلّم يقع في الجهة الجنوبية الشرقية من المصبنة يؤدِّي إلى الطابق الثاني. يتكون الطابق الثاني من قاعة واسعة تسمَّى مفرشاً، وذلك لأنها المكان الذي تفرَش فيه مادة الصابون اللزجة. يتشكَّل سقف هذا الطابق من قباب ضحلة متتالية تستند على عقود تستند بدورها على دعامات.  
تعتبر صناعة الصابون في مدينة نابلس صناعة تقليدية قديمة وهامّة، حيث بلغ عدد المصابن في المدينة في مطلع القرن العشرين حوالي ثلاثين مصبنة. وكان أصحاب المصابن في مدينة نابلس من الزعماء والأشراف والعلماء وكبار التجار. وقد اهتم هؤلاء بالدعاية لصابونهم ممّا أدّى إلى انتشاره في الأسواق الخارجية، خاصة في الدول العربية مثل مصر وسورية.

تقع المصبنة في قلب نابلس القديمة، كواحدة من سلسلة من المصابن التي كانت تعجُّ بها مدينة نابلس، منذ القرن السابع عشر الميلادي. تتكوَّن المصبنة من بناء وظيفي كبير، خال من الزخارف، مستطيل الشكل من طابقين. اشتمل الطابق الأرضي على المكاتب وقدور طبخ الصابون وآبار الزيت، في حين اشتمل الطابق العلوي على قاعة واسعة كثيرة الشبابيك، تستخدم لفرش الصابون لتجفيفه وتقطيعه ولفَّه. وقد اشتهر الصابون النابلسي في كل المشرق العربي، ووصل إلى أوروبا، وعُرف بجودته العالية.
keywords: حسن طوقان؛ صابون؛ صابون نابلسي؛ طوقان؛ مصبنة؛ مصبنة طوقان.

en.name: Tuqan Soap Factory.
description:
The Tuqan Soap Factory is a large, rectangular in plan, two-storey stone building. The principle façade of the building is sparsely decorated. A large portal located on the ground floor level facilitates both the entry of oil used in soap manufacture, as well as the exit of finished soap products. Above the entrance there is a pointed arch, both sides of which are flanked by a number of small-sized windows. The upper section of the façade has been worked into a series of large windows that end with tapered arches. The windows allow light and air into the second floor of the soap factory, assisting in ventilation and facilitating soap drying.  
It is possible to enter the first floor of the factory by means of a large door. This level is composed of a long hall with a high ceiling that is supported by cross-vaults; these in turn are supported by stone piers. The soap is made on this level in a spacious area called *al-balat* (the hall). The oil, used to make the soap, is preserved and stored in a well; the soap-making process itself takes place in a large copper pot.  
A stairwell located on the southeast side of the factory leads to the second level, composed of a wide hall called *al-mafrash* where the sticky soap matter is left to dry. The ceiling on this level forms a series of successive shallow domes supported by arches which, in turn, are supported by columns.  
The soap industry is considered to be a traditional and important one in the city of Nablus, where the number of soap factories at the beginning of the 20th century numbered around 30. Historically the owners of soap factories in Nablus have included political leaders, nobility, powerful merchants and scholars (*'ulama)*. Their active interest in advertising the soap they produced led to a broader market, especially those in the Arab regions such as Egypt and Syria.

The soap factory is located in the heart of old Nablus and is part of the soap industry on which Nablus has thrived since the AH 11th / AD 17th century. It consists of a large, rectangular, functional, two-storey building, devoid of decoration. The ground floor has offices, pots for making the soap and oil wells. The upper storey is composed of a wide hall with many windows which is used to spread out the soap and to dry, cut and wrap it. Nablus soap was renowned throughout the Arab East and also reached Europe. It was known for its high quality.
dates: The end of hegira 13th century / AD 19th century.
keywords: Hasan Tuqan; soap; Nablus soap; soap factory

es.name: Jabonería de la familia Tuqan.
description:
La fábrica de jabón de los Tuqan es un gran edificio rectangular de dos pisos. La fachada principal está prácticamente exenta de decoración. En la planta baja dispone de un gran portal por el que entra el aceite para fabricar el jabón y sale el producto manufacturado. Sobre la entrada presenta un arco apuntado con varias ventanas pequeñas a los lados. La parte superior de la fachada posee una serie de ventanas grandes rematadas con arcos apuntados que permiten la entrada de luz y aire en el segundo piso de la fábrica, lo que contribuye a la ventilación del edificio y el secado del jabón.  
Al primer piso se entra por una puerta de gran tamaño. Este piso consta de un espacio largo de techos altos con bóvedas de crucería que reposan sobre pilares de piedra. Es en este piso donde se hace el jabón, en una sala espaciosa denominada *al-balat* ('el salón'). El aceite con el que se fabrica el jabón se conserva en un pozo. El proceso de elaboración del jabón se lleva a cabo en un enorme caldero de cobre.  
Una escalera que arranca en el lado sureste de la fábrica conduce al segundo piso, que alberga una sala llamada *al-mafrash*, donde se pone a secar el jabón. El techo de este piso presenta una serie de cúpulas bajas que reposan sobre arcos apoyados en columnas.  
La industria del jabón es muy tradicional e importante en la ciudad de Nablús, donde a principios del siglo XX había unas treinta jabonerías. A lo largo de la historia, entre los empresarios jaboneros de Nablús ha habido líderes políticos, nobles, mercaderes poderosos y ulemas. Se emplearon a fondo en dar publicidad de su jabón, lo que les permitió ampliar el mercado, sobre todo a países árabes como Egipto o Siria.

Fábrica de jabón ubicada en el centro de la antigua Nablús. La industria jabonera es muy importante en Nablús desde el siglo XI / XVII. Es un gran edificio funcional, de planta rectangular y dos pisos, carente de decoración. En la planta baja hay oficinas, ollas para fabricar jabón y pozos de aceite. En el piso superior hay un amplio espacio con muchas ventanas en el que se seca, corta y envuelve el jabón. La calidad del jabón de Nablús es notoria en todo el Oriente islámico e incluso en Europa.
dates: Finales del siglo XIII de la Hégira / XIX d. C.
keywords: Hasan Tuqan; jabón; jabón de Nablús; fábrica de jabón.

fr.name: Manufacture de savon de la famille Touqan.
description:
Cette manufacture occupe un vaste bâtiment à étage et de plan carré. Sa façade principale est peu décorée. Le grand portail sert aussi bien à la réception de l'huile utilisée dans la fabrication du savon qu'à la livraison des produits finis. Il s'ouvre sous un arc brisé flanqué de plusieurs petites fenêtres. La partie supérieure de la façade présente une succession de grandes fenêtres prises dans des arcs brisés, qui permettent d'éclairer l'étage et de l'aérer pour accélérer le séchage du savon.  
On peut aussi accéder au rez-de-chaussée par une grande porte. Ce niveau se compose d'une haute et vaste salle (*al-balat*) à voûtes croisées reposant sur des piliers de pierre. Le processus de fabrication s'y déroule dans un énorme chaudron de cuivre. L'huile est stockée dans un puits.  
Au sud-ouest, un escalier conduit à l'étage qui comporte une grande salle appelée *al-mafrach* où le savon est mis à sécher. La couverture est assurée par une série de coupoles soutenues par des arcs reposant sur des colonnes.  
La fabrication du savon est une activité traditionnelle importante de la ville de Naplouse qui comptait encore 30 fabriques au début du XXe siècle. Au cours de l'histoire, les propriétaires de ces entreprises ont compté dans leurs rangs des responsables politiques, des nobles, de grands marchands ou même des érudits (oulémas). La production était destinée à un vaste marché, en particulier à des pays comme l'égypte et la Syrie.

La manufacture de savon est située au cœur du vieux Naplouse et fait partie de l’industrie du savon sur laquelle Naplouse a prospéré depuis le XIe siècle H (XVIIe siècle J.-C.). Elle consiste en un grand bâtiment fonctionnel rectangulaire de deux niveaux, dépourvu de toute décoration. Le rez-de-chaussée comprend des bureaux, des cuves pour la fabrication du savon et des puits pour l’huile. Le niveau supérieur est constitué d’une large salle dotée de nombreuses fenêtres, qui est utilisée pour étaler et pour sécher le savon, le couper et l’emballer. La renommée du savon de Naplouse, apprécié pour sa qualité, était importante dans l’est de la péninsule Arabique et atteignit également l’Europe.
dates: Fin du XIIIe siècle de l'Hégire (XIXe siècle J.-C.).
keywords: Manufacture de savon Hassan Touqan ; savon ; savon de Naplouse ; manufacture de savon

ar.name: جامع سيدي بو مروان.
description:
يقع جامع سيدي بو مروان في مرتفع المدينة القديمة. بُنيت قاعة الصلاة على صخرة، لكن الشرفة التي كانت تحيط بها من الجانبين الشرقي والشمالي تغطي مستويين من الأقبية التي يعتقد أنها سابقة على بناء المسجد. وقد طرأت على صحن المسجد تغييرات عديدة بحيث يتعذر حالياً معرفة الحالة الأولى التي كان عليها. وفي المقابل، تكفي مقارنة الشكل الحالي للمئذنة بالرسوم الموجودة في الطباعة الحجرية القديمة لتكوين فكرة عن الإصلاحات التي شهدتها. ويشير رشيد بورويبة في كتابه "إسهامات الجزائر في العمارة العربية الإسلامية" "Apports de l'Algérie à l'architecture arabo-islamique " إلى قاعة صغيرة للصلاة يمكن الدخول إليها من خلال المئذنة: "إن الصرح الوحيد، حسب علمنا، الذي يضم برجاً مع قاعة صلاة هو برج خلف في سوسة ( …). وبما أن برج خلف لايعد مئذنة، فإنه في وسعنا القول إن جامع سيدي بو مروان هو الجامع الوحيد الذي يضم قاعةً للصلاة في مئذنته".  
قُسمت قاعة الصلاة (19،21 x 19،64 متر) إلى تسع بلاطات وسبعة أساكيب. وثمة أعمدة قديمة تستخدم كدعائم للطيقان الزخرفية، أما تيجان الأعمدة، فتمثل طبليات وقمريات. وتحتضن الدعائم الصغيرة العقود نصف الدائرية الحدوية الشكل. وقد أدى تحويل قاعة الصلاة إلى قاعة مستشفى إلى إحداث تغييرات إذ انضوى صفان من الأعمدة في دعائم ذات قاعدة مربعة، وأدى بناء قاعة عليا إلى تحطيم قبتين: الأولى كانت تعلو وسط الرواق قبالة القاعة، والثانية فوق مقدمة المحراب.

يقعُ هذا المسجد في الجزء العلوي للمدينة القديمة لعنابة. وقد تعرض الباب لتعديلات؛ وبنيت قاعة الصلاة فوق المرتفع الصخري؛ إلا أن الشرفة التي تحيط بجانبيه، الشرقي والشمالي، تغطي مستويين من الأقبية اللذين يُحتمل أنهما سابقين على بناء المسجد. كما عُدل الصحن؛ وقُسمت قاعة الصلاة ذات الشكل القريب من المربع إلى تسع بلاطات وسبعة أساكيب. وتسندُ أعمدةٌ قديمة مع تيجان تعلوها طبليات وقمريات العقودَ. وتشتمل المنارة على قاعة صغيرة للصلاة.
keywords: عمارة دينيّة.

en.name: Sidi Bou Marouan Mosque.
description: The Sidi Bou Marouan mosque is situated in the upper part of the old town. The prayer hall is built on the rock, but the terrace that surrounds it on both the northern and eastern sides is built over two levels of caves that could have existed before the mosque itself. The *sahn* (courtyard) has undergone too many transformations for its original state to be still understood. One can, however, compare the current appearance of the minaret to those portrayed in old lithographs to get an idea of the changes it has been subjected to. R. Bourouiba, in *Apports de l'Algérie à l'architecture arabo-islamique* (see Bibliography), points out a small prayer hall that is accessed through the minaret: 'Only a single monument, to our knowledge, possesses a tower with a prayer hall. It is the Khalaf tower in Sousse … As the Khalaf tower is not a minaret, we can say that the Sidi Bou Marouan mosque is the only mosque that has a prayer hall within its minaret.' The prayer hall (19.21 m x 19.64 m) is divided into nine *balatat* (naves) and seven bays. Ancient columns serve as supports for the arches, and the capitals feature abacuses and imposts, small pillars from which the semi-circular horseshoe arches spring. The transformation of the prayer hall into a hospital ward entailed major changes: two rows of columns were recast into square-based pillars, and the construction of an upper room entailed the destruction of two domes, one of which covered the middle section of the gallery in front of the hall, the other of which crowned the front of the *mihrab*.

This mosque is situated in the upper part of the old town of Annaba and has been modified in the past. The prayer room was built on the rock while the terrace on its north and east sides covers a two-level cellar that may predate it. The courtyard has been altered. The almost square prayer room is divided into nine naves of seven bays. The arches are supported on Antique columns topped with abacuses and imposts. The minaret includes a small prayer room.
keywords: Religious architecture

es.name: Mezquita de Sidi Abu Marwan.
description: La sala de oración está construida sobre la roca, mientras que la terraza que se extiende a lo largo de los lados este y norte cubre dos niveles de cuevas que podrían ser anteriores a la mezquita. El patio (*sahn*) ha sufrido numerosas transformaciones y resulta difícil poder distinguir su estado original. Sin embargo, bastaría comparar el aspecto actual del alminar con el de las litografías antiguas para hacerse una idea de las reformas que ha sufrido. R. Bourouiba, en su libro *Apports de l’Algérie à l’architecture religieuse arabo-islamique*, señala la existencia de una pequeña sala de oración a la que se entraba desde el alminar: “Un solo monumento, que sepamos, ostenta una torre con una sala de oración. Se trata de la torre Jalaf en Susa \[…\]. Como la torre Jalaf no es un alminar, podemos decir que la mezquita de Sidi Abu Marwan es la única mezquita que posee una sala de oración dentro de su alminar”. La sala de oración (19,21 x 19,64 m) está dividida en nueve naves y siete galerías. Columnas de mármol, tomadas de la ciudad romana de Hipona (a unos dos kilómetros al sur), sirven de apoyo a los arcos; los capiteles presentan ábacos e impostas, pequeños pilares que reciben los arcos de herradura. La transformación de la sala de oración en sala de hospital conllevó importantes modificaciones: dos filas de columnas fueron coladas en pilares de base cuadrada, y la construcción de una sala alta tuvo como consecuencia la destrucción de dos cúpulas: una en medio de la galería, delante de la sala; la otra, delante del *mihrab*.

Esta mezquita, ubicada en la parte alta del casco antiguo de la ciudad de Annaba, ha sufrido transformaciones. La sala de oración está construida sobre la roca, mientras que la terraza que se extiende a lo largo de los lados este y norte cubre dos niveles de cuevas que podrían ser anteriores. El patio ha sido modificado. La sala de oración, prácticamente cuadrada, está dividida en nueve naves y siete galerías. Columnas de la Antigüedad, con capiteles que presentan ábacos e impostas, sostienen los arcos. El alminar comprende una pequeña sala de oración.
keywords: Arquitectura religiosa.

fr.name: Mosquée Sidi Bou Merouan.
description: La mosquée Sidi Bou Merouan est située sur la partie haute de la vieille ville. La salle de prière est construite sur le rocher, mais la terrasse qui la borde sur les côtés est et nord couvre deux niveaux de caves qui pourraient être antérieures à la mosquée. Le *sahn* (cour) a subi de trop nombreuses transformations pour que l'état premier en soit encore “lisible”. En revanche, il suffirait de comparer l'aspect actuel du minaret à celui des lithographies anciennes pour avoir une idée des réformes qu'il a connues. R. Bourouiba, dans *Apports de l'Algérie à l'architecture arabo-islamique*, signale une petite salle de prière accessible par le minaret : “Un seul monument, à notre connaissance, possède une tour avec une salle de prière. C'est la tour Khalaf à Sousse (…). Comme la tour Khalaf n'est pas un minaret, nous pouvons dire que la mosquée Sidi Bou Merouan est la seule mosquée à posséder une salle de prière dans son minaret.” La salle de prière (19,21 x 19,64 m) est divisée en neuf *balatat* (nefs) et sept travées. Des colonnes antiques servent de supports aux arcatures, les chapiteaux présentent des abaques et des impostes, petits piliers qui reçoivent les arcs plein cintre outrepassés. La transformation de la salle de prière en salle d'hôpital a entraîné des interventions “lourdes” : deux rangées de colonnes ont été coulées dans des piliers à base carrée, la construction d'une salle haute a entraîné la destruction des deux coupoles : l'une surmontait le milieu de la galerie au-devant de la salle, l'autre au-dessus de l'avant du *mihrab*.

Cette mosquée est située sur la partie haute de la vieille ville d'Annaba. Elle a subi des transformations. La salle de prière est construite sur le rocher, mais la terrasse qui la borde sur les côtés est et nord couvre deux niveaux de caves peut-être antérieures. La cour a été modifiée. La salle de prière presque carrée est divisée en neufs nefs et sept travées. Des colonnes antiques avec chapiteaux surmontés d'abaques et d'impostes supportent les arcs. Le minaret comporte une petite salle de prière.
keywords: architecture religieuse

en.name: Kébili
description:
The al-Jerid Chott  
The al-Jerid Chott, like other chotts bordering on the Maghrebi Sahara, is a depression deepened by wind-erosion, whose ground level is below sea level. Formerly the site of a lake that dried out thousands of years ago, to the traveller it looks like an immense expanse of greyish, hilly land which is covered in patches of dried vegetation. This is only a mirage. The al-Jerid Chott was until recently a trap into which all those venturing without a guide fell. For this reason, chotts have remained of interest and have inspired fear. A small temple, situated north of the al-Jerid Chott, offered protection to those who were planning to cross it. The traveller who returned safe and well felt obliged to offer a sacrifice to the gods of the temple.  
The Arab chroniclers and voyagers did not omit writing about chotts, insisting on the dangers they entailed. According to these accounts, the swampy and unstable chotts swallowed up individuals, caravans and entire armies. Abu al-Hajjaj thought of them as one of the world’s strangest curiosities. A tarmac road built by the Tunisian army around 1970 has since shortened the journey between the Jérid and Kébili.

es.name: KEBILI
description:
Chott el-Yerid  
El chott el-Yerid, como los otros chotts limítrofes al Sahara magrebí, corresponde a una depresión hecha por la erosión del viento y cuyo nivel es inferior al nivel del mar. Antiguamente estaba ocupado por un lago que se secó hace milenios, y se presenta al viajero como una inmensa extensión que se desarrolla en tierra grisácea, cubierta de montículos y de mojones vegetales secos. Esto no es más que un espejismo. El chott el-Yerid era, hasta época reciente, una trampa en la que caían todos aquellos que se aventuraban en él sin guía, a ciegas.  
Por esto los chotts siempre han atraído la atención y han inspirado miedo. Un pequeño templo, situado en el Norte del chott el-Yerid, protegía a los que habían decidido atravesarlo. El viajero que volvía sano y salvo se sentía obligado a ofrecer un sacrificio a los dioses del templo. Los cronistas y viajeros árabes nunca han dejado de mencionar los chotts e insistir en sus peligros. Fangosos e inestables, han engullido individuos, caravanas y ejércitos enteros. Abu el-Hayyay los consideraba como una de las curiosidades más sorprendentes del mundo. Una carretera asfaltada, hecha por el ejército tunecino hacia 1970, ha permitido desde entonces hacer el viaje entre el Yerid y Kebili.

fr.name: KÉBILI
description:
Chott el-Jérid  
Le Chott el-Jérid, comme les autres chotts limitrophes du Sahara maghrébin, correspond à une dépression approfondie par l’érosion éolienne et dont le niveau est inférieur au niveau de la mer. Anciennement occupé par un lac qui s’est asséché depuis des millénaires, il se présente au voyageur comme une immense étendue se déployant en une terre grisâtre, mamelonnée et couverte de touffes végétales desséchées. Ce n’est que l’apparence d’un mirage. Le Chott el-Jérid était jusqu’à une date récente un piège dans lequel s’enlisaient tous ceux qui s’y aventuraient sans guide.  
Les chotts ont, de ce fait, retenu l’attention et inspiré la crainte. Un petit temple, situé au nord du Chott el-Jérid, protégeait ceux qui entreprenaient de le traverser. Le voyageur qui revenait sain et sauf se sentait obligé d’offrir un sacrifice aux dieux du temple.  
Les chroniqueurs et voyageurs arabes n’ont pas manqué de citer les chotts, insistant sur leurs dangers. Boueux, instables, ils ont englouti selon eux des individus, des caravanes et des armées entières. Abou el-Hajjaj les considérait comme étant l’une des curiosités les plus étonnantes du monde. Une route goudronnée construite par l’armée tunisienne vers 1970 a permis dès lors de raccourcir le voyage entre le Jérid et Kébili.

en.name: *Allegorical celebration of the thermal water in Porretta*
description: This painted decoration was created to celebrate the family by enhancing the therapeutic properties of the thermal water which springs in Porretta, a small village on the mountains around Bologna, a feud of the Ranuzzi from 1482. Girolamo Ranuzzi asked the poet Pier Jacopo Martello to create an iconographic programme to translate in painting. Vittorio Bigari and Stefano Orlandi painted the ceiling between 1724 and 1725.

it.name: *Allegoria delle acque termali della Porretta*
description: Per celebrare la propria famiglia attraverso la celebrazione delle virtù terapeutiche dell'acqua termale che sgorga a Porretta, feudo della famigli Ranuzzi dal 1428, Girolamo Ranuzzi chiese al letterato Pier Jacopo Martello di eleborare un programma iconografico da tradurre in pittura. Vittorio Bigari e Stefano Orlandi dipinsero la volta tra il 1724 e il 1725.

ar.name: صحن براق

en.name: *Partium Regni Sclavoniae et Croatiae*
names: Geographical-historical map of the northwest region of Croatia in 1673
description:
A map depicting the northwest region of Croatia with inscriptions and dates that detail the most important battles against the Ottoman Turks in the 15th, 16th and 17th centuries.  
There is a letterpress dedication to Martin Borković, Bishop of Zagreb from 1647 until 1667, and to Count Nikola Erdödy. A signature on the bottom right in a cartouche reads “*per R.P. STEPHANVM GLAVACH” and* “*NOVA hactenus ... SCLAVONIAE et CROATIAE ... Confiniumque Descriptio ... Professorem 1673”.*  
The map is an announcement of the Croatian Counter-Reformation and the beginning of the Baroque style. Made by the Jesuit, Stjepan Glavač the first teacher of logic at Zagreb Jesuit Academy and professor of philosophy, exegesis and controversy at Graz University, its production was the incentive of the Bishop of Zagreb Martin Borković, and the Croatian *ban* (viceroy) Nikola Erdödy.  
The map shows the “remnants of the remnants” of the former Kingdom of Croatia after Ottoman expansion ended. Drawings, made by Glavač while he travelled throughout Croatia accompanied by soldiers and Krajina officers as consultants, decorate the map. The map presents a rare example of decoration in the spirit of the Society of Jesus, shown particularly in the drawings of Mars in armour and the female figures of *Fidelitate constanti* and *Catholica Fide*.

A geographical-historical map of northwest Croatia in 1673, it was drawn by the Jesuit Stjepan Glavač, a teacher at the Zagreb Jesuit Academy and at Graz University. Glavač spent several years travelling through dangerous and inaccessible regions of Croatia accompanied by soldiers and Krajina officers who acted as consultants. The map, showing the “remnants of the remnants” of the former Kingdom of Croatia, and decorated solely with Glavač's drawings, is a rare example of decoration in the spirit of the Society of Jesus.
holder: Metropolitan Library, Valvasor Collection of prints and drawings
place: From the Johann Weichard Valvasor Collection
keywords: Map; chart; Jesuit; university; academy; Ottoman; personification; symbolism; mithology; Christian themes; north-west Croatia; collection; collector

en.name: San Remo: The Conference of the Four Nations
description: San Remo Conference, April 1920. Held after World War I, this conference brought together Britain, France, Italy and Japan to decide the fate of former Ottoman lands. Britain received mandates over Palestine and Mesopotamia (later Iraq), while France gained Syria and Lebanon. Rooted in the Sykes–Picot plan and the Balfour Declaration, these decisions also determined the future of Ottoman infrastructure such as the Hijaz Railway. Strikingly, no representatives from the region were present and the map of the Middle East was redrawn without local voices.

en.name: *The Nightmare of Zahhak*. Miniature from the *Shahnama* of Shah Tahmasp
description: This Safavid folio once belonged to the so-called *Shahnama* of Shah Tahmasp (r. AH 930-984 / AD 1524-1576). It is probably the most luxurious and celebrated Shahnama manuscript ever produced for a royal patron. This painting depicts the tyrant Zahhak as he wakes up terrified from a nightmare announcing his death by the hands of the Iranian hero Faridun. His scream has awakened the entire palace. The *Shahnama*, composed in the AH 5th century / AD early 11th century, remains a nation epic of Iran.

ar.name: طغراء (التوقيع الرسمي ) للسلطان سليمان الكبير (حكم خلال 1520-66)
description: إن الطغراءات العثمانية هي تخطيط لشعارات الدولة ممثلة لسلطة السلطان وكانت تتضمن في كل الوثائق الرسمية بما فيها الفرمان (المراسيم السلطانية ) وأوراق الوقف ، المراسلات ، والقطع النقدية . وقد استخدمت من قبل أول سلطان عثماني في عام 1324 وطورت لاحقا إلى شكل أكثر تعقيدا الذي لم يكن من السهل قراءته أو نسخه. وهذا المثال عبارة عن الأحرف الأولى من اسم السلطان سليمان الكبير (حكم خلال 1520-66) وإن شكله ذو الطراز الخاص هو تشكيل تخطيطي معقد يتضمن اسم وألقاب السلطان واسم والده وعبارة ""المنتصر أبدا"" . وإن الخط الثخين الدلالي يتباين مع التحلية بلفات الكرمة الملتفة كزخرفة وهذه الطغراء عبارة عن ترويسة لوثيقة طويلة ضيقة بشكل ملفوف والسطر الأول فيها مكتوب بخط ذهبي في أسفل الصفحة.

en.name: *Tughra* (official signature) of Sultan Süleyman the Magnificent (r. 1520–66)
description: Ottoman *tughra*s are calligraphic emblems of the sultan's authority and were included in all official documents, including *firman*s (royal decrees), endowment papers, correspondence, and coins. Used by the first Ottoman sultan in 1324, they later developed into a more complex form that was not easily read or copied. This example served as the monogram of Sultan Süleyman the Magnificent (r. 1520–66). Its stylised form is an intricate calligraphic composition comprising the name and titles of the sultan, his father's name, and the phrase “the eternally victorious”. Its bold, gestural line contrasts with the delicate, swirling vine scroll illumination as ornamentation. This *tughra* served as the heading for a long, narrow document in scroll form, the first line of which is preserved in golden script at the bottom of the page.

ar.name: صينية معدنية كبيرة عليها منظر لمكة
description: الصينية المعدنية الكبيرة ذات الإطار الملفوف مرسوم عليها منظر لمكة والمسجد الحرام والمشهد محاط بباقات زهور على أرضية خضراء ناصعة. وربما القطعة قد صنعت في القرن التاسع عشر في أوربا للسوق العثمانية. وهذا الطراز من الصواني كان يصنع مع صور في وسطه تظهر مواقع مهمة في إسطنبول ، التي تجعل هذا المنظر فريدا بشكل خاص.إن تصوير مكة واضح ومدهش وبعض المواقع المهمة في الجوار مرسومة أيضا كأبنية صغيرة وقباب والتي تتضمن مقبرة المعلا (أسفل اليسار) و المسجد (أعلى اليسار) الذي يوجد في غار حراء أعلى جبل النور وهو المكان الذي كان فيه يتنزل الوحي على النبي محمد في بدء الرسالة.

en.name: A large metal tray with a view of Mecca
description:
This large metal tray with scalloped rim is painted with a view of Mecca and the Masjid al-Haram surrounded by floral bouquets on a bright green ground. It was probably made in the 19th century in Europe for the Ottoman market. This style of tray was often made with central depictions illustrating significant locations in Istanbul, which makes this view particularly unique.  
The depiction of Mecca is clear and striking, some significant locations in the vicinity depicted as small buildings and domes, including the Mu‘alla graveyard (to the bottom left) and a mosque (to the top left) which used to stand at the cave of Hira on top of Jabal al-Nur, the place where Prophet Muhammad received his first revelation.
holder: Khalili Family Trust – Hajj and the Arts of Pilgrimage Collection

In one of the streets in the Trocadero Pavilion buildings were constructed based on those built in Algeria after the French-Prussian war (1870–71) by the Society Protecting Alsatian and Lorenese People for refugees coming from France. The interior shows all the territories donated to the Protecting Society and in the lower part the villages of Hanssonvillers and Bacckhalfa.

en.name: *Interior of a school, Cairo*
short_description: In this scene depicted by Lewis, the Hoja or teacher is listening to his assistant rhythmically reciting the Quran (while beating time), as some children pay attention and others not. Some commentators have regarded the presence of a young girl as inauthentic, but young girls were able to attend Quran schools, according to the artist Charles de Tournemine, the scholar Edward Lane and the translator Richard Burton. Certainly not all women were illiterate, and some female descendants of the prophet were noted for their ability to read and recite the scriptures.
keywords: education; school; teaching; children; childhood; kuttab

en.name: 'Scorpion' rug
description: Standing in distinct contrast to the typically red and blue colours of Ottoman Turkish carpets are the 'white' rugs, whose fields are created using undyed wool, which is an ivory or light beige colour. They have a maximum of 5–8 colours (usually white, red, blue, yellow and brown), but also can include manganese violet, green and pink, with low knot density, between 621 and 837. They are subdivided by pattern as "ball" or "çintamani", "bird" and "scorpion" white rugs. Referred to in Hungarian historical sources as *fejér* (white) carpets, they were popular in 16–17th century Hungary, and particularly in Transylvania (now part of Romania). The rarest version of white rugs has a motif reminiscent of a stylised scorpion, seen by some as a crab. They are known as "scorpion" rugs. Four scorpion rugs are known of Transylvanian origin. Apart from the Budapest rug, there are two in Transylvania (in the collections of the Black Church in Braşov and of the St Margaret Church in Mediaş), and one in the Keir Collection in London. The main field of the rug is divided into two rectangles by narrow columns of arrowhead rods linked to round rosettes in the centre and the two edges. Palmettes reminiscent of a stylised scorpion or crab arranged in varying orientations and colours in a vertical column alternate with each other in the rectangles.
keywords: Ottoman rug; Wool
materials: Pile: wool; Symmetrical (Turkish or Ghiordes) knot

ar.name: سجادة التنين
description:
يهيمن على الساحة المركزية الكبيرة للسجادة هيكلان شبكيان متشابكان (أبيض وأزرق) موضوعان على أرضية حمراء مع سعيفات منمقة موضوعة لتحديد نقاط تقاطعهما. اسم تصميم السجادة مستمد من إدراج تنين متعرج يملأ نصف الحقول الغائرة ذات الشكل المعيني. في هذا المثال، يمتلئ النصف الآخر من الحقول بزخارف يمكن فهمها على أنها تمثل سعيفات. تحيط حدود ضيقة من الزخارف على شكل حرف Z بالمجال المركزي.  
  
في حين وجد التنين الصيني طريقه إلى فن العالم الإسلامي في وقت مبكر من القرن الثالث عشر، فقد تم تصنيع سجاد التنين من هذا النوع في جنوب القوقاز منذ حوالي القرن السابع عشر فصاعدًا. وتجدر الإشارة أيضًا إلى أوجه التشابه الهيكلية مع السجاد الفارسي ذو المزهرية في ذلك الوقت. إن الأسلوب القوي لهذه السجادة، والذي يمتد في بعض الحالات إلى درجة لا يمكن معها التعرف على الزخارف، يشير إلى أن السجادة تعود إلى أواخر القرن الثامن عشر.
dates: أواخر القرن 12 الهجري/ أواخر القرن 18 الميلادي

en.name: *Dragon* carpet
description:
The large central field of the carpet is dominated by two interlocked lattice structures (white and blue) set onto a red ground with stylised palmettes placed to mark their points of intersection. The carpet design's name derives from the inclusion of a sinuous dragon which fills half of the recessed diamond-shaped fields. In this example, the other half of the fields are filled with motifs that can be understood as representing palmettes. A narrow border of Z-shaped motifs encloses the central field.  
  
Whilst the Chinese dragon found its way into the art of the Islamic world as early as the 13th century, dragon carpets of this kind were made in the southern Caucasus from around the 17th century onwards. The structural parallels to Persian vase carpets of that time is also noteworthy. The strong stylisation of this carpet, which in some cases extends to the point where the motifs are unrecognisable, suggests that the carpet dates from the later 18th century.
dates: Hegira late 12th century / AD late 18th century

en.name: Astronomical Observatory of Lisbon Polytechnic School
names: Observatório Astronómico da Escola Politécnica de Lisboa
short_description: The Astronomical Observatory is a teaching observatory. It includes one classroom and three observation domes. It dates from 1898 and it encompasses three buildings. The main building is octagonal in shape, located in the upper part of the Botanical Garden. Inside, it has a classroom and the Meridian Room, all covered in wood panels. Another building, with three-floors, used to host the library, more classrooms and workshops. The Observatory collection includes c. 150 scientific instruments, including several apparatuses built in house by Portuguese astronomer Campos Rodrigues (1836–1919).
holder: National Museum of Natural History and Science (MUHNAC) / Museums of the University of Lisbon
artist: Vitor Augusto Gomes da Encarnação (19th century) and José Cecílio da Costa (19th century)
history: Teaching of Astronomy existed in the Lisbon Polytechnic School since its creation in 1837. It was aimed at providing training for cartography surveys. Initially, teaching was done at the so-called Marine Tower (1837–1843) and then at the Royal Maritime Observatory (1843–1875). In 1876, a new Observatory was inaugurated in the Garden. However, the first building had low stability and a new one had to be constructed. Astronomy teaching started in 1898. Until the 1930s, the Observatory was autonomous within the School, but later it was put under the jurisdiction of the Department of Mathematics. In 1999 teaching was discontinued and the Observatory was integrated in the Museum.
keywords: Observatory; Scientific Heritage; Teaching; Astronomy; National Museum of Natural History and Science; University of Lisbon

de.name: Kassettendecke
description: Wohl von einem im Profanbau geschulten Meister wurde im Langhaus eine mit Rechteck- und Achteckfeldern sowie vergoldeten Rosetten gestaltete hölzerne Kassettendecke geschaffen. Aufgrund der Kleinteiligkeit und Verschachtelung der Felder war sie wohl nie für ein Bildprogramm vorgesehen. Dennoch verleiht sie dem Raum den Charakter eines Festsaals und unterstreicht dadurch die Wirkung der Altäre.

en.name: Panelled ceiling
description: Presumably the work of master craftsmen schooled in secular architecture, the nave features a wooden panelled ceiling composed of rectangular and octagonal panels and gilded rosettes. Due to the intricacy and interlacing of the panels it was never intended for a programme of pictures. Nevertheless, it lends the space the character of a festive hall and heightens the impression generated by the altars.

en.name: Algerian Pavilion in the Trocadéro Park [Paris Exhibition, 1878]
short_description: At the International Exhibition in Paris, 1878, the Algerian Pavilion was designed by the architect M. Wable, who was appointed by General Chanzy. The building represents one of the greatest proofs of French colonisation policy. The front-door, four metres wide, is a copy from the ‘Ubbad Mosque of Sidi Bumadyan in Tlemcen, and is richly decorated with enamelled majolica and arabesque decorations. The decorations of the minaret echo the tower in ruins from the mosque of Mansoura, 1,200 square metres wide. The pavilion was meant to show the productive potential of the colony to the French capitalists.
