en.name: Sidi Tuati Mosque
description:
Situated at the entrance to Tamerza, at the start of the axial street, the Sidi Tuati Mosque is composed of a prayer hall, a mausoleum where the saint rests, and of rooms reserved for visitors. The prayer hall is distinct for the orientation of its *mihrab* towards the east, contrary to Muslim norms. One can explain this anomaly if one compares this mosque to churches. Was it originally a church, or did it copy one? These are valid questions if one refers to the writings of al-Tijani, a traveller of the 8th/14th century. According to him, for a long time the Arabs tolerated the churches that were present in the Jérid, they even authorised the construction of a mosque next to each one.  
The prayer-hall roof, made of palm-tree wood, is supported by arches resting on indented brick capitals and palm-tree trunk columns, cut octagonally. A piece of apricot-tree wood, functioning as a cushion support, separates each capital from its column, both made of different materials. The use of palm-tree wood to support structures was most widespread in the Jérid. This use slowly decreased in favour of brick and stone. Therefore, the wooden columns made of palm tree in the Sidi Tuati Mosque represent a rare example of its kind in the region. Their octagonal form is even rarer. Could it be a result of foreign influence?  
Octagonal pillars transport us to the 12th/18th century, which saw the Italian introduction of this kind of pillar, but in marble. Their use, as much in religious architecture as in the domestic architecture of Tunis, took off a little later throughout the rest of the country. The mausoleum, architecturally different from the prayer hall, is, no doubt, of more recent origin. Its interest lies in its ovoidal dome. This shape recalls that of Sidi al-Kharassani in al-Mahassin and that of Sidi bel-‘Abbes in Nefta. This type of dome, which is non-existant if not rare outside the Jérid, is, according to art historians, descended from Oriental art. One can find examples of it particularly in Persia, Yemen and Egypt.

es.name: Mezquita Sidi Tuwati
description:
Situada a la entrada de Tamerza, al comienzo de la calle axial, la mezquita Sidi Tuwati está formada por una sala de oración, el mausoleo donde reposa el santo y algunas habitaciones reservadas al alojamiento de los visitantes.  
La sala de oración se distingue por la orientación de su *mihrab* hacia el este, contrariamente a las normas musulmanas. No se puede encontrar una explicación a esta anomalía más que si entendemos que esta mezquita pudo ser antes una iglesia. ¿Era acaso una iglesia en su origen? Podemos hacernos esta pregunta si retenemos los testimonios de el-Tiyani, viajero del siglo VIII/XIV: “Los árabes —decía— han tolerado por mucho tiempo las iglesias en el Yerid; incluso han autorizado la construcción de una mezquita cerca de cada una de ellas”.  
La cubierta de la sala de oración, en madera de palmera, está soportada por arcos que descansan sobre capiteles dentados de ladrillo y columnas octogonales de palmera. Un cojín de madera de albaricoque, que hace el papel de amortiguador, separa cada capitel de su columna, cada uno de diferente forma. La utilización de la madera de palmera como soporte era la más difundida en el Yerid; pero poco a poco ha dejado de emplearse, ante la utilización del ladrillo y de la piedra. Así, las columnas de madera de palmera de la mezquita Sidi Tuwati representan un ejemplo raro en esta región. Su forma octogonal es aún más extraña. ¿Es acaso una influencia extranjera?  
Los pilares octogonales nos muestran cómo en el siglo XII/XVIII se introdujo este género de pilar italiano, aunque en mármol. Su utilización, tanto en la arquitectura religiosa como en la doméstica de Túnez, llegó algo más tarde al interior del país.  
El mausoleo es de factura diferente a la sala de oración, por lo que se entiende que es más reciente. Su interés reside en su cúpula ovoide. Esta forma recuerda la de Sidi el-Jarasani en el-Mahasin y la de Sidi Belabbas en Nefta. Este género de cúpula, casi inexistente fuera del Yerid, revela, según ciertos historiadores, el arte oriental. Lo encontramos particularmente en Persia, en el Yemen y en Egipto.

fr.name: Mosquée Sidi Touati
description:
Située à l’entrée de Tamerza, au commencement de la rue axiale, la mosquée Sidi Touati est formée d’une salle de prière, celle du mausolée où repose le saint, et de chambres réservées au séjour des visiteurs. La salle de prière se distingue par l’orientation de son *mihrab* vers l’est, contrairement aux normes musulmanes. On ne peut trouver une explication à cette anomalie que si on rapproche cette mosquée des églises. En était-elle une à son origine, ou a-t-elle copié l’une d’elles? On peut se poser ces questions si on retient les témoignages d’el-Tijani, voyageur du VIIIe/XIVe siècle. Les Arabes, d’après lui, ont toléré pendant longtemps les églises au Jérid. Ils y ont même autorisé la construction d’une mosquée auprès de chacune d’elles.  
La couverture de la salle de prière, en bois de palmier, est supportée par des arcs reposant sur des chapiteaux dentelés en briques et des colonnes en troncs de palmiers taillés octogonalement. Un coussin de bois d’abricotier, jouant le rôle d’amortisseur, sépare chaque chapiteau de sa colonne, tous les deux de natures différentes. L’utilisation du bois de palmier comme support était la plus répandue au Jérid. Elle a peu a peu reculé devant l’utilisation de la brique et de la pierre. Ainsi les colonnes en bois de palmier de la mosquée Sidi Touati représentent un spécimen rare dans cette région. Leur forme octogonale est encore plus rare. Résulte-t-elle d’une influence étrangère?  
Les piliers orthogonaux nous portent au XIIe/XVIIIe qui a vu l’introduction d’Italie de ce genre de pilier, mais en marbre. Leur utilisation, aussi bien dans l’architecture religieuse que domestique de Tunis, a gagné un peu plus tard l’intérieur du pays. Le mausolée, d’une architecture différente de la salle de prière, est sans doute plus récent. Son intérêt réside dans sa coupole de forme ovoïdale. Cette forme rappelle celle de Sidi el-Kharassani à el-Mahassin et de Sidi bel-Abbes, à Nefta. Ce genre de coupole, inexistant, sinon rare en dehors du Jérid, relève, selon certains historiens, de l’art oriental. On le trouve particulièrement en Perse, au Yémen et en Egypte.

ar.name: زهرية أو حامل
description: هذه القطعة عبارة عن زهرية ذات جسم بشكل عامود مصنوع بالخراطة. والفوهة/الفم واسعة وجزء كبير منها مخرم بشكل زخرفة مكررة. ويحمل العنق نطاقا ذو نقش ربما يعبر عن أمنيات طيبة لمالك القطعة.وأسفل ذلك يرى تزيين من دوائر مصمتة متناوبة وتشغيل مخرم وشرائط ملتفة على بعضها. وحول الجسم تبدي الزهرية صفين من الأسنان / الثقوب الدائرية المقعرة. وفيما بينها توجد رصائع دائرية صغيرة بحيث أن كل اثنتين تبديان زخرفة مشابهة لعقدة سليمان ولكن بنهايات منحنية/ملتفة. والقدم لا تبدي أي تزيين وبدلا من ذلك فإن إطارها قد قطع حيث أنه أصابه البلى وغير متساوي.إن مجموعة من القطع المشابهة تماما تبدي قدما تشبه قعرا بشكل الجرس وعالي الارتفاع. وقد قيل بأن القطعة الحالية كان لها سابقا حلية مشابهة. والقاعدة كانت مصنوعة من صفيحة منفصلة وبعدها وصلت مع الزهرية. من المدهش أن هناك تقريبا قطعة مطابقة تقريبا لهذه القطعة وهي موجودة في متحف ليندن في شتوتغارت ( LM VL 95/6).

en.name: Vase or Stand
description:
This is a vase with a baluster-shaped body, sometimes referred to as pear-shaped.  
The mouth is wide and a great part of it is openwork of a repetitive ornamental motif. The neck bears a belt with an inscription, probably stating good wishes for the owner. Below that, a decor of alternating solid circles and open-worked, intertwining ribbons can be seen. Around the body, the vase shows two rows of concave circular dents. In between those are small circular medallions, with every second one showing an ornament similar to the Solomon’s knot, but with curled ends. The foot does not show any decoration. Instead the rim of it was cut, as it is frayed and uneven. A group of fairly similar objects exhibit a rather high and bell-bottom-like foot. It is suggested, that the artifact at hand once possessed a similar feature. The base was made from a separate plate and then fused onto the vase.  
Interestingly, there is one almost identical piece to this one. It is stored in the Linden-Museum, Stuttgart (LM VL 96/5).
holder: University Museum of Islamic Art | The Bumiller Collection
keywords: Metalwork; vase; stand; openwork; rim
partner: University Museum of Islamic Art | The Bumiller Collection

en.name: "The Clever Hare with the King of the Elephants at the Spring of the Moon"
names: Folio from a Kalila wa Dimna
description: This manuscript contains seventy-eight paintings and many text folios telling the famous tales of the jackals Kalila and Dimna. Based on the book of ancient Indian animal fables, the Panchatantra written by Vidyapati (Bidpai), the stories spread all over the Middle East where they became wildly popular. This manuscript has a strong flavour of Mamluk Egypt in the figure styles and bold drawings, with hints of Ottoman tulips and Safavid turbans. However, the burnt orange palette and darkly-inked lines have led to an attribution to Sultanate Gujarat where it is suggested this manuscript was copied from an Egyptian original. Its life in India is also attested by a Devanagari inscription at the end, although the rest of the Arabic text is written in a strong, left-leaning naskh-like script.
dates: AH second quarter of the 10th century / AD second quarter 16th century

en.name: Dish with artichokes and tulips
description: Beginning sometime in the Hegira 950s / AD 1540s Iznik potters introduced manganese purple, sage green and black to their palette, while their decorative repertoire continued to focus on floral designs such as pomegranates, rosettes, tulips and artichokes. The latter two motifs form the main decoration at the centre of this large dish, where they are depicted in blue and green, while the cavetto and rim bear green pomegranates alternating with blue sprays of leaves or else tulips.
holder: Los Angeles County Museum of Art (LACMA)
keywords: Ceramic; Ottoman ceramic; Iznik pottery; floral decoration
partner: Los Angeles County Museum of Art (LACMA)

en.name: Caparison for a horse given by the Sultan of Morocco to the King of Italy, on the occasion of a visit to Italy of a Moroccan Ambassador in 1890
short_description:
In 1890, the Sultan of Morocco sent Hagi El Maati el Mazamizi as an Ambassador to Italy. The Ambassador landed in Naples on June 7th and arrived by train in Rome on June 13th. At the railway station, he was received by the Mayor of Rome, the Prefect, and other authorities. A military band was playing and military men in high uniform were paraded in the station to greet the Ambassador.  
Outside the station, three of the King’s gala carriages were waiting for the Ambassador and a military unit was paraded in his honour. Some carabinieri in high uniform escorted the Ambassador to the hotel.  
Hagi El Maati el Mazamizi presented the King with gifts, including some superb horses that the King immensely appreciated. The King presented the Ambassador with a magnificent small gold and diamonds small box and a hunting rifle and gave gold watches to the members of his escort.
holder: National Museum of Prehistory and Ethnography
partner: MIBACT | National Museum of Prehistory and Ethnography “Luigi Pigorini”

ar.name: لوح مستطيل، عليه نقش جنائزي باللغة العربية بالخط الكوفي.
description:
لوح من الرخام، مستطيل الشكل، مقطوع من الأسفل، مزخرف بإطار مستطيل نافر، فوقه قوس(منفوخ) يشبه حدوة الحصان. وبين الإطار والقوس ثمة رسوم متناظرة لنبات له ثلاثة براعم، تشبه اللوزة، يحيط بها أوراق نباتات صغيرة تشبه صورة القلب وتشكل دوائر متداخلة.  
أما الخط الكوفي فهو في داخل الإطار المذكور آنفاً ومن النوع التقليدي الذي يجمع لامات كلمة الله المقدسة، ويجعلها على شكل ورقة نباتية ورسوم شجر النخيل؛ والأوراق الملتفة حول جذوعها تشبه رسوم شواهد قبور مدينة القيروان في القرن الحادي عشر.  
أما العبارات المكتوبة بالخط الكوفي فهي قوله تعالى: ﴿ بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم﴾﴿ كُلُّ نَفْسٍ ذَآئِقَةُ الْمَوْتِ وَإِنَّمَا تُوَفَّوْنَ أُجُورَكُمْ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ فَمَن زُحْزِحَ عَنِ النَّارِ وَأُدْخِلَ الْجَنَّةَ فَقَدْ فَازَ وَما الْحَيَاةُ الدُّنْيَا إِلاَّ مَتَاعُ الْغُرُورِ﴾( 3/ آل عمران/185).هذا جثمان عبد الكريم بن سليمان الزاهد، رحمه الله، الذي توفي يوم السبت الحادي عشر\[...... \] سنة أربع مائة وأربع وسبعين"  
التاريخ غير مقروء بشكل واضح، قدره السيد م.أماري بـ: يوم السبت الحادي عشر من سنة 1474 من شهر ربيع الثاني أو شهر رمضان : أي 18/9/1081 أو 12/2/1082.

تقدم هذه الشاهدة الجنائزية نقيشة كتابية داخل عقد يستحضر مشكاة محراب من أجل التذكير بأن الموت ممر؛ وأن القبر طقس عبور.  وجريا على العادة، فإن الشواهد الجنائزية تحوي عبارات نموذجية مأخوذة من القرءان، وتخلد أيضا فضائل وتقوى الميت.
keywords: خط كوفي؛ شاهدة قبر؛ نقش

en.name: Rectangular slab with Arabic funerary inscription in *kufic* characters
description:
Rectangular marble slab, damaged at the base, decorated with a filleted rectangular frame and a horseshoe arch (*mânfukh*) that delimits the top of the inscribed area. The space between the extrados of the arch and the rectangular frame is filled with two symmetrical decorative elements: a three-petal flower with a central almond-shaped element, and lateral spirals, surrounded by a heart-shaped stem, from the base of which grow two tendrils that creep around the resulting space. The *kufic* characters include the characteristic presence of the trefoil motif linking the two *lam* of the sacred name. The motif of the palmette surrounded by heart-shaped stems is similar to the decoration on the 11th-century funerary stelae from Kairouan.  
The text of the inscription reads (translation by M. Amari – see Bibliography): ‘In the name of God the merciful and compassionate. God bless the prophet Muhammad and his offspring and give them peace. Say: this is a grave notice, from which you flee. Whoever misses Hell, barely, and makes it to Paradise, has attained a great triumph. The life of this world is no more than an illusion. This is the tomb of ‘Abd al-Karim ibn Sulaiman the Ascetic, God have mercy on him. He died on Saturday the eleventh … of the year four hundred and seventy-four’.  
The date, partially lost, has been reconstructed by Amari on the basis of the coincidence of Saturday with the eleventh of the month, which in AH 474 happened in the months of *Rabi II* and *Ramadan*, or 18 September 1081 and 12 February 1082.

This stele bears an inscription inside an arch reminiscent of the *mihrab* niche, evoking the idea of death as a journey and burial as a rite of passage. Traditionally, sepulchral stelae include common formulas taken from the Qur’an alongside celebrations of the virtue and devotion of the deceased.
keywords: kufic; calligraphy; funerary stele; funerary inscription; gravestone

es.name: Lápida funeraria con inscripción cúfica.
description:
Lápida rectangular de mármol deteriorada en la parte inferior. Está decorada con un marco rectangular fileteado y un arco de herradura *(manfuj)* que cierra el campo epigráfico por arriba. El espacio entre el extradós del arco y el marco rectangular está ocupado por elementos decorativos simétricos: una flor de tres pétalos con un motivo central en forma de almendra y volutas laterales, rodeada por un tallo que dibuja un corazón y de cuya base surgen dos zarcillos que penetran en el espacio resultante. En cuanto a los caracteres cúficos, resulta característica la presencia del motivo de tres hojas que enlaza las dos *lam* del nombre sagrado. El motivo de la palmeta rodeada por el tallo en forma de corazón tiene antecedentes en la decoración de estelas funerarias del siglo V / XI de Kairuán.  
El texto de la inscripción, según la traducción de M. Amari, es el siguiente: “En el nombre de Dios el Misericordioso, el Clemente. Que Dios bendiga al profeta Muhammad y a su estirpe y les conceda la paz. Di: Este anuncio que rehuís es serio. Quien sea alejado del fuego e introducido en el Paraíso, se salvará. La vida de aquí abajo no es sino una ilusión. Este es el sepulcro de Abd al-Karim ibn Sulayman, el Asceta, que Dios tenga misericordia de él; que murió el día sábado, once \[…\] del año cuatrocientos setenta y cuatro».  
La fecha, conservada sólo parcialmente, fue reconstruida por Amari a partir de la coincidencia del día de la semana con el 11 del mes, durante el año 474, en los meses de rabi II y ramadán. Por lo tanto, el 18 de septiembre de 1801 o el 12 de febrero de 1082.

La lápida presenta una inscripción dentro de un arco, que emula el nicho de un *mihrab* para evocar la idea de la muerte como paso y de la sepultura como rito de paso.  
Tradicionalmente, las estelas funerarias contienen fórmulas típicas extraídas del Corán junto con la exaltación de las virtudes y la devoción del difunto.
dates: Año 474 de la Hégira / 1081-1082 d. C.
keywords: lápida funeraria; caracteres cúficos; estela funeraria; inscripción funeraria

fr.name: Stèle rectangulaire avec inscription funéraire en caractères coufiques.
description:
Plaque de marbre rectangulaire, mutilée dans sa partie inférieure, décorée d'un cadre rectangulaire à listel et d'un arc en fer à cheval délimitant, en haut, l'espace épigraphique. L'espace entre l'extrados de l'arc et le cadre rectangulaire est occupé par deux éléments décoratifs symétriques (à droite comme à gauche, une même grosse fleur à trois pétales, avec élément central en forme d'amande et des volutes latérales) et enveloppé par une tige dessinant un cœur, dont la base laisse échapper deux vrilles qui s'insinuent dans l'espace de réserve. En ce qui concerne les caractères coufiques, la présence du motif trifolié reliant les deux *lam* du nom sacré est très caractéristique. Le motif de palmette entouré d'une tige en forme de cœur se retrouve dans le décor des stèles funéraires du Ve siècle H (XIe siècle J.-C.) à Kairouan.  
Le texte de l'inscription est le suivant (traduction d'après M. Amari) : “Au nom de Dieu miséricordieux et clément. Que Dieu bénisse le prophète Mahomet et sa lignée et leur accorde la paix. Dis : ceci est une annonce grave, que vous fuyez. Alors, celui qui sera éloigné du feu et introduit au Paradis sera sauvé. La vie ici-bas n'est qu'une marchandise trompeuse. Ceci est le sépulcre d'Abd al-Karim ibn Sulayman, l'Ascétique, que Dieu l'ait en miséricorde ; lequel est mort le jour de samedi, onze (---) de l'an quatre cent soixante-quatorze.” La date, qui n'est pas conservée intégralement, est reconstituée par Amari en fonction de la coïncidence du samedi avec le 11 d'un mois qui, pour l'année 474, ne peut être que *rabi' II* ou *ramadan* ; donc, le 18 septembre 1081 ou le 12 février 1082.

Cette stèle présente une inscription à l'intérieur d'un arc, qui évoque la niche d'un *mihrab* afin de rappeler que la mort est un *passage*, et la sépulture un *rite de passage*. Traditionnellement, les stèles funéraires contiennent des formules typiques tirées du Coran ainsi que la célébration des vertus et de la piété du défunt.
keywords: stèle funéraire ; caractères coufiques; inscription funéraire ; pierre tombale

it.name: lastra rettangolare con iscrizione funeraria araba in caratteri cufici.
description: lastra di marmo rettangolare, mutila in basso, decorata con una cornice rettangolare a listello, e con un arco a ferro di cavallo (mânfukh) che chiude in alto il campo epigrafico. Lo spazio tra l'estradosso dell'arco e l'incorniciatura rettangolare è riempito da due elementi decorativi simmetrici: un fiorone a tre petali con elemento centrale a forma di mandorla, e volute laterali, avvolto da uno stelo con andamento cuoriforme, dalla cui base emergono due viticci che si insinuano all'interno dello spazio di risulta. Per i caratteri cufici, risulta caratteristica la presenza del motivo trifoliato che collega i due lam del nome sacro. Il motivo a palmetta circondato da stelo cuoriforme trova confronti nelle decorazioni delle stele funerarie di XI secolo a Kairouan. Il testo dell'iscrizione è il seguente (traduzione di M. Amari): “Nel nome di Dio misericordioso e clemente. Benedica Dio il profeta Maometto e la sua stirpe e dia loro pace. Dì: questo è annuncio grave, da cui voi rifuggite. Allora chi sarà allontanato dal fuoco e introdotto nel Paradiso, sarà salvo. La vita di quaggiù non è che merce d'inganno. Questo è il sepolcro di 'Abd al-Karîm ibn Sulaiman, l'Ascetico, che Dio abbia misericordia di lui; il quale è morto il giorno di sabato, undici [---] dell'anno quattrocentosettantaquattro”. La data, non del tutto conservata, è ricostruita da Amari in base alla coincidenza del giorno di sabato con l'11 del mese, che si verificò, nell'anno 474, nei mesi di rabi' secondo e di ramadan: dunque, il 18 settembre 1081 o il 12 febbraio 1082.

La stele presenta un'iscrizioni entro un arco, che rievoca la nicchia di un *mihrâb* perrichiamare l'idea della morte come *passaggio*, e della sepoltura come *rito di passaggio*. Tradizionalmente, le stele sepolcrali contengono formule tipiche tratte dal Corano insieme alla celebrazione delle virtù e della devozione del defunto.
holder: collezione G.M. Di Ferro, Trapani (1830 circa).
keywords: stele funeraria; caratteri cufici; calligrafia; iscrizione funeraria; pietra tombale

en.name: *The Battle of Abukir 1799*
short_description: During the French occupation of Egypt, in fact three battles centered on the area around Abukir (Abu Qir), a town on the Mediterranean northeast of Alexandria. The first, in 1798, was a naval battle in which the French were defeated devastatingly by the British navy under the command of Rear Admiral Horatio Nelson. The second battle – shown here – marked a decisive confrontation between Ottoman troops under the command of Sayyid Mustapha Pasha, shipped to Egypt by the British navy, and the occupying French forces led by Napoleon Bonaparte. On the 14th of July 1799, the Ottomans stormed Abukir’s harbor and briefly took control of the city, only to be rebuffed and decisively defeated by the French eleven days later. The scene here appears to mark the moment of surrender. Napoleon Bonaparte, seated on a white horse and surrounded by his officers  is supplicated by Ottoman figures, while fighting still goes on and the smoke of battle continues to billow all around. At sea lie the ships of the British navy – unable to intervene.  The last battle fought near Abukir in 1801 between the French and British helped to prepare the ground for France’s final expulsion from Egypt.
holder: Sharjah Art Museum / Sharjah Museums Department
place: Published around 1820 by Carle Vernet in his Album *Campagnes des Francais sous le Consulat et L´Empire*
artist: J. Couche; J. F. J. Swebach; Francois Dequevauvillers
keywords: Abukir; Abu Qir; Horatio Nelson; Sayyid Mustapha Pasha; Napoleon Bonaparte

en.name: Town, mosque and madrasa
names: Ma’arrat al-Nu’man: the town, great mosque and madrasa
description:
Ma’arrat al-Nu’man is a good example of a frontier town, lying on the crossroads between Aleppo, Antioch, Hama and Homs and witness to much medieval warfare. Having been recovered by the Seljuqs, and then governed by the Ayyubids, the town experienced a period of reprieve. Its main monuments reflect the Islamic artistic and architectural styles of this period.  
The town is a minor one, named after Nu’man bin Bashir al-Ansari, the companion of the Prophet and governor of the region under the Umayyads. Because of its coveted strategic position in northern Syria, the town was conquered repeatedly during the medieval period. Throughout the 4th/10th and 5th/11th centuries, the town was subjugated by the Hamdanids, Byzantines, Fatimids, Seljuqs and Mirdasids successively and became the preferred target of the Franks during the First Crusade. It suffered a very difficult period of war and famine, particularly during the Crusader siege of 492/1098. The fall of Ma’arrat al-Nu’man to the Crusaders, and the dreadful massacre of the city's population, shocked everyone; the episode recounted in detail in Muslim historical literature. In 529/1135 the Seljuq Atabeg, ‘Imad al-Din Zangi, reconquered Ma‘arrat al-Nu‘man and it reverted back to the Muslims. After Salah al-Din’s successful expeditions throughout western Syria in 584/1188, the town lost some of its strategic significance and was relieved of its wartime pressure, allowing for its architectural and infrastructural development. During the first half of the 7th/13th century, rivalling Ayyubid principalities of Damascus and Hama contested the town’s possession. It was finally granted by the Mamluks as an *iqtâ‘* to the Prince of Hama.  
Two main monuments from the constructive Ayyubid period are the renovated Great Mosque and the new Madrasat Abu al-Fawaris, both easily discernable in the  
town’s main square. The Umayyads constructed the Great Mosque in the 2nd/8th century, the Byzantines destroyed it in 358/969 and the Seljuqs then restored it in the first half of the 6th/12th century. The mosque was damaged and repaired by Nur al-Din after the earthquakes of 552/1157 and 565/1170; the mosque and the minaret were given a last major restoration in 595/1199 and epigraphically signed by the architect Qahir al-Sarmani. The elegant, square minaret is clearly inspired by the monumental minaret of the Umayyad Mosque in Aleppo.  
The Ma’arrat al-Nu’man Madrasa, now known locally as Jami’ Nur al-Din, was built by the same architect as the mosque and in the same year, 595/1199. It belonged to the *Shafi’i* rite and first named Madrasat Abu al-Fawaris. It offers a typical *madrasa* plan ubiquitously adapted in Syria, a *muqarnas* entrance that leads to a central courtyard surrounded by an *iwan* to the west, a prayer-hall with a *mihrab* to the south and the founder’s tomb-chamber on the north-east corner. As for the castle, it lies today in a bad condition on a hill to the north-west of the town. Built on a circular plan and initially defended by a ditch, the castle suffered from a recent occupation that led to the dismantling and re-use of its construction stones, except for the outer wall, which is partly preserved and is constructed from mixed courses of small blocks and of large smooth ashlars.

en.name: Magnetism I - IV (Photogravure), 2012
description: This limited edition of four etchings by Ahmad Mater was published by EOA Projects in 2012. Using iron filings scattered around two magnets (with only one visible), this installation entitled '*Magnetism*' evokes the attraction pilgrims feel towards the Ka‘ba. Ahmed Mater is a doctor and an artist who lives and works in Saudi Arabia. He is widely considered as one of the most important artists in Saudi Arabia and is notable for his particular interest in the development of Mecca.
holder: Khalili Family Trust – Hajj and the Arts of Pilgrimage Collection
keywords: Hajj; Hijaz; Holy place; Ka'ba; Medina; Mosque; paper; Pilgrimage; Prayer; Prophet Muhammad; Religion; Mecca

ar.name: زبدية ذات تصميم لشخص واقف وأربعة طيور
description: هذه القطعة هي زبدية من الطراز النيسابوري على قاعدة حلقية لها غطاء ببطانة خارجية مزينة بعصابة من المثلثات الداكنة ويوجد تحتها خطوط أفقية متساوية المسافات في نفس التزجيج للأسفل تجاه القاعدة. وأيضا في الخارج يوجد مناطق غير منتظمة من تزجيج بلون أحمر فاتح وأصفر. وداخل الإطار يوجد أربعة خطوط داكنة تحيط بثلاثة عصابات تزجيج صفراء ، حمراء وبيضاء. وبقية الجزء الداخلي له خلفية صفراء فاتحة. والشخص الذكر في الوسط  محاط بإطار ثخين من التزجيج الداكن وله رأس ، أنف ، شارب   وفم ويرتدي ملابس لها نطاق تمتد حتى الكاحل ذات بطانة خارجية سوداء. وفوق الخصر الملابس حمراء وذات تصاميم صفراء بشكل X . والمئزر مزين بمربعات نموذجية بأطر سوداء وعصابة أفقية زرقاء عبر الأسفل وهو يرتدي أيضا أحذية مدببة داكنة. والشخص محاط بالعديد من التصاميم ذات الطراز الخاص والأشكال الهندسية والنباتية ونقوش بالخط الكوفي وأربعة طيور طويلة العنق ذات أعراف ربما طواويس .ويوجد بشكل غير منتظم حول المجال المتوسط وحواف الزبدية بقع مرسومة بشكل مقصود من التزجيج الفيروزي. وخارج وأسفل الزبدية مغطى بتزجيج بلون أصفر مائل للبرتقالي وهي غير مزينة وتستند الزبدية على قاعدة منخفضة والقعر مجوف بشكل طفيف ومغطى بنفس التزجيج الأصفر- البرتقالي وهناك الكثير من نقاط الكسر الصغيرة خاصة حول الإطار وعلى كامل الجزء الخارجي من الزبدية و يوجد شقوق رفيعة في كل القطعة وهناك العديد من الكسور المرممة والكسور الصغيرة حول القدم / القاعدة.

en.name: Bowl with Design of Standing Figure and Four Birds
description:
A Nishapur-style bowl on a ring base has an exterior lip decorated with a band of dark triangles; below are horizontal, equidistant lines in the same glaze down toward the base. Also on the exterior are irregular areas of light red and yellow glaze. The interior of the rim has four horizontal dark lines outlining three bands of yellow, red, and white glaze. The rest of the interior has a bright yellow background. The central, male figure is thickly outlined in dark glaze and has a squared head, simplified eyes, nose, moustache, and mouth, and wears an ankle-length, belted garment with a black overlay. Above the waist the garment is red with yellow X designs. The skirt is decorated with patterned squares in dark outlines and a horizontal, blue band across the bottom; he also wears dark, pointed shoes. The figure is surrounded by numerous stylized, geometrical and vegetal designs, pseudo-*Kufic* inscriptions, and four long-necked birds with crests, possibly peacocks. Irregularly around the central field and edges of the bowl are intentional spots of turquoise glaze. The exterior and bottom of the bowl are covered in buff glaze and are undecorated. The bowl rests on a low foot, bottom slightly concave, covered in the same buff glaze.  
There is much chipping and cracking in the glaze, especially around the rim and over the entire exterior of the bowl; hairline cracks throughout. There are numerous, restored breaks, and chipping around the foot.
dates: Hegira Late 2nd to late 4th / AD 10th century

ar.name: مبخرة
description: هذه المبخرة هي مثال آخر على مجموعة من المباخر المشابهة جدا. وضمن المجموعة يمكن تحديد نظامين تزينيين رئيسيين. وهذه المبخرة هي مثال عن أحد هذين النظامين والذي يرتبط بشكل أربعة شطور من سعيفات النخل المرتبة بشكل رصيعة دائرية. ويمكن مقارنتها (من بين قطع أخرى) بمبخرتين في متحف هيرات الوطني (HNM 01.15.86, HNM 01.30.86a) واحدة في متحف ليندن وواحدة في متحف المتروبوليتان للفن (MET 1975.314).القطعة بشكل عامود مصنوع بالخراطة  ذو قاعدة / قدم مفلطحة. ويبدو من الممكن أن هذه القطعة كان يراد بها ان توضع فوق زبدية تحتوي المبخرة حيث أن القاعدة مفتوحة كليا. وجسم القطعة يمكن أن يقسم إلى ثلاثة مقاطع مختلفة .المقطع الأخفض هو مصمت ذو تزيين محفور الذي ينتهي تماما أعلى القاعدة /القدم ويتألف الجزء المتوسط من تشغيل مخرم. وفي الوسط حول أكبر قطر هناك رصائع دائرية ذات أربع سعيفات نخل موضوعة حول دائرة مركزية. وهذه مؤطرة بشرائط ملفوفة على بعضها. وفي الطرف السفلي من الرصائع يتقاطع التصميم بواسطة شريط أفقي الذي يجمع الشكل المخرم والمقاطع المصمتة ، بينما الجزء العلوي من التصميم مشطب بشكل دقيق. والجزء الأعلى هو مصمت ثانية ويظهر نقشا الذي يبدو أنه من نوع خاص. وربما يعرب عن أمنيات طيبة لمالك القطعة. ويوجد في النقش ثقوب صغيرة بفواصل منتظمة وهذه ثقبت لاحقا حيث تمر عبر النقش مما يجعله غير مقروء في هذه المناطق. وتماما حول فوهة المبخرة يوجد شريط من اللؤلؤ.إن التحليل الفني حول القطعة واعتبارها كمبخرة مقبول بشكل واسع حيث أن الشغل المخرم يجعلها غير مناسبة لأن تكون زهرية ولكن يمكن أن تكون قد استخدمت كمصباح خاصة باعتبار الثقوب الموجودة في النقش التي يمكن أن تستخدم لتعليقها.
keywords: مشغولة معدنية ، مبخرة ، عمل مخرم ، مصباح

en.name: Incense Burner
description:
This incense burner is another example of a group of very similar burners. Within the group, two major decorative schemes can be determined. This burner is an example of one such schemes, which is associated with a motif of four split palmettes arranged in a circular medallion. It can be (among others) compared to two burners in the Herat National Museum (HNM 01.15.86, HNM 01.30.86a), one in the Linden-Museum and one in Metropolitan Museum of Art (MET 1975.314).  
The artefact is baluster-shaped with a splayed foot. It seems possible that this object was meant to be placed on top of a bowl holding the incense because the base is entirely open. The body of the object can be divided in three different sections. The lowest part is solid with an engraved decoration that ends just above the foot. The middle part consists of openwork. Centrally, around the largest diameter are circular medallions with the four palmettes placed around a central circle. These are framed by intertwining ribbons. At the lower end of the medallions, the design is interrupted by a horizontal ribbon which combines open-worked and solid sections, while the upper part of the design is carefully finished. The uppermost part is solid again, showing an inscription, which seems to be in a special style. It probably states good wishes for the owner. Through the inscription little holes are found in steady intervals. These were punched through later, as they go through the inscription making it unreadable in those areas. Right around the mouth of the burner is a pearl-ribbon.  
The interpretation as an incense burner is widely accepted as the openwork makes it unsuitable for use as a vase. It could have been used, however, as a lamp, especially considering the holes through the inscription to hang it up.
holder: University Museum of Islamic Art | The Bumiller Collection
keywords: Metalwork; incenseburner; open work; lamp
materials: Bronze; cast, engraved and probably perforated
partner: University Museum of Islamic Art | The Bumiller Collection

de.name: Schaezler-Palais (ehem. Palais Liebert)
description:
Die kürzere, zur Maximilianstraße weisende Fassade bildet, deren städtebaulicher Bedeutung als Magistrale gemäß, die Schauseite des Palais. Der dreigeschossige Bau ist hier durch einen dreiachsigen Mittelrisalit akzentuiert, der mit dem breiten Torbogen, dem Zeremonialbalkon am Piano nobile und dem abschließenden Dreieckgiebel mit dem Wappen des Bauherrn mehrere nobilitierende Bauelemente vereinigt und dadurch eine dezente Pracht nach Art des französischen Klassizismus entfaltet. Dem gegenüber ist der lange, Appartementfluchten und den rückwärtigen Festssalbau vereinigende 32achsige Flügel entlang der Katharinengasse von einer gewissen Monotonie geprägt.  
Das Prunkstück des Gebäudes ist der 23 x 11 Meter große, zwei Stockwerke einnehmende und aufgrund der freistehenden Lage zwischen Gasse und Garten beidseitig befensterte Festsaal, dessen üppige Dekoration in Rokokoformen, dem sogenannten Augsburger Geschmack, gehalten ist. Der Gesamtentwurf stammt wohl von Gregorio Guglielmi, der 1767 auch das Deckenfresko schuf. Die Stuckaturen der Brüder Feichtmayr gehören zu den herausragendsten Elementen der Dekoration. Die Wände sind mit ornamental gerahmten Feldern dekoriert, in die Spiegel oder Gemälde wie z. B. die einheimische und exotische Flora und Fauna zeigenden Supraporten eingelassen wurden. Meisterhaft modelliert sind vor allem die sich aus architektonischen Gebundenheiten befreienden Gesimse der oberen Fensterreihe, die in freiem ornamentalen Spiel einen fließenden Übergang zur flachen Decke und dem daran applizierten Freskenrahmen schaffen – alles in allem ein meisterhaftes Rokoko-Interieur von höfischem Anspruch.

Das für einen reichen Bankier erbaute Schaezlerpalais ist der bedeutendste historische Profanbau der Stadt Augsburg. An zentraler Stelle an deren Hauptstraße gelegen prägt sich die verhalten repräsentative Noblesse der Hauptfassade tief ins Stadtbild ein. Der für ein Privatpalais ungewöhnlich prunkvolle Festsaal im Inneren ist geprägt von einer üppigen Dekoration, die ein hervorragendes Beispiel der lokalen Ausprägung des Rokoko, des so genannten Augsburger Geschmacks ist.
artist: Freiherr Benedikt Adam Liebert von Liebenhofen (1731-1810)
history: Der Bankier und Silberhändler Benedikt Adam Liebert, dessen Finanz- und Handelsbeziehungen weit in internationale Märkte reichten, ließ von 1765-70 das Palais in bester Lage an der Hauptstraße der Stadt erbauen. Der Auftrag erging in Folge seiner Nobilitierung zum Reichsritter (1763), die nach einem dem neuen gesellschaftlichen Stand entsprechenden repräsentativen Wohnhaus verlangte. Von den weitreichenden Beziehungen des Auftraggebers zeugen die Baupläne des damaligen Münchner Hofbaumeisters Karl Albert von Lespilliez, gemäß denen der lokale Baumeister Johann Gottfried Stumpe das Palais errichtete, sowie das Engagement des römischen Wandermalers Gregorio Guglielmi, der auch für den Wiener Kaiserhof tätig war.
keywords: Stadtpalais; Festsaal; Profanbau; Augsburger Geschmack; Treppenhaus; Zeremonialbalkon; Allegorie; Allegorie der vier Erdteile

en.name: Liebert Palace
description: The shorter facade oriented towards the Maximiliansstrasse is, according to the role of the street in the cityscape, the most prominent and most visible side of the palace. There, the three-story building is structured with a small central projection which unites several stately elements, such as a broad archway, a balcony in the *piano nobile* and a gable with the coat-of-arms of von Liebenhofen. The building evokes a discreet splendour following the example of French Classicism. On the contrary, the long facade facing the Katharinengasse seems quite monotonous. The large ballroom (23 x 11 m) ranging over two storeys is the showpiece of the building. The rich decoration, executed entirely in the local “Augsburgian taste” Rococo style, was probably designed by Gregorio Guglielmi, who also painted the ceiling fresco. The walls are adorned with ornamentally framed panels (wood carving by Placidius Verhelst) partially filled with mirrors or paintings, as are the over-doors, which illustrate local and exotic flora and fauna. The stuccowork by the brothers Franz-Xaver and Simpert Feichtmayr is maybe the most superb element of the decoration. Especially the cornices of the upper windows, which freed from all architectural constraints, are an outstanding masterpiece. Their ornamental richness establishes a floating connection with the frame of the fresco. All in all, a masterly Rococo interior of courtly ambition.

The Schaezlerpalais, built for a rich banker, is the most important secular building in the city of Augsburg. Situated prominently in the centre of the city’s main street, its noble splendour coins the cityscape. The impressively lush interior decoration is an outstanding example of the local Rococo style, the so-called *Augsburger Geschmack* (Augsburgian taste). The ballroom in particular is especially large and ostentatious, even for a private palace.
artist: Baron Benedict Adam Liebert von Liebenhofen (1731–1810)

Palace architecture: Karl Albert von Lespilliez (1723–1796); execution: Johann Gottfried Stumpe (1708–1777); ballroom, design and fresco: Gregorio Guglielmi (1714–1773); stucco: Franz-Xaver Feichtmayr (1735–1803), Simpert Feichtmayr (1732–1806); wood carving: Placidus Verhelst (1727–1778)
history: The Augsburgian banker and silver-trader Benedict Adam Liebert von Liebenhofen (1730–1810) whose business connections were wide-reaching in international markets, commissioned the construction of the palace (1765–70 executed by local builder, Johann Gottfried Stumpe) in a prime location on the city’s main street. The occasion for the project was the ennoblement of Liebert to the rank of a Reichsritter (knight), which required an adequate, new and representative residence. For the design of his palace Liebert engaged internationally-renowned artists, as for instance, the courtly master-builder Karl Albert von Lespillez from Munich and the Roman mural painter Gregorio Guglielmi who, as a travelling artist, also worked for the imperial court in Vienna.
keywords: City palace; secular architecture; “Augsburger taste”; allegory of the four continents; ceremonial balcony; stairwell; ballroom
partner: University of Munich, Institute of Art History

en.name: Dar ‘Aziza Bint al-Bay
description:
Dar ‘Aziza was part of the Djenina, a large complex of buildings that comprised Dar al-Soltane, or Palace of the Deys, which was used as the residence of the kings of Algiers. The last of these, Salim Tumi, was assassinated there by order of Aroudj Barbarossa, who replaced him. The Ottomans lived in it until 1817. The oldest description of the Djenina Palace dates back to about 956/1550. Its entrance was located not far from Bad al-Oued, and included a small garden, *djenina* in Arabic, which gave its name to the collection of buildings that constituted the palace. Over nearly three centuries it was the centre of the political, military, and administrative life of the Algiers Regency: royal residence, seat of the assemblies of *diwan*, or council, tribunal, the place to receive diplomats and envoys, and for selling slaves. It was also where Martin de Vargas, defender of the Spanish Fortress of Peñon, died after being captured.  
  
Dar ‘Aziza is the only surviving part of this complex, which was destroyed by the French in their redevelopment of the Lower Casbah. Its name comes from the tradition according to which a dey gave it to his daughter, ‘Aziza bent Dey, who was to marry the bey of Constantine. After the French conquest the palace was the site of the Archbishopric. It was classified a historic monument in 1887.  
  
The current entrance, designed in the modern era, does not conform to the traditional *sqifa* (entryway). It opens onto the *wast al-dar*, paved with decorated white marble, with a square white marble basin in the centre. The patio has galleries bordered by four pointed horseshoe arches resting on marble columns with twisted barrels and Tuscan-style capitals. These are decorated with acanthus leaves and garlands of flowers. The carved crescent, signature of a Muslim order, is affixed to these columns imported from Italy.  
  
On three sides of the gallery you can view classical or *byout* rooms, which have the traditional recess, or *qbou*, and arches at both ends indicating locations of the sleeping alcoves. The fourth wall of the gallery, facing the entrance, is reserved for service areas, hammam (bathhouses), kitchen, laundry and lodging for servants. The first storey repeats the layout of the rooms on the ground floor. Of particular interest are the magnificent domes ornamented with coloured mosaic tiles on the ceilings of the four corners of the gallery.  
  
On one side is the salon of honour. It contains two parts: an antechamber that opens onto the gallery with four arches richly decorated with garlands, followed by the salon itself – a large room with an imposing recess that is itself a square room topped by a dome. Everything is abundantly decorated by fine plaster carvings in an arch motif. This is where the host would stand. The beautiful polychrome wood ceilings in a local style are ornamented by circles inside squares, and by profusely repeated star-shaped, geometric or floral motifs.  
Decorative forms here find their full expression. Exits and interior doors display the same designs: semicircular arch frames of white marble sculpted with a variety of floral motifs, and crescents at the height of the spandrels, or upper corners.  
  
These wooden doors exhibit remarkable carpentry: rectangular panels that interlock vertically and horizontally, embellished at their centres by carved designs in relief.  
  
The large doors that provide access to the main rooms are two-panelled and rectangular, in which small doors in the shape of horseshoe arches are cut and decorated on their edges. Above, three panels of openwork plaster with coloured glass transmit light from the patio. The windows, barred in bronze (including those facing the interior) are double-framed, as in Dar Mustafa Pasha: the first is white marble richly sculpted with floral motifs resembling those of the doors; the second is decorated with bands of coloured ceramic.  
  
Dar ‘Aziza has no balcony. It is believed that there was a second floor but that it was destroyed, probably as a result of an earthquake.  
  
The originality of Dar ‘Aziza, apart from the refinement of its decoration, is due mainly to its imposing reception room preceded by the antechamber, which lends it a palatial character. It resembles the Palace of Ziri in Achir, attesting to the continuity and permanence of architectural features specific to the region, which were likely inherited from the East.

fr.name: Dar ‘Aziza
description:
Dar ‘Aziza faisait partie de la Djenina, grand ensemble de bâtiments qui constituait Dar al-Soltane ou palais des Deys qui servait de résidence aux rois d’Alger. Le dernier d’entre eux, Salim Toumi, y fut assassiné sur ordre d’Aroudj, un des frères Barberousse, qui prit sa place. Les Ottomans y résidèrent aussi jusqu’en 1817. La plus ancienne description du palais de la Djenina remonte aux alentours de 956/1550. Son entrée se trouvait non loin de Bab al-Oued et abritait un petit jardin, *djenina* en arabe, qui a donné son nom à l’ensemble des édifices qui composaient le palais. Ce dernier fut, pendant près de trois siècles, le théâtre de la vie politique, militaire et administrative de la Régence d’Alger : résidence royale, siège des assemblées du Diwan ou Conseil, tribunal, lieu de réception des diplomates et consuls, des ventes d’esclaves… C’est aussi là que mourut, après sa capture, le défenseur de la forteresse espagnole du Peñon, Martin de Vargas.  
Dar ‘Aziza est la seule partie subsistante de cet ensemble qui fut détruit par les Français à l’occasion de leurs travaux de réaménagement de la Basse Casbah. Son nom vient de la tradition selon laquelle un dey en aurait fait don à sa fille, ‘Aziza bent Dey, qui devait épouser le bey de Constantine. Après la conquête française, ce palais fut le siège de l’Archevêché et classé monument historique en 1887.  
L’entrée actuelle, aménagée à l’époque moderne, ne présente pas la traditionnelle *sqifa*. Elle donne sur le *wast al-dar*, pavé de carreaux de marbre blanc et orné, en son centre, d’un bassin carré avec jet d’eau, en marbre blanc lui aussi. Le patio présente des galeries bordées de quatre arcs brisés outrepassés, reposant sur des colonnes en marbre à fûts torsadés et à chapiteaux de style toscan, inspiré du style antique à la feuille d’acanthe, entourée de guirlandes de fleurs à peine ébauchées. Le croissant sculpté, signature d’une commande musulmane, est apposé sur ces colonnes importées d’Italie.  
  
Sur trois des côtés de la galerie, on retrouve les pièces classiques ou *byout*, présentant, face à la porte, le traditionnel renfoncement ou *qbou* ainsi que, aux deux extrémités, des arcs indiquant les emplacements des alcôves-lits. Le quatrième côté de la galerie, face à l’entrée, est réservé aux espaces de service, hammam, cuisine, buanderie et logement des domestiques.  
Le premier étage reproduit la disposition des pièces du rez-de-chaussée. On notera particulièrement, au niveau des plafonds des quatre angles de la galerie, les magnifiques coupoles ornées de mosaïques colorées.  
Sur un des côtés se trouve le salon d’honneur. Il présente deux parties : une avantsalle, ou anti-salle, ouverte sur la galerie par quatre arcs richement décorés de festons, puis le salon lui-même, grande pièce avec un *qbou* important qui constitue une véritable pièce carrée surmontée d’une coupole. Le tout est abondamment orné de fines ciselures de stucs reproduisant le motif de l’arc. C’est en ce lieu que se tient l’hôte. Les très beaux plafonds de bois polychromes de pure tradition locale sont ornés de cercles circonscrits dans des carrés, motifs stellaires, géométriques ou floraux répétés à profusion.  
Les formes décoratives trouvent ici leur pleine expression. Les issues et portes intérieures présentent les mêmes décors : encadrements en arc de plein cintre de marbre blanc sculpté de motifs floraux, à chaque fois différents, et de croissants au niveau des écoinçons ou angles supérieurs.  
  
Le bois de ces portes présente un remarquable travail d’ébénisterie : des panneaux rectangulaires, imbriqués verticalement et horizontalement, et rehaussés en leur centre de motifs en relief.  
Les grandes portes donnant accès aux pièces principales sont à double vantail, rectangulaire, où sont découpées de petites portes en forme d’arcs outrepassés et festonnés sur leur rebord. Au-dessus, trois claustras de plâtre ajouré et orné de verre coloré diffusent la lumière du patio.  
Les fenêtres barreaudées de bronze, y compris celles donnant sur l’intérieur, présentent un double encadrement, comme à Dar Mustapha Pacha : le premier, de marbre blanc richement sculpté de motifs floraux rappelant celui des portes, le second, de bandeaux de céramique colorée.  
Dar ‘Aziza n’a pas de terrasse. On peut supposer qu’il existait un deuxième étage mais qu’il a été détruit, probablement à la suite d’un tremblement de terre.  
L’originalité de Dar ‘Aziza, outre le raffinement de sa décoration, tient essentiellement à son imposant salon de réception précédé de son anti-salle qui lui donne son cachet de résidence palatiale. Elle s’apparente en cela au palais de Ziri à Achir, attestant la continuité et la permanence de traits architecturaux propres à la région, eux-mêmes hérités, pour certains, de l’Orient.

en.name: Slope and Ditch with Bulwark and Ravelin
description: Besides its military efficiency, the large earthworks and buildings were important to social cohesion. The bulk of the architecture was a rhetorical statement that the country could face any menace from foreign armies. The fortification was, therefore built both symbolically and practically to discourage further enemy actions.
